4 And Aaron and his sons you shall bring near to the door of the Tent of Meeting, and you shall wash them with water.

5 And you shall take the garments and put on Aaron the tunic and the robe of the ephod and the ephod and the breastplate, and you shall fasten the ephod on him with its woven band.

6 And you shall put the turban on his head, and you shall put the holy crown on the turban.

7 And you shall take the anointing oil and pour it on his head and anoint him.

8 And his sons you shall bring near, and you shall put tunics on them.

9 And you shall gird them with a sash — Aaron and his sons — and bind caps on them, and the priesthood shall be theirs by a statute forever, and you shall fill the hand of Aaron and the hand of his sons.

10 And you shall bring the bull before the Tent of Meeting, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the head of the bull.

11 And you shall slaughter the bull before Yahweh, at the door of the Tent of Meeting.

12 And you shall take some of the blood of the bull and put it on the horns of the altar with your finger, and all the blood you shall pour out at the base of the altar.

13 And you shall take all the fat that covers the innards, and the lobe on the liver, and the two kidneys and the fat that is on them, and you shall burn them on the altar.

14 And the flesh of the bull and its skin and its dung you shall burn with fire outside the camp; it is a sin offering.

15 And the one ram you shall take, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the head of the ram.

16 And you shall slaughter the ram and take its blood and throw it on the altar all around.

17 And the ram you shall cut into its pieces, and you shall wash its innards and its legs and put them on its pieces and on its head.

18 And you shall burn the whole ram on the altar; it is a burnt offering to Yahweh, a pleasing aroma, a fire offering to Yahweh.

19 And you shall take the second ram, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the head of the ram.

20 And you shall slaughter the ram and take some of its blood and put it on the lobe of Aaron's right ear and on the lobe of his sons' right ear, and on the thumb of their right hand and on the big toe of their right foot, and you shall throw the blood on the altar all around.

21 And you shall take some of the blood that is on the altar and some of the anointing oil and sprinkle it on Aaron and on his garments and on his sons and on his sons' garments with him, and he shall be holy, and his garments, and his sons and his sons' garments with him.

22 And you shall take from the ram the fat and the fat tail and the fat that covers the innards and the lobe of the liver and the two kidneys and the fat that is on them and the right thigh — for it is a ram of consecration —

23 and one loaf of bread and one cake of oiled bread and one wafer, from the basket of unleavened bread that is before Yahweh.

24 And you shall put the whole on Aaron's palms and on his sons' palms, and you shall wave them as a wave offering before Yahweh.

25 And you shall take them from their hand and burn them on the altar on the burnt offering, for a pleasing aroma before Yahweh; it is a fire offering to Yahweh.

26 And you shall take the breast of Aaron's ram of consecration and wave it as a wave offering before Yahweh, and it shall be your portion.

27 And you shall make holy the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution, which was waved and which was lifted up, from the ram of consecration, from what is for Aaron and from what is for his sons.

28 And it shall be for Aaron and for his sons as a due forever from the children of Israel, for it is a contribution, and a contribution it shall be from the children of Israel from their peace offerings — their contribution to Yahweh.

29 And the holy garments that are Aaron's shall be for his sons after him, to be anointed in them and to fill their hand in them.

30 Seven days shall the priest from his sons in his place wear them, who comes into the Tent of Meeting to serve in the holy place.

31 And the ram of consecration you shall take, and you shall boil its flesh in a holy place.

32 And Aaron and his sons shall eat the flesh of the ram and the bread that is in the basket, at the door of the Tent of Meeting.

33 And they shall eat those things with which atonement was made, to fill their hand, to make them holy; and a stranger shall not eat, for they are holy.

34 And if any of the flesh of the consecration or of the bread remains until the morning, you shall burn what remains with fire; it shall not be eaten, for it is holy.

35 And you shall do for Aaron and for his sons so, according to all that I have commanded you; seven days you shall fill their hand.

36 And a bull of sin offering you shall offer daily for the atonement, and you shall cleanse the altar when you make atonement for it, and you shall anoint it to make it holy.

37 Seven days you shall make atonement for the altar and make it holy, and the altar shall be most holy; whatever touches the altar shall be holy.

38 And this is what you shall offer on the altar: two lambs a year old, daily, continually.

39 The one lamb you shall offer in the morning, and the second lamb you shall offer at twilight.

40 And a tenth of fine flour mixed with a quarter of a hin of beaten oil, and a drink offering of a quarter of a hin of wine, for the one lamb.

41 And the second lamb you shall offer at twilight; according to the grain offering of the morning and according to its drink offering you shall do for it, for a pleasing aroma, a fire offering to Yahweh.

42 A continual burnt offering throughout your generations, at the door of the Tent of Meeting before Yahweh, where I will meet with you there, to speak to you there.

43 And I will meet there with the children of Israel, and it shall be made holy by my glory.

44 And I shall make holy the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and Aaron and his sons I shall make holy, to serve as priest for me.

45 And I shall dwell among the children of Israel, and I shall be God for them.

46 And they shall know that I am Yahweh their God, who brought them out of the land of Egypt, so that I might dwell among them; I am Yahweh their God.

Exodus 30

1 And you shall make an altar for burning incense; of acacia wood you shall make it.

2 A cubit its length and a cubit its width — it shall be square — and two cubits its height; its horns shall be of one piece with it.

3 And you shall cover it with pure gold — its top and its walls all around and its horns — and you shall make for it a gold border all around.

4 And two gold rings you shall make for it, under its border, on its two ribs; on its two sides you shall make them, and it shall be for holders for poles, to carry it with them.

5 And you shall make the poles of acacia wood and cover them with gold.

6 And you shall put it before the veil that is over the ark of the testimony, before the cover that is over the testimony, where I will meet with you there.

7 And Aaron shall burn on it incense of spices; morning by morning, when he tends the lamps, he shall burn it.

8 And when Aaron lights the lamps at twilight he shall burn it — a continual incense before Yahweh throughout your generations.

9 You shall not offer on it strange incense, or a burnt offering or a grain offering, and you shall not pour a drink offering on it.

10 And Aaron shall make atonement on its horns once in the year; from the blood of the sin offering of atonement, once in the year, he shall make atonement for it throughout your generations; it is most holy to Yahweh.

11 And Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

12 When you take the sum of the children of Israel according to their counted ones, each man shall give a ransom for his life to Yahweh when you count them, and there shall be no plague among them when you count them.

13 This they shall give — everyone who passes over to the counted ones — half a shekel by the shekel of the sanctuary (twenty gerahs the shekel); half a shekel, a contribution to Yahweh.

14 Everyone who passes over to the counted ones, from twenty years old and upward, shall give Yahweh's contribution.

15 The rich shall not give more and the poor shall not give less than half a shekel, in giving Yahweh's contribution, to make atonement for your lives.

16 And you shall take the atonement silver from the children of Israel and give it for the service of the Tent of Meeting, and it shall be for the children of Israel a memorial before Yahweh, to make atonement for your lives.

17 And Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

18 And you shall make a basin of bronze and its stand of bronze, for washing, and you shall put it between the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and you shall put water there.

19 And Aaron and his sons shall wash from it their hands and their feet.

20 When they go in to the Tent of Meeting they shall wash with water and they shall not die; or when they draw near to the altar to serve, to burn a fire offering to Yahweh.

21 And they shall wash their hands and their feet and they shall not die, and it shall be for them a statute forever — for him and for his seed throughout their generations.

22 And Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

23 And you, take for yourself the chief spices: flowing myrrh, five hundred, and spice cinnamon, half of it, two hundred and fifty, and spice cane, two hundred and fifty,

24 and cassia, five hundred, by the shekel of the sanctuary, and olive oil, a hin.

25 And you shall make it a holy anointing oil, a blended perfume, the work of a perfumer; it shall be a holy anointing oil.

26 And you shall anoint with it the Tent of Meeting and the ark of the testimony,

27 and the table and all its vessels, and the lampstand and its vessels, and the altar of incense,

28 and the altar of burnt offering and all its vessels, and the basin and its stand.

29 And you shall make them holy, and they shall be most holy; whatever touches them shall be holy.

30 And Aaron and his sons you shall anoint, and you shall make them holy, to serve as priest for me.

31 And to the children of Israel you shall speak, saying: A holy anointing oil shall this be for me throughout your generations.

32 On the flesh of a man it shall not be poured, and by its measure you shall not make any like it; it is holy; holy it shall be to you.

33 Any man who blends any like it, or who puts any of it on a stranger, shall be cut off from his peoples.

34 And Yahweh said to Moses: Take for yourself spices — stacte and onycha and galbanum — spices, and pure frankincense; part for part it shall be.

35 And you shall make it incense, a perfume, the work of a perfumer, salted, pure, holy.

36 And you shall beat some of it fine, and you shall put some of it before the testimony in the Tent of Meeting, where I will meet with you there; most holy it shall be to you.

37 And the incense that you make — by its measure you shall not make for yourselves; holy it shall be to you, for Yahweh.

38 Any man who makes any like it, to smell it, shall be cut off from his peoples.

Exodus 31

1 And Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

2 See, I have called by name Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah,

3 and I have filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom and in understanding and in knowledge and in all workmanship,

4 to devise designs, to work in gold and in silver and in bronze,

5 and in cutting stone for setting and in carving wood, to work in all workmanship.

6 And I, behold, I have appointed with him Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, and in the heart of every wise-hearted one I have put wisdom, and they shall make all that I have commanded you:

7 the Tent of Meeting, and the ark for the testimony, and the cover that is on it, and all the vessels of the Tent,

8 and the table and its vessels, and the pure lampstand and all its vessels, and the altar of incense,

9 and the altar of burnt offering and all its vessels, and the basin and its stand,

10 and the service garments, and the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons, to serve as priest,

11 and the anointing oil, and the incense of spices for the holy place; according to all that I have commanded you they shall do.

12 And Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

13 And you, speak to the children of Israel, saying: Surely my Sabbaths you shall keep, for it is a sign between me and you throughout your generations, to know that I am Yahweh who makes you holy.

14 And you shall keep the Sabbath, for it is holy to you; those who profane it shall surely be put to death, for everyone who does work on it — that person shall be cut off from among his peoples.

15 Six days work shall be done, and on the seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest, holy to Yahweh; everyone who does work on the Sabbath day shall surely be put to death.

16 And the children of Israel shall keep the Sabbath, to observe the Sabbath throughout their generations, a covenant forever.

17 Between me and the children of Israel it is a sign forever, for in six days Yahweh made the heavens and the earth, and on the seventh day he rested and was refreshed.

18 And he gave to Moses, when he had finished speaking with him on Mount Sinai, the two tablets of the testimony, tablets of stone, written with the finger of God.

Exodus 32

1 And the people saw that Moses was delayed in coming down from the mountain, and the people gathered against Aaron and said to him, "Come, make us gods who shall go before us; for this Moses, the man who brought us up out of the land of Egypt — we do not know what has become of him."

2 And Aaron said to them, "Take off the gold rings that are in the ears of your wives, your sons, and your daughters, and bring them to me."

3 And all the people took off the gold rings that were in their ears, and brought them to Aaron.

4 And he took them from their hand, and shaped it with a tool, and made it a cast calf. And they said, "These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt."

5 And Aaron saw, and built an altar before it, and Aaron called out and said, "Tomorrow is a feast to Yahweh."

6 And they rose early on the next day, and offered burnt offerings, and brought peace offerings. And the people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.

7 And Yahweh spoke to Moses, "Go, go down, for your people, whom you brought up out of the land of Egypt, have corrupted themselves.

8 They have quickly turned aside from the way that I commanded them. They have made for themselves a cast calf, and bowed down to it, and sacrificed to it, and said, 'These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt.'"

9 And Yahweh said to Moses, "I have seen this people, and see, it is a stiff-necked people.

10 And now, leave me alone, and my anger shall burn against them, and I shall consume them, and I will make you into a great nation."

11 And Moses pleaded before Yahweh his God, and said, "Why, Yahweh, should your anger burn against your people, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt with great power and with a mighty hand?

12 Why should the Egyptians say, 'With evil intent he brought them out, to kill them in the mountains and to consume them from the face of the earth'? Turn from the fierceness of your anger, and relent concerning the evil against your people.

13 Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, your slaves, to whom you swore by yourself and said to them, 'I will multiply your offspring as the stars of the heavens, and all this land that I have spoken of I will give to your offspring, and they shall inherit it forever.'"

14 And Yahweh relented concerning the evil that he had spoken of doing to his people.

15 And Moses turned and went down from the mountain, and the two tablets of the testimony were in his hand — tablets written on both their sides; on this side and on that side they were written.

16 And the tablets were the work of God, and the writing was the writing of God, engraved on the tablets.

17 And Joshua heard the sound of the people in its shouting, and said to Moses, "There is a sound of war in the camp."

18 And he said, "It is not the sound of a cry of might, and it is not the sound of a cry of weakness; it is the sound of singing that I hear."

19 And it happened, as he came near to the camp, that he saw the calf and the dancing. And Moses' anger burned, and he threw the tablets from his hands and broke them beneath the mountain.

20 And he took the calf that they had made, and burned it in the fire, and ground it until it was fine, and scattered it on the face of the waters, and made the children of Israel drink it.

21 And Moses said to Aaron, "What did this people do to you, that you have brought a great sin upon them?"

22 And Aaron said, "Let not my lord's anger burn. You know the people, that they are set on evil.

23 And they said to me, 'Make us gods who shall go before us; for this Moses, the man who brought us up out of the land of Egypt — we do not know what has become of him.'

24 And I said to them, 'Whoever has gold, take it off.' And they gave it to me, and I threw it into the fire, and this calf came out."

25 And Moses saw the people, that they were unrestrained — for Aaron had let them loose — to their shame among those who rise against them.

26 And Moses stood in the gate of the camp and said, "Whoever is for Yahweh — to me!" And all the sons of Levi gathered to him.

27 And he said to them, "Thus says Yahweh, the God of Israel: 'Put each man his sword on his thigh. Go through and return from gate to gate in the camp, and kill each man his brother, and each man his neighbour, and each man his close one.'"

28 And the sons of Levi did according to the word of Moses, and about three thousand men of the people fell that day.

29 And Moses said, "Consecrate yourselves today to Yahweh — for each man has been against his son and against his brother — so that he may give a blessing on you today."

30 And on the next day Moses said to the people, "You have sinned a great sin. And now I will go up to Yahweh; perhaps I can make atonement for your sin."

31 And Moses returned to Yahweh and said, "Oh, this people have sinned a great sin, and have made for themselves gods of gold.

32 And now, if you will forgive their sin — and if not, blot me out, please, from your book that you have written."

33 And Yahweh said to Moses, "Whoever has sinned against me, him I will blot out of my book.

34 And now go, lead the people to where I have spoken to you. See, my angel shall go before you. And on the day of my visiting, I will visit their sin upon them."

35 And Yahweh struck the people, because they made the calf, which Aaron made.

Exodus 33

1 And Yahweh spoke to Moses, "Go, go up from here, you and the people whom you brought up out of the land of Egypt, to the land that I swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, saying, 'To your offspring I will give it.'

2 And I will send an angel before you, and I will drive out the Canaanite, the Amorite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite —

3 to a land flowing with milk and honey. For I will not go up in your midst, for you are a stiff-necked people, lest I consume you on the way."

4 And the people heard this evil word, and they mourned, and no man put his ornaments on himself.

5 And Yahweh said to Moses, "Say to the children of Israel, 'You are a stiff-necked people. If I go up in your midst for one moment, I shall consume you. And now, take your ornaments off from you, and I shall know what I will do to you.'"

6 And the children of Israel stripped off their ornaments, from Mount Horeb onward.

7 And Moses would take the tent and pitch it for himself outside the camp, far from the camp, and he called it the Tent of Meeting. And everyone who sought Yahweh would go out to the Tent of Meeting, which was outside the camp.

8 And when Moses went out to the tent, all the people would rise and stand, each man at the opening of his tent, and watch after Moses until he had entered the tent.

9 And when Moses entered the tent, the pillar of cloud would come down and stand at the opening of the tent, and he would speak with Moses.

10 And all the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the opening of the tent, and all the people rose and bowed down, each man at the opening of his tent.

11 And Yahweh spoke to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his neighbour. And he returned to the camp, but his attendant Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, did not depart from inside the tent.

12 And Moses said to Yahweh, "See, you say to me, 'Bring up this people,' and you have not let me know whom you will send with me. And you have said, 'I know you by name, and you have also found favour in my eyes.'

13 And now, if I have found favour in your eyes, let me know your ways, please, and I shall know you, so that I may find favour in your eyes. And see that this nation is your people."

14 And he said, "My face shall go, and I will give you rest."

15 And he said to him, "If your face does not go, do not bring us up from here.

16 And by what, then, shall it be known that I have found favour in your eyes, I and your people? Is it not by your going with us, so that we are set apart, I and your people, from all the people who are on the face of the earth?"

17 And Yahweh said to Moses, "This word also that you have spoken I will do, for you have found favour in my eyes, and I know you by name."

18 And he said, "Show me your glory, please."

19 And he said, "I will make all my goodness pass before your face, and I will proclaim by the name Yahweh before you. And I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and I will show mercy to whom I will show mercy."

20 And he said, "You cannot see my face, for no man shall see me and live."

21 And Yahweh said, "See, there is a place with me, and you shall stand on the rock.

22 And when my glory passes by, I will put you in the cleft of the rock, and I will cover you with my palm until I have passed by.

23 And I will remove my palm, and you shall see my back, but my face shall not be seen."

Exodus 34

1 And Yahweh said to Moses, "Cut for yourself two tablets of stone like the first, and I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke.

2 And be ready by the morning, and go up in the morning to Mount Sinai, and stand there for me on the top of the mountain.

3 And no man shall go up with you, and no man shall be seen on all the mountain. Even the flock and the herd shall not graze in front of that mountain."

4 And he cut two tablets of stone like the first, and Moses rose early in the morning and went up to Mount Sinai, as Yahweh had commanded him, and took in his hand two tablets of stone.

5 And Yahweh came down in the cloud, and stood with him there, and proclaimed by the name Yahweh.

6 And Yahweh passed by before his face and proclaimed, "Yahweh, Yahweh, a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and great in kindness and truth,

7 keeping kindness for thousands, forgiving iniquity and transgression and sin, and he will by no means clear the guilty, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children and on the children's children, on the third and on the fourth generation."

8 And Moses hurried and bowed to the earth and bowed down.

9 And he said, "If I have found favour in your eyes, my Lord, let my Lord go, please, in our midst — for it is a stiff-necked people — and forgive our iniquity and our sin, and take us as your inheritance."

10 And he said, "See, I am cutting a covenant. Before all your people I will do wonders such as have not been created in all the earth or in any nation. And all the people in whose midst you are shall see the work of Yahweh, for it is a fearful thing that I am doing with you.

11 Keep for yourself what I command you today. See, I am driving out before you the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite.

12 Take care for yourself, lest you cut a covenant with the inhabitant of the land to which you are going, lest it become a snare in your midst.

13 For their altars you shall break down, and their pillars you shall smash, and their Asherah poles you shall cut down.

14 For you shall not bow down to another god, for Yahweh — Jealous is his name — is a jealous God.

15 Lest you cut a covenant with the inhabitant of the land, and they whore after their gods and sacrifice to their gods, and he calls to you and you eat of his sacrifice,

16 and you take from his daughters for your sons, and his daughters whore after their gods and make your sons whore after their gods.

17 You shall not make for yourself cast gods.

18 The feast of unleavened bread you shall keep. Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the appointed time of the month Abib, for in the month Abib you came out of Egypt.

19 Every firstborn of a womb is mine, and all your livestock that are male, the firstborn of ox and sheep.

20 And the firstborn of a donkey you shall redeem with a lamb, and if you do not redeem it, you shall break its neck. Every firstborn of your sons you shall redeem. And my face shall not be seen empty-handed.

21 Six days you shall work, and on the seventh day you shall rest; in ploughing and in harvest you shall rest.

22 And the feast of weeks you shall make for yourself, the firstfruits of the wheat harvest, and the feast of ingathering at the turn of the year.

23 Three times in the year every male of yours shall be seen before the face of the Lord Yahweh, the God of Israel.

24 For I will dispossess nations before you and enlarge your border, and no man shall covet your land when you go up to be seen before the face of Yahweh your God three times in the year.

25 You shall not slaughter the blood of my sacrifice with leavened bread, and the sacrifice of the feast of the Passover shall not remain overnight until the morning.

26 The first of the firstfruits of your ground you shall bring to the house of Yahweh your God. You shall not boil a kid in its mother's milk."

27 And Yahweh said to Moses, "Write for yourself these words, for according to these words I have cut a covenant with you and with Israel."

28 And he was there with Yahweh forty days and forty nights. He ate no bread and drank no water. And he wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the ten words.

29 And when Moses came down from Mount Sinai — and the two tablets of the testimony were in Moses' hand when he came down from the mountain — Moses did not know that the skin of his face shone, because he had spoken with him.

30 And Aaron and all the children of Israel saw Moses, and see, the skin of his face shone, and they were afraid to come near to him.

31 And Moses called to them, and Aaron and all the leaders in the congregation returned to him, and Moses spoke to them.

32 And afterwards all the children of Israel came near, and he commanded them all that Yahweh had spoken with him on Mount Sinai.

33 And Moses finished speaking with them, and put a veil on his face.

34 And when Moses came before Yahweh to speak with him, he would remove the veil until he came out. And he came out and spoke to the children of Israel what he was commanded.

35 And the children of Israel saw Moses' face, that the skin of Moses' face shone, and Moses put the veil back on his face until he came in to speak with him.

Exodus 35

1 And Moses gathered all the congregation of the children of Israel, and said to them, "These are the words that Yahweh has commanded, to do them.

2 Six days work shall be done, and on the seventh day there shall be for you a holy Sabbath of complete rest to Yahweh. Everyone who does work on it shall be put to death.

3 You shall not kindle a fire in any of your dwellings on the Sabbath day."

4 And Moses spoke to all the congregation of the children of Israel, saying, "This is the word that Yahweh commanded, saying,

5 'Take from yourselves a contribution to Yahweh. Everyone whose heart is willing shall bring it — Yahweh's contribution: gold, silver, and bronze,

6 and blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine linen, and goats' hair,

7 and rams' skins dyed red, and tachash hides, and acacia wood,

8 and oil for the light, and spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense,

9 and onyx stones, and stones for setting, for the ephod and for the breastplate.'

10 And every wise-hearted man among you shall come and make all that Yahweh has commanded:

11 the tabernacle, its tent and its covering, its clasps and its boards, its bars, its pillars, and its sockets;

12 the ark and its poles, the cover, and the veil of the screen;

13 the table and its poles and all its vessels, and the bread of the presence;

14 and the lampstand for the light and its vessels and its lamps, and the oil for the light;

15 and the altar of incense and its poles, and the anointing oil, and the fragrant incense, and the screen of the opening, for the opening of the tabernacle;

16 the altar of burnt offering and the bronze grating that belongs to it, its poles and all its vessels, the basin and its stand;

17 the hangings of the court, its pillars and its sockets, and the screen for the gate of the court;

18 the pegs of the tabernacle and the pegs of the court and their cords;

19 the service garments for serving in the holy place, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons, to serve as priests."

20 And all the congregation of the children of Israel went out from before Moses.

21 And they came — every man whose heart lifted him up, and everyone whose spirit made him willing — and brought Yahweh's contribution for the work of the Tent of Meeting, and for all its service, and for the holy garments.

22 And the men came, together with the women. Everyone whose heart was willing brought a brooch, and a ring, and a signet ring, and a pendant — every article of gold — and every man who waved a wave offering of gold to Yahweh.

23 And every man with whom was found blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine linen, and goats' hair, and rams' skins dyed red, and tachash hides, brought them.

24 Everyone who contributed a contribution of silver and bronze brought Yahweh's contribution, and everyone with whom was found acacia wood for any work of the service brought it.

25 And every wise-hearted woman spun with her hands, and brought the spun work: the blue, and the purple, the scarlet, and the fine linen.

26 And all the women whose heart lifted them up in wisdom spun the goats' hair.

27 And the leaders brought the onyx stones and the stones for setting, for the ephod and for the breastplate,

28 and the spice and the oil, for the light and for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense.

29 Every man and woman whose heart made them willing to bring for all the work that Yahweh had commanded to be done by the hand of Moses — the children of Israel brought a freewill offering to Yahweh.

30 And Moses said to the children of Israel, "See, Yahweh has called by name Bezalel, the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.

31 And he has filled him with the Spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding, in knowledge, and in all work,

32 and to devise designs, to work in gold, in silver, and in bronze,

33 and in cutting stone for setting, and in cutting wood, to work in all work of design.

34 And he has put in his heart to teach — he, and Oholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan.

35 He has filled them with wisdom of heart, to do all work of the craftsman, and the designer, and the embroiderer in the blue, and in the purple, in the scarlet, and in the fine linen, and the weaver — those who do all work, and those who devise designs."

Exodus 36

1 "And Bezalel and Oholiab shall work, and every wise-hearted man in whom Yahweh has put wisdom and understanding, to know how to do all the work of the service of the holy place, according to all that Yahweh has commanded."

2 And Moses called Bezalel and Oholiab, and every wise-hearted man in whose heart Yahweh had put wisdom — everyone whose heart lifted him up to come near to the work, to do it.

3 And they took from before Moses all the contribution that the children of Israel had brought for the work of the service of the holy place, to do it. And they still brought freewill offerings to him morning by morning.

4 And all the wise men who were doing all the work of the holy place came, each man from his work that they were doing,

5 and they said to Moses, "The people are bringing much more than enough for the service of the work that Yahweh commanded to do."

6 And Moses commanded, and they made a voice pass through the camp, saying, "Man and woman shall no longer make work for the contribution of the holy place." And the people were restrained from bringing.

7 And the material was enough for them for all the work, to do it, and there was surplus.

8 And all the wise-hearted among those doing the work made the tabernacle: ten curtains of fine twisted linen, and blue, and purple, and scarlet, with cherubim — the work of a designer he made them.

9 The length of the one curtain was twenty-eight cubits, and the width of the one curtain was four cubits; one measure for all the curtains.

10 And he joined the five curtains one to another, and the five curtains he joined one to another.

11 And he made loops of blue on the edge of the one curtain, at the end in the joined set. So he did on the edge of the outermost curtain in the second joined set.

12 Fifty loops he made in the one curtain, and fifty loops he made at the end of the curtain that was in the second joined set; the loops were opposite one to another.

13 And he made fifty clasps of gold, and joined the curtains one to another with the clasps, and the tabernacle became one.

14 And he made curtains of goats' hair for a tent over the tabernacle; eleven curtains he made them.

15 The length of the one curtain was thirty cubits, and four cubits the width of the one curtain; one measure for the eleven curtains.

16 And he joined the five curtains separately, and the six curtains separately.

17 And he made fifty loops on the edge of the outermost curtain in the joined set, and fifty loops he made on the edge of the curtain of the second joined set.

18 And he made fifty clasps of bronze, to join the tent, to be one.

19 And he made a covering for the tent of rams' skins dyed red, and a covering of tachash hides above.

20 And he made the boards for the tabernacle of acacia wood, standing upright.

21 Ten cubits was the length of the board, and a cubit and half a cubit the width of the one board.

22 Two tenons for the one board, joined one to another; so he did for all the boards of the tabernacle.

23 And he made the boards for the tabernacle: twenty boards for the south side, southward.

24 And forty sockets of silver he made under the twenty boards: two sockets under the one board for its two tenons, and two sockets under the one board for its two tenons.

25 And for the second side of the tabernacle, for the north side, he made twenty boards,

26 and their forty sockets of silver: two sockets under the one board, and two sockets under the one board.

27 And for the rear of the tabernacle, westward, he made six boards.

28 And two boards he made for the corners of the tabernacle in the rear.

29 And they were doubled beneath, and together they were complete to its top, to the one ring; so he did for both of them, for the two corners.

30 And there were eight boards, and their sockets of silver, sixteen sockets: two sockets, two sockets under the one board.

31 And he made bars of acacia wood: five for the boards of the one side of the tabernacle,

32 and five bars for the boards of the second side of the tabernacle, and five bars for the boards of the tabernacle for the rear, westward.

33 And he made the middle bar to pass through inside the boards, from end to end.

34 And he overlaid the boards with gold, and their rings he made of gold, as holders for the bars, and he overlaid the bars with gold.

35 And he made the veil of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twisted linen; the work of a designer he made it, with cherubim.

36 And he made for it four pillars of acacia, and overlaid them with gold — their hooks were gold — and he cast for them four sockets of silver.

37 And he made a screen for the opening of the tent, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer,

38 and its five pillars and their hooks. And he overlaid their tops and their bands with gold, and their five sockets were bronze.

Exodus 37

1 Bezalel made the ark of acacia wood: two and a half cubits was its length, and a cubit and a half its width, and a cubit and a half its height.

2 He overlaid it with pure gold, inside and outside, and made for it a crown of gold all around.

3 He cast for it four rings of gold on its four feet: two rings on its one side, and two rings on its second side.

4 He made poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.

5 He put the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, to carry the ark.

6 He made a cover of pure gold: two and a half cubits was its length, and a cubit and a half its width.

7 He made two cherubim of gold. Of beaten work he made them, at the two ends of the cover:

8 one cherub at one end on this side, and one cherub at one end on that side. From the cover he made the cherubim, at its two ends.

9 The cherubim were spreading out wings upward, screening the cover with their wings, and their faces were one toward another; toward the cover were the faces of the cherubim.

10 He made the table of acacia wood: two cubits was its length, and a cubit its width, and a cubit and a half its height.

11 He overlaid it with pure gold, and made for it a crown of gold all around.

12 He made for it a rim of a handbreadth all around, and made a crown of gold for its rim all around.

13 He cast for it four rings of gold, and put the rings on the four corners that were on its four feet.

14 Close by the rim were the rings, holders for the poles, to carry the table.

15 He made the poles of acacia wood, and overlaid them with gold, to carry the table.

16 He made the vessels that were on the table — its dishes, its pans, its bowls, and its jars with which to pour out — of pure gold.

17 He made the lampstand of pure gold. Of beaten work he made the lampstand: its base and its shaft, its cups, its knobs, and its flowers were from it.

18 And six branches went out from its sides: three branches of the lampstand from its one side, and three branches of the lampstand from its second side:

19 three cups shaped like almonds in one branch, a knob and a flower, and three cups shaped like almonds in one branch, a knob and a flower — so for the six branches going out from the lampstand.

20 And in the lampstand were four cups shaped like almonds, its knobs and its flowers.

21 And a knob under two branches from it, and a knob under two branches from it, and a knob under two branches from it — for the six branches going out from it.

22 Their knobs and their branches were from it; all of it was one beaten work of pure gold.

23 He made its lamps, seven, and its tongs and its trays, of pure gold.

24 Of a talent of pure gold he made it, and all its vessels.

25 He made the altar of incense of acacia wood: a cubit was its length, and a cubit its width, square, and two cubits its height; its horns were from it.

26 He overlaid it with pure gold — its top, its walls all around, and its horns — and made for it a crown of gold all around.

27 And he made for it two rings of gold under its crown, on its two sides, on its two sides, as holders for poles, to carry it with them.

28 He made the poles of acacia wood, and overlaid them with gold.

29 He made the holy anointing oil and the pure incense of the spices, the work of a perfumer.

Exodus 38

1 He made the altar of the burnt offering of acacia wood: five cubits was its length, and five cubits its width, square, and three cubits its height.

2 He made its horns on its four corners; its horns were from it, and he overlaid it with bronze.

3 He made all the vessels of the altar: the pots, the shovels, the basins, the forks, and the fire pans. All its vessels he made of bronze.

4 He made for the altar a grating, a work of bronze network, under its ledge, from below, up to its middle.

5 He cast four rings on the four ends of the bronze grating, as holders for the poles.

6 He made the poles of acacia wood, and overlaid them with bronze.

7 He put the poles into the rings on the sides of the altar, to carry it with them. Hollow, with planks, he made it.

8 He made the basin of bronze, and its base of bronze, from the mirrors of the serving women who served at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

9 He made the court: for the side of the Negev, southward, the hangings of the court were of fine twisted linen, a hundred cubits;

10 their pillars were twenty, and their sockets twenty, of bronze; the hooks of the pillars and their bands were of silver.

11 And for the north side, a hundred cubits; their pillars were twenty, and their sockets twenty, of bronze; the hooks of the pillars and their bands were of silver.

12 And for the west side, hangings of fifty cubits; their pillars were ten, and their sockets ten; the hooks of the pillars and their bands were of silver.

13 And for the east side, eastward, fifty cubits.

14 Hangings of fifteen cubits to the one side; their pillars were three, and their sockets three.

15 And for the second side — from this side and from that side of the gate of the court — hangings of fifteen cubits; their pillars were three, and their sockets three.

16 All the hangings of the court all around were of fine twisted linen.

17 And the sockets for the pillars were of bronze; the hooks of the pillars and their bands were of silver, and the overlaying of their tops was silver; and they were banded with silver, all the pillars of the court.

18 And the screen for the gate of the court was the work of an embroiderer, of blue and purple and scarlet and fine twisted linen; and twenty cubits was its length, and its height in width five cubits, corresponding to the hangings of the court.

19 And their pillars were four, and their sockets four, of bronze; their hooks were of silver, and the overlaying of their tops and their bands was of silver.

20 And all the pegs for the tabernacle and for the court all around were of bronze.

21 These are the accounts of the tabernacle, the tabernacle of the testimony, which were counted at the mouth of Moses — the service of the Levites, by the hand of Ithamar, son of Aaron the priest.

22 And Bezalel, son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, made all that Yahweh commanded Moses.

23 And with him was Oholiab, son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, a craftsman and a designer and an embroiderer in blue and in purple and in scarlet and in fine linen.

24 All the gold used for the work, in all the work of the holy place — and the gold of the wave offering was twenty-nine talents and seven hundred and thirty shekels, by the shekel of the sanctuary.

25 And the silver of those counted of the congregation was a hundred talents and a thousand and seven hundred and seventy-five shekels, by the shekel of the sanctuary:

26 a beka per head, half a shekel, by the shekel of the sanctuary, for everyone passing over to those counted, from twenty years old and upward — for six hundred and three thousand and five hundred and fifty.

27 And the hundred talents of silver were for casting the sockets of the holy place and the sockets of the veil: a hundred sockets for the hundred talents, a talent for a socket.

28 And from the thousand and seven hundred and seventy-five he made hooks for the pillars, and overlaid their tops, and banded them.

29 And the bronze of the wave offering was seventy talents and two thousand and four hundred shekels.

30 And with it he made the sockets for the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, and the bronze altar, and the bronze grating that belonged to it, and all the vessels of the altar,

31 and the sockets of the court all around, and the sockets of the gate of the court, and all the pegs of the tabernacle, and all the pegs of the court all around.

Exodus 39

1 And from the blue and the purple and the scarlet they made service garments, for serving in the holy place, and they made the holy garments that were for Aaron, as Yahweh commanded Moses.

2 He made the ephod of gold, blue and purple and scarlet and fine twisted linen.

3 They beat out the plates of gold and cut them into threads, to work them into the blue and into the purple and into the scarlet and into the fine linen, the work of a designer.

4 They made shoulder pieces for it, joined together; at its two ends it was joined together.

5 And the band of its fastening that was on it was from it, like its work: gold, blue and purple and scarlet and fine twisted linen, as Yahweh commanded Moses.

6 They made the onyx stones, set round in settings of gold, engraved with the engravings of a signet, according to the names of the children of Israel.

7 He set them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod, stones of remembrance for the children of Israel, as Yahweh commanded Moses.

8 He made the breastplate, the work of a designer, like the work of the ephod: gold, blue and purple and scarlet and fine twisted linen.

9 It was square, doubled they made the breastplate: a span was its length, and a span its width, doubled.

10 They filled in it four rows of stone: a row of ruby, topaz, and beryl — the first row;

11 and the second row, a turquoise, a sapphire, and a diamond;

12 and the third row, a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst;

13 and the fourth row, a chrysolite, an onyx, and a jasper; set round in settings of gold in their settings.

14 And the stones were according to the names of the children of Israel, twelve, according to their names; engravings of a signet, each according to his name, for the twelve tribes.

15 They made on the breastplate chains at the ends, a work of cords, of pure gold.

16 They made two settings of gold and two rings of gold, and put the two rings on the two ends of the breastplate.

17 They put the two cords of gold on the two rings, on the ends of the breastplate.

18 And the two ends of the two cords they put on the two settings, and put them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod, toward its front.

19 They made two rings of gold and set them on the two ends of the breastplate, on its edge that was toward the side of the ephod, inward.

20 They made two rings of gold and put them on the two shoulder pieces of the ephod from below, toward its front, close by its joining, above the band of the ephod.

21 They bound the breastplate from its rings to the rings of the ephod with a thread of blue, to be on the band of the ephod, and so that the breastplate should not be loosened from the ephod, as Yahweh commanded Moses.

22 He made the robe of the ephod, the work of a weaver, wholly of blue.

23 And the opening of the robe was within it, like the opening of a coat of mail; a binding was round its opening, so that it should not be torn.

24 They made on the skirts of the robe pomegranates of blue and purple and scarlet, twisted.

25 They made bells of pure gold, and put the bells among the pomegranates on the skirts of the robe all around, among the pomegranates:

26 a bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, on the skirts of the robe all around, for serving, as Yahweh commanded Moses.

27 They made the tunics of fine linen, the work of a weaver, for Aaron and for his sons,

28 and the turban of fine linen, and the fine headbands of fine linen, and the linen trousers of fine twisted linen,

29 and the sash of fine twisted linen and blue and purple and scarlet, the work of an embroiderer, as Yahweh commanded Moses.

30 They made the plate, the holy crown, of pure gold, and wrote on it a writing, the engravings of a signet: Holy to Yahweh.

31 They put on it a thread of blue, to put it on the turban from above, as Yahweh commanded Moses.

32 And all the work of the tabernacle of the Tent of Meeting was finished, and the children of Israel did according to all that Yahweh commanded Moses; so they did.

33 They brought the tabernacle to Moses: the tent and all its vessels, its clasps, its boards, its bars, and its pillars and its sockets,

34 and the covering of the rams' skins dyed red, and the covering of the tachash skins, and the veil of the screen,

35 the ark of the testimony and its poles, and the cover,

36 the table, all its vessels, and the bread of the presence,

37 the pure lampstand, its lamps — the lamps of the arrangement — and all its vessels, and the oil for the light,

38 and the golden altar, and the anointing oil, and the incense of the spices, and the screen for the entrance of the tent,

39 the bronze altar and the bronze grating that belonged to it, its poles and all its vessels, the basin and its base,

40 the hangings of the court, its pillars and its sockets, and the screen for the gate of the court, its cords and its pegs, and all the vessels of the service of the tabernacle for the Tent of Meeting,

41 the service garments for serving in the holy place, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons, for serving as priests.

42 According to all that Yahweh commanded Moses, so the children of Israel did all the work.

43 Moses saw all the work, and behold, they had done it: as Yahweh had commanded, so they had done; and Moses blessed them.

Exodus 40

1 Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

2 "On the day of the first month, on the first of the month, you shall raise up the tabernacle of the Tent of Meeting.

3 You shall put there the ark of the testimony, and you shall screen the ark with the veil.

4 You shall bring in the table and arrange its arrangement, and you shall bring in the lampstand and raise up its lamps.

5 You shall set the golden altar for incense before the ark of the testimony, and put the screen of the entrance for the tabernacle.

6 You shall set the altar of the burnt offering before the entrance of the tabernacle of the Tent of Meeting.

7 You shall set the basin between the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and put water there.

8 You shall set up the court all around, and put the screen of the gate of the court.

9 "You shall take the anointing oil and anoint the tabernacle and all that is in it, and make it holy, and all its vessels, and it shall be holy.

10 You shall anoint the altar of the burnt offering and all its vessels, and make the altar holy, and the altar shall be most holy.

11 You shall anoint the basin and its base, and make it holy.

12 "You shall bring Aaron and his sons near to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, and wash them with water.

13 You shall clothe Aaron with the holy garments, and anoint him, and make him holy, and he shall serve me as priest.

14 You shall bring his sons near, and clothe them with tunics.

15 You shall anoint them as you anointed their father, and they shall serve me as priests; and their anointing shall be for them for a priesthood forever, throughout their generations."

16 Moses did so: according to all that Yahweh commanded him, so he did.

17 It was in the first month, in the second year, on the first of the month, that the tabernacle was raised up.

18 Moses raised up the tabernacle, and set its sockets, and set up its boards, and put in its bars, and raised up its pillars.

19 He spread the tent over the tabernacle, and put the covering of the tent over it from above, as Yahweh commanded Moses.

20 He took and put the testimony into the ark, and set the poles on the ark, and put the cover on the ark from above.

21 He brought the ark into the tabernacle, and set up the veil of the screen, and screened the ark of the testimony, as Yahweh commanded Moses.

22 He put the table in the Tent of Meeting, on the side of the tabernacle northward, outside the veil.

23 He arranged on it an arrangement of bread before Yahweh, as Yahweh commanded Moses.

24 He set the lampstand in the Tent of Meeting, opposite the table, on the side of the tabernacle southward.

25 He raised up the lamps before Yahweh, as Yahweh commanded Moses.

26 He set the golden altar in the Tent of Meeting before the veil,

27 and burned on it incense of spices, as Yahweh commanded Moses.

28 He set up the screen of the entrance for the tabernacle.

29 He set the altar of the burnt offering at the entrance of the tabernacle of the Tent of Meeting, and offered up on it the burnt offering and the grain offering, as Yahweh commanded Moses.

30 He set the basin between the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and put water there for washing.

31 And Moses and Aaron and his sons washed from it their hands and their feet:

32 when they came into the Tent of Meeting and when they drew near to the altar, they washed, as Yahweh commanded Moses.

33 He raised up the court all around the tabernacle and the altar, and put the screen of the gate of the court. So Moses finished the work.

34 Then the cloud covered the Tent of Meeting, and the glory of Yahweh filled the tabernacle.

35 Moses could not come into the Tent of Meeting, because the cloud rested on it, and the glory of Yahweh filled the tabernacle.

36 And when the cloud was raised up from over the tabernacle, the children of Israel journeyed on, in all their journeys;

37 and if the cloud was not raised up, they did not journey until the day it was raised up.

38 For the cloud of Yahweh was on the tabernacle by day, and fire would be in it by night, in the sight of all the house of Israel, in all their journeys.

Clear English Bible — Leviticus (Chapters 1–27): A Clear English Translation

COMPLETE — This book of the Clear English Bible is complete. This is a fresh translation made directly from the Hebrew: the Masoretic text of the Westminster Leningrad Codex, verified letter by letter against the Mechon Mamre edition. It was inserted into this edition on 23 November 2026, under the editor's ruling that the Torah of this Bible rests on the Hebrew, replacing the clear-English modernization of the World English Bible Classic that stood here before. This text was prepared with AI assistance. Robert Tilford is the editor.

Draft history — 25 October 2026. Leviticus chapters 1–27 were all internally audited (AUDITED), formerly stood as drafts awaiting Robert's read-through, and were formerly labeled a partial draft, unpublished. The completion statement above was substituted for the former draft header in the final handling under Ruling 20, after the campaign's rulings had been applied and verified; the former header's history is preserved here and in the repository history.

Insertion record — 23 November 2026. The text of Leviticus in this file was replaced by the fresh translation from the Hebrew described above (27 chapters, 859 verses), in the master-insertion carried out under the editor's rulings of 22–23 November 2026. The text it replaced stands in the repository history. The differences between the two texts, each with its Hebrew ground stated, are recorded in the translation's working papers.

Leviticus 1

1 Yahweh called to Moses, and spoke to him from the Tent of Meeting, saying,

2 “Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them, ‘When a man among you brings an offering to Yahweh, you shall bring your offering from the livestock, from the herd and from the flock.

3 “‘If his offering is a burnt offering from the herd, he shall offer a male without defect. He shall offer it at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, that he may be accepted before Yahweh.

4 And he shall lay his hand on the head of the burnt offering, and it shall be accepted for him to make atonement for him.

5 And he shall slaughter the young bull before Yahweh, and Aaron's sons, the priests, shall present the blood and sprinkle the blood around on the altar that is at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

6 And he shall skin the burnt offering, and cut it into its pieces.

7 And the sons of Aaron the priest shall put fire on the altar, and arrange wood on the fire;

8 and Aaron's sons, the priests, shall arrange the pieces, the head, and the fat on the wood that is on the fire that is on the altar;

9 and its innards and its legs he shall wash with water. And the priest shall burn the whole of it on the altar, a burnt offering, a fire offering, a pleasing aroma to Yahweh.

10 “‘And if his offering is from the flock, from the sheep or from the goats, for a burnt offering, he shall offer a male without defect.

11 And he shall slaughter it on the north side of the altar before Yahweh, and Aaron's sons, the priests, shall sprinkle its blood around on the altar.

12 And he shall cut it into its pieces, and its head and its fat, and the priest shall arrange them on the wood that is on the fire that is on the altar,

13 and the innards and the legs he shall wash with water. And the priest shall offer the whole, and burn it on the altar. It is a burnt offering, a fire offering, a pleasing aroma to Yahweh.

14 “‘And if his offering to Yahweh is a burnt offering of birds, then he shall offer his offering from the turtledoves or from the young pigeons.

15 And the priest shall bring it to the altar, and pinch off its head, and burn it on the altar; and its blood shall be drained out on the wall of the altar;

16 and he shall remove its crop with its feathers, and throw it beside the altar on the east side, to the place of the ashes.

17 And he shall tear it by its wings; he shall not divide it. And the priest shall burn it on the altar, on the wood that is on the fire. It is a burnt offering, a fire offering, a pleasing aroma to Yahweh.

Leviticus 2

1 “‘And when a person offers a grain offering to Yahweh, his offering shall be fine flour, and he shall pour oil on it, and put frankincense on it.

2 And he shall bring it to Aaron's sons, the priests, and he shall take from there his handful from its fine flour and from its oil, with all its frankincense, and the priest shall burn its memorial portion on the altar, a fire offering, a pleasing aroma to Yahweh.

3 And what is left of the grain offering shall be Aaron's and his sons'. It is most holy, from the fire offerings of Yahweh.

4 “‘And when you offer a grain offering baked in the oven, it shall be unleavened cakes of fine flour mixed with oil, or unleavened wafers spread with oil.

5 And if your offering is a grain offering on the griddle, it shall be fine flour mixed with oil, unleavened.

6 You shall break it into pieces, and pour oil on it. It is a grain offering.

7 And if your offering is a grain offering of the frying pan, it shall be made of fine flour with oil.

8 And you shall bring the grain offering that is made from these things to Yahweh, and it shall be presented to the priest, and he shall bring it near to the altar.

9 And the priest shall lift out from the grain offering its memorial portion, and burn it on the altar, a fire offering, a pleasing aroma to Yahweh.

10 And what is left of the grain offering shall be Aaron's and his sons'. It is most holy, from the fire offerings of Yahweh.

11 “‘No grain offering that you offer to Yahweh shall be made leavened, for you shall burn no leaven and no honey from it as a fire offering to Yahweh.

12 You may offer them to Yahweh as an offering of first fruits, but they shall not go up on the altar for a pleasing aroma.

13 And every grain offering of yours you shall season with salt, and you shall not let the salt of the covenant of your God be lacking from your grain offering. With all your offerings you shall offer salt.

14 “‘And if you offer a grain offering of first fruits to Yahweh, you shall offer, for the grain offering of your first fruits, fresh ears roasted with fire, crushed grain of the fresh ear.

15 And you shall put oil on it, and lay frankincense on it. It is a grain offering.

16 And the priest shall burn its memorial portion, from its crushed grain and from its oil, with all its frankincense. It is a fire offering to Yahweh.

Leviticus 3

1 “‘And if his offering is a sacrifice of peace offerings, if he is offering from the herd, whether male or female, he shall offer it without defect before Yahweh.

2 And he shall lay his hand on the head of his offering, and slaughter it at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, and Aaron's sons, the priests, shall sprinkle the blood around on the altar.

3 And he shall offer from the sacrifice of the peace offerings a fire offering to Yahweh: the fat that covers the innards, and all the fat that is on the innards,

4 and the two kidneys, and the fat that is on them, which is by the loins, and the lobe on the liver; with the kidneys he shall remove it.

5 And Aaron's sons shall burn it on the altar, on the burnt offering that is on the wood that is on the fire. It is a fire offering, a pleasing aroma to Yahweh.

6 “‘And if his offering for a sacrifice of peace offerings to Yahweh is from the flock, male or female, he shall offer it without defect.

7 If he is offering a lamb as his offering, then he shall offer it before Yahweh,

8 and he shall lay his hand on the head of his offering, and slaughter it before the Tent of Meeting, and Aaron's sons shall sprinkle its blood around on the altar.

9 And he shall offer from the sacrifice of the peace offerings a fire offering to Yahweh: its fat, the whole fat tail — he shall remove it close to the backbone — and the fat that covers the innards, and all the fat that is on the innards,

10 and the two kidneys, and the fat that is on them, which is by the loins, and the lobe on the liver; with the kidneys he shall remove it.

11 And the priest shall burn it on the altar. It is food, a fire offering to Yahweh.

12 “‘And if his offering is a goat, then he shall offer it before Yahweh,

13 and he shall lay his hand on its head, and slaughter it before the Tent of Meeting, and Aaron's sons shall sprinkle its blood around on the altar.

14 And he shall offer from it his offering, a fire offering to Yahweh: the fat that covers the innards, and all the fat that is on the innards,

15 and the two kidneys, and the fat that is on them, which is by the loins, and the lobe on the liver; with the kidneys he shall remove it.

16 And the priest shall burn them on the altar. It is food, a fire offering, for a pleasing aroma. All the fat is Yahweh's.

17 It shall be a statute forever throughout your generations in all your dwellings: you shall eat no fat and no blood.’”

Leviticus 4

1 And Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

2 “Speak to the children of Israel, saying, ‘When a person sins unintentionally, in any of the commandments of Yahweh that shall not be done, and does any one of them,

3 if the anointed priest sins, so as to bring guilt on the people, then he shall offer for his sin that he has sinned a young bull without defect to Yahweh for a sin offering.

4 And he shall bring the bull to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting before Yahweh, and lay his hand on the head of the bull, and slaughter the bull before Yahweh.

5 And the anointed priest shall take from the blood of the bull, and bring it to the Tent of Meeting.

6 And the priest shall dip his finger in the blood, and sprinkle from the blood seven times before Yahweh, in front of the veil of the sanctuary.

7 And the priest shall put from the blood on the horns of the altar of fragrant incense before Yahweh, which is in the Tent of Meeting, and all the blood of the bull he shall pour out at the base of the altar of the burnt offering, which is at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

8 And all the fat of the bull of the sin offering he shall lift out from it: the fat that covers the innards, and all the fat that is on the innards,

9 and the two kidneys, and the fat that is on them, which is by the loins, and the lobe on the liver; with the kidneys he shall remove it,

10 just as it is lifted out from the ox of the sacrifice of the peace offerings. And the priest shall burn them on the altar of the burnt offering.

11 And the skin of the bull, and all its flesh, with its head and with its legs, and its innards and its dung,

12 he shall carry out, the whole bull, outside the camp to a clean place, to the place where the ashes are poured out, and burn it on wood with fire. On the place where the ashes are poured out it shall be burned.

13 “‘And if the whole congregation of Israel errs, and a matter is hidden from the eyes of the assembly, and they do any one of all the commandments of Yahweh that shall not be done, and are guilty,

14 when the sin that they have sinned is known, then the assembly shall offer a young bull for a sin offering, and bring it before the Tent of Meeting.

15 And the elders of the congregation shall lay their hands on the head of the bull before Yahweh, and the bull shall be slaughtered before Yahweh.

16 And the anointed priest shall bring from the blood of the bull to the Tent of Meeting.

17 And the priest shall dip his finger from the blood, and sprinkle seven times before Yahweh, in front of the veil.

18 And from the blood he shall put on the horns of the altar that is before Yahweh, which is in the Tent of Meeting, and all the blood he shall pour out at the base of the altar of the burnt offering, which is at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

19 And all its fat he shall lift out from it, and burn it on the altar.

20 And he shall do to the bull just as he did to the bull of the sin offering; so shall he do to it. And the priest shall make atonement for them, and they shall be forgiven.

21 And he shall carry the bull outside the camp, and burn it just as he burned the first bull. It is a sin offering for the assembly.

22 “‘When a ruler sins, and does unintentionally any one of all the commandments of Yahweh his God that shall not be done, and is guilty,

23 or his sin that he has sinned is made known to him, then he shall bring his offering, a male goat without defect.

24 And he shall lay his hand on the head of the goat, and slaughter it in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered before Yahweh. It is a sin offering.

25 And the priest shall take from the blood of the sin offering with his finger, and put it on the horns of the altar of the burnt offering, and its blood he shall pour out at the base of the altar of the burnt offering.

26 And all its fat he shall burn on the altar, like the fat of the sacrifice of the peace offerings. And the priest shall make atonement for him from his sin, and he shall be forgiven.

27 “‘And if any one person of the people of the land sins unintentionally, in doing any one of the commandments of Yahweh that shall not be done, and is guilty,

28 or his sin that he has sinned is made known to him, then he shall bring his offering, a female goat without defect, for his sin that he has sinned.

29 And he shall lay his hand on the head of the sin offering, and slaughter the sin offering in the place of the burnt offering.

30 And the priest shall take from its blood with his finger, and put it on the horns of the altar of the burnt offering, and all its blood he shall pour out at the base of the altar.

31 And all its fat he shall remove, just as fat is removed from the sacrifice of the peace offerings, and the priest shall burn it on the altar for a pleasing aroma to Yahweh. And the priest shall make atonement for him, and he shall be forgiven.

32 “‘And if he brings a lamb as his offering for a sin offering, he shall bring a female without defect.

33 And he shall lay his hand on the head of the sin offering, and slaughter it for a sin offering in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered.

34 And the priest shall take from the blood of the sin offering with his finger, and put it on the horns of the altar of the burnt offering, and all its blood he shall pour out at the base of the altar.

35 And all its fat he shall remove, just as the fat of the lamb is removed from the sacrifice of the peace offerings, and the priest shall burn them on the altar, on the fire offerings of Yahweh. And the priest shall make atonement for him for his sin that he has sinned, and he shall be forgiven.

Leviticus 5

1 “‘And when a person sins, and hears the voice of an oath, and he is a witness, whether he has seen or known, if he does not tell it, then he shall bear his iniquity.

2 Or when a person touches any unclean thing, whether the carcass of an unclean animal, or the carcass of unclean livestock, or the carcass of unclean swarming things, and it is hidden from him, and he is unclean and guilty,

3 or when he touches the uncleanness of a man, whatever his uncleanness by which he becomes unclean, and it is hidden from him, and he comes to know it, and is guilty,

4 or when a person swears, speaking rashly with the lips, to do evil or to do good, in all that a man may speak rashly with an oath, and it is hidden from him, and he comes to know it, and is guilty in one of these,

5 then when he is guilty in one of these, he shall confess that in which he has sinned,

6 and he shall bring his guilt offering to Yahweh for his sin that he has sinned, a female from the flock, a lamb or a female goat, for a sin offering, and the priest shall make atonement for him from his sin.

7 “‘And if his hand does not reach enough for a lamb, then he shall bring his guilt offering for that in which he has sinned, two turtledoves or two young pigeons, to Yahweh, one for a sin offering and one for a burnt offering.

8 And he shall bring them to the priest, and he shall offer the one for the sin offering first, and pinch off its head from the back of its neck, and shall not divide it.

9 And he shall sprinkle from the blood of the sin offering on the wall of the altar, and what remains of the blood shall be drained out at the base of the altar. It is a sin offering.

10 And the second he shall make a burnt offering, according to the ordinance, and the priest shall make atonement for him from his sin that he has sinned, and he shall be forgiven.

11 “‘And if his hand does not reach two turtledoves or two young pigeons, then he shall bring his offering for that in which he has sinned, a tenth of an ephah of fine flour, for a sin offering. He shall put no oil on it, and he shall put no frankincense on it, for it is a sin offering.

12 And he shall bring it to the priest, and the priest shall take from it his handful, its memorial portion, and burn it on the altar, on the fire offerings of Yahweh. It is a sin offering.

13 And the priest shall make atonement for him for his sin that he has sinned in any one of these, and he shall be forgiven. And it shall be the priest's, like the grain offering.’”

14 And Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

15 “When a person acts unfaithfully, a breach of faith, and sins unintentionally in the holy things of Yahweh, then he shall bring his guilt offering to Yahweh, a ram without defect from the flock, at your valuation in silver shekels, by the shekel of the sanctuary, for a guilt offering.

16 And for what he has sinned in the holy thing he shall make restitution, and he shall add a fifth of it to it, and give it to the priest. And the priest shall make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering, and he shall be forgiven.

17 “And if a person sins, and does any one of all the commandments of Yahweh that shall not be done, and he did not know, and is guilty, and bears his iniquity,

18 then he shall bring a ram without defect from the flock, at your valuation, for a guilt offering, to the priest. And the priest shall make atonement for him for his error that he erred, and he did not know, and he shall be forgiven.

19 It is a guilt offering. He has surely become guilty before Yahweh.”

Leviticus 6

1 Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying:

2 If a person sins and acts unfaithfully against Yahweh, and deals falsely with his neighbour about a deposit, or about a pledge, or about robbery, or has oppressed his neighbour,

3 or has found a lost thing and deals falsely about it and swears falsely — about any one of all the things that a man does, sinning by them —

4 then it shall be, when he sins and is guilty, that he shall restore what he took by robbery, or the thing that he got by oppression, or the deposit that was deposited with him, or the lost thing that he found,

5 or anything about which he swore falsely. He shall pay it back in full, and shall add a fifth part to it. To the one to whom it belongs he shall give it, on the day of his guilt.

6 And he shall bring his guilt offering to Yahweh: a ram without defect from the flock, according to your valuation, for a guilt offering, to the priest.

7 And the priest shall make atonement for him before Yahweh, and he shall be forgiven for any one of all the things that he does, becoming guilty by it.

8 Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying:

9 Command Aaron and his sons, saying: This is the law of the burnt offering. The burnt offering shall be on its hearth on the altar all night until morning, and the fire of the altar shall be kept burning on it.

10 The priest shall put on his linen garment, and he shall put linen breeches on his flesh, and he shall take up the ashes to which the fire has consumed the burnt offering on the altar, and he shall put them beside the altar.

11 And he shall put off his garments and put on other garments, and he shall carry the ashes outside the camp to a clean place.

12 And the fire on the altar shall be kept burning on it; it shall not go out. The priest shall burn wood on it morning by morning, and he shall arrange the burnt offering on it, and shall burn on it the fat of the peace offerings.

13 Fire shall be kept burning on the altar continually; it shall not go out.

14 And this is the law of the grain offering: the sons of Aaron shall offer it before Yahweh, in front of the altar.

15 And he shall take up from it, in his handful, some of the fine flour of the grain offering and some of its oil, and all the frankincense that is on the grain offering, and he shall burn its memorial portion on the altar, a pleasing aroma to Yahweh.

16 And what is left of it Aaron and his sons shall eat. It shall be eaten as unleavened cakes in a holy place; in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting they shall eat it.

17 It shall not be baked leavened. I have given it as their portion from my offerings by fire. It is most holy, like the sin offering and like the guilt offering.

18 Every male among the sons of Aaron shall eat it. It is a statute forever throughout your generations, from Yahweh's offerings by fire. Whatever touches them shall be holy.

19 Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying:

20 “This is the offering of Aaron and his sons, which they shall offer to Yahweh on the day he is anointed: a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a regular grain offering, half of it in the morning and half of it in the evening.

21 On a griddle it shall be made with oil. Thoroughly mixed, you shall bring it in. You shall offer the baked pieces of the grain offering as a pleasing aroma to Yahweh.

22 And the anointed priest in his place, from among his sons, shall make it. It is a statute forever to Yahweh; it shall be wholly burned.

23 And every grain offering of a priest shall be wholly burned; it shall not be eaten.”

24 Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying:

25 “Speak to Aaron and to his sons, saying: This is the law of the sin offering. In the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered, the sin offering shall be slaughtered before Yahweh. It is most holy.

26 The priest who offers it for sin shall eat it. In a holy place it shall be eaten, in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting.

27 Whatever touches its flesh shall be holy. And when any of its blood is sprinkled on a garment, you shall wash what was sprinkled on it in a holy place.

28 And an earthen vessel in which it is boiled shall be broken. And if it is boiled in a bronze vessel, it shall be scoured and rinsed in water.

29 Every male among the priests shall eat it. It is most holy.

30 And no sin offering from whose blood any is brought into the Tent of Meeting to make atonement in the holy place shall be eaten. It shall be burned with fire.”

Leviticus 7

1 And this is the law of the guilt offering. It is most holy.

2 In the place where they slaughter the burnt offering, they shall slaughter the guilt offering, and its blood he shall sprinkle on the altar all around.

3 And all its fat he shall offer from it: the fat tail, and the fat that covers the innards,

4 and the two kidneys, and the fat that is on them, which is by the loins, and the lobe on the liver; with the kidneys he shall remove it.

5 And the priest shall burn them on the altar as an offering by fire to Yahweh. It is a guilt offering.

6 Every male among the priests shall eat it. In a holy place it shall be eaten. It is most holy.

7 As the sin offering, so the guilt offering: there is one law for them. The priest who makes atonement with it, his it shall be.

8 And the priest who offers a man's burnt offering — the skin of the burnt offering that he offered shall be the priest's, his.

9 And every grain offering that is baked in the oven, and everything made in a frying pan, and on a griddle, shall be the priest's who offers it; his it shall be.

10 And every grain offering mixed with oil, or dry, shall belong to all the sons of Aaron, a man as his brother.

11 And this is the law of the sacrifice of peace offerings, which he shall offer to Yahweh.

12 If he offers it for thanksgiving, then he shall offer, with the sacrifice of thanksgiving, unleavened cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers anointed with oil, and fine flour thoroughly mixed, cakes mixed with oil.

13 With cakes of leavened bread he shall offer his offering, with the sacrifice of thanksgiving of his peace offerings.

14 And he shall offer from it one from each offering as a contribution to Yahweh. It shall be the priest's who sprinkles the blood of the peace offerings; his it shall be.

15 And the flesh of the sacrifice of thanksgiving of his peace offerings shall be eaten on the day of his offering. He shall not leave any of it until morning.

16 And if the sacrifice of his offering is a vow or a freewill offering, it shall be eaten on the day he offers his sacrifice, and on the next day what is left of it shall be eaten.

17 And what is left of the flesh of the sacrifice on the third day shall be burned with fire.

18 And if any of the flesh of the sacrifice of his peace offerings is eaten at all on the third day, it shall not be accepted. It shall not be credited to the one who offers it. It shall be an abhorrent thing, and the person who eats of it shall bear his iniquity.

19 And the flesh that touches any unclean thing shall not be eaten; it shall be burned with fire. And as for the flesh, everyone who is clean may eat flesh.

20 And the person who eats flesh from the sacrifice of peace offerings that belong to Yahweh, while his uncleanness is on him — that person shall be cut off from his people.

21 And a person who touches any unclean thing — the uncleanness of man, or an unclean animal, or any unclean detestable thing — and eats of the flesh of the sacrifice of peace offerings that belong to Yahweh, that person shall be cut off from his people.

22 Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying:

23 “Speak to the children of Israel, saying: All the fat of an ox, or a sheep, or a goat, you shall not eat.

24 And the fat of an animal that dies of itself, and the fat of an animal torn by beasts, may be used for any work, but you shall surely not eat it.
