2 “Command the children of Israel, and they shall bring to you clear olive oil, beaten, for the light, to set up a lamp continually.

3 Outside the veil of the testimony, in the tent of meeting, Aaron shall arrange it from evening to morning before Yahweh continually. It is a statute forever throughout your generations.

4 On the pure lampstand he shall arrange the lamps before Yahweh continually.

5 And you shall take fine flour and bake it into twelve loaves; two tenths of an ephah shall be in one loaf.

6 And you shall set them in two rows, six in a row, on the pure table before Yahweh.

7 And you shall put clear frankincense on the row, and it shall be for the bread as a memorial portion, a fire offering to Yahweh.

8 On the Sabbath day, on the Sabbath day, he shall arrange it before Yahweh continually, from the children of Israel, an everlasting covenant.

9 And it shall belong to Aaron and to his sons, and they shall eat it in a holy place, for it is most holy to him from Yahweh's fire offerings, a statute forever.

10 And the son of an Israelite woman — and he was the son of an Egyptian man — went out among the children of Israel, and the son of the Israelite woman and an Israelite man fought in the camp.

11 And the son of the Israelite woman pronounced the Name and cursed, and they brought him to Moses. And his mother's name was Shelomith, daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.

12 And they put him in custody, until it should be made clear to them by the mouth of Yahweh.

13 And Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

14 “Bring out the one who cursed to outside the camp, and all who heard him shall lay their hands on his head, and all the congregation shall stone him.

15 And to the children of Israel you shall speak, saying: Any man who curses his God shall bear his sin.

16 And one who pronounces the name of Yahweh shall surely be put to death; all the congregation shall surely stone him. As the foreigner, so the native-born: when he pronounces the Name, he shall be put to death.

17 And a man who strikes any human life shall surely be put to death.

18 And one who strikes an animal's life shall make it good, life for life.

19 And a man who inflicts a defect on his fellow: as he has done, so it shall be done to him —

20 fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth; as he inflicts a defect on a man, so it shall be inflicted on him.

21 And one who strikes an animal shall make it good, and one who strikes a man shall be put to death.

22 One ordinance shall there be for you: as the foreigner, so shall the native-born be, for I am Yahweh your God.

23 And Moses spoke to the children of Israel, and they brought out the one who had cursed to outside the camp, and they stoned him with stone. And the children of Israel did as Yahweh had commanded Moses.

Leviticus 25

1 Yahweh spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai, saying:

2 Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them: When you come into the land which I give you, then the land shall keep a Sabbath to Yahweh.

3 Six years you shall sow your field, and six years you shall prune your vineyard, and you shall gather in its produce.

4 But in the seventh year there shall be a Sabbath of complete rest for the land, a Sabbath to Yahweh. You shall not sow your field, and you shall not prune your vineyard.

5 What grows of itself of your harvest you shall not reap, and the grapes of your undressed vine you shall not gather. It shall be a year of complete rest for the land.

6 And the Sabbath of the land shall be for you for food: for you, and for your slave, and for your female slave, and for your hired worker, and for your settler who sojourns with you.

7 And for your cattle, and for the beast that is in your land, all its produce shall be for food. {ס}

8 You shall count for yourself seven Sabbaths of years, seven years, seven times, and the days of seven Sabbaths of years shall be for you forty-nine years.

9 And you shall sound a horn, a blast, in the seventh month, on the tenth of the month. On the Day of Atonement you shall sound the horn throughout all your land.

10 And you shall make the fiftieth year holy, and proclaim liberty in the land to all its inhabitants. It shall be a jubilee for you, and you shall return, each man to his possession, and each man to his family you shall return.

11 It shall be a jubilee; the fiftieth year shall be for you. You shall not sow, and you shall not reap what grows of itself in it, and you shall not gather the grapes of its undressed vines.

12 For it is a jubilee; it shall be holy to you. From the field you shall eat its produce.

13 In this year of jubilee you shall return, each man to his possession.

14 And when you sell a sale to your fellow, or buy from the hand of your fellow, you shall not wrong, each man, his brother.

15 According to the number of years after the jubilee you shall buy from your fellow. According to the number of years of crops he shall sell to you.

16 According to the multitude of the years you shall increase its price, and according to the fewness of the years you shall decrease its price, for he is selling to you the number of the crops.

17 And you shall not wrong, each man, his fellow, and you shall fear your God, for I am Yahweh your God.

18 And you shall do my statutes, and you shall keep my ordinances and do them, and you shall dwell on the land in safety.

19 And the land shall give its fruit, and you shall eat to fullness, and dwell in safety on it.

20 And if you say, "What shall we eat in the seventh year? Look, we shall not sow, and we shall not gather in our produce,"

21 then I will command my blessing for you in the sixth year, and it shall make the produce for the three years.

22 And you shall sow the eighth year, and eat from the produce, the old, until the ninth year. Until its produce comes in, you shall eat the old.

23 And the land shall not be sold permanently, for the land is mine, for you are strangers and settlers with me.

24 And in all the land of your possession you shall grant a redemption for the land. {ס}

25 If your brother becomes poor, and sells from his possession, then his redeemer who is near to him shall come, and shall redeem what his brother has sold.

26 And if a man has no redeemer, and his hand attains, and he finds enough for his redemption,

27 then he shall count the years of his sale, and return the surplus to the man to whom he sold it, and he shall return to his possession.

28 But if his hand has not found enough to return to him, then what he has sold shall be in the hand of the one who bought it until the year of jubilee, and it shall go out in the jubilee, and he shall return to his possession.

29 And if a man sells a dwelling house in a city of a wall, then its redemption shall be until the completion of the year of its sale. For a full year shall be its redemption.

30 And if it is not redeemed until a full year is completed for him, then the house that is in the city that has a wall shall be established permanently for the one who bought it, throughout his generations. It shall not go out in the jubilee.

31 But the houses of the villages that have no wall around them shall be reckoned with the field of the land. Redemption shall be for it, and it shall go out in the jubilee.

32 And as for the cities of the Levites, the houses of the cities of their possession, a perpetual redemption shall be for the Levites.

33 And what is redeemed from the Levites — the sale of a house and the city of his possession shall go out in the jubilee, for the houses of the cities of the Levites are their possession in the midst of the children of Israel.

34 And the field of the pasture land of their cities shall not be sold, for it is a perpetual possession for them. {ס}

35 And if your brother becomes poor, and his hand falters with you, then you shall strengthen him. As a stranger and a settler shall he live with you.

36 You shall not take interest or increase from him, and you shall fear your God, and your brother shall live with you.

37 Your money you shall not give to him at interest, and at increase you shall not give your food.

38 I am Yahweh your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt, to give you the land of Canaan, to be God for you. {ס}

39 And if your brother becomes poor with you, and sells himself to you, you shall not make him serve the service of a slave.

40 As a hired worker, as a settler, he shall be with you. Until the year of jubilee he shall serve with you.

41 And he shall go out from with you, he and his children with him, and he shall return to his family, and to the possession of his fathers he shall return.

42 For they are my slaves, whom I brought out from the land of Egypt. They shall not be sold as the sale of a slave.

43 You shall not rule over him with harshness, and you shall fear your God.

44 And your slave and your female slave whom you may have — from the nations that are around you, from them you shall buy a slave and a female slave.

45 And also from the children of the settlers who sojourn with you, from them you shall buy, and from their family that is with you, which they have begotten in your land, and they shall be for you as a possession.

46 And you shall hand them down as an inheritance to your children after you, to inherit as a possession. For ever you shall make them serve, but over your brothers, the children of Israel, each man over his brother, you shall not rule over him with harshness. {ס}

47 And if the hand of a stranger and settler with you attains, and your brother beside him becomes poor, and he sells himself to the stranger, the settler with you, or to the stock of the family of a stranger,

48 after he is sold, redemption shall be for him. One of his brothers shall redeem him.

49 Or his uncle, or the son of his uncle, shall redeem him, or one from the flesh of his flesh, from his family, shall redeem him, or his hand attains and he redeems himself.

50 And he shall reckon with the one who bought him, from the year that he sold himself to him until the year of jubilee, and the money of his sale shall be according to the number of years. As the days of a hired worker he shall be with him.

51 If there are still many in the years, according to them he shall return his redemption price from the money of his purchase.

52 And if few remain in the years until the year of jubilee, then he shall reckon with him. According to his years he shall return his redemption price.

53 As a hired worker, year by year, he shall be with him. He shall not rule over him with harshness before your eyes.

54 And if he is not redeemed by these, then he shall go out in the year of jubilee, he and his children with him.

55 For to me the children of Israel are slaves. They are my slaves, whom I brought out from the land of Egypt. I am Yahweh your God.

Leviticus 26

1 You shall make no idols for yourselves, and a carved image and a pillar you shall not raise up for yourselves, and a figured stone you shall not place in your land, to bow down on it, for I am Yahweh your God.

2 You shall keep my Sabbaths, and you shall revere my sanctuary. I am Yahweh. {ס}

3 If you walk in my statutes, and keep my commandments, and do them,

4 then I will give your rains in their time, and the land shall give its produce, and the tree of the field shall give its fruit.

5 And the threshing shall reach to the vintage for you, and the vintage shall reach to the sowing, and you shall eat your bread to fullness, and dwell in safety in your land.

6 And I will give peace in the land, and you shall lie down, and no one shall make you tremble, and I will make the evil beast cease from the land, and a sword shall not pass through your land.

7 And you shall pursue your enemies, and they shall fall before you by the sword.

8 And five of you shall pursue a hundred, and a hundred of you shall pursue ten thousand, and your enemies shall fall before you by the sword.

9 And I will turn to you, and make you fruitful, and multiply you, and establish my covenant with you.

10 And you shall eat old, long stored, and you shall bring out the old before the new.

11 And I will set my dwelling in your midst, and my soul shall not abhor you.

12 And I will walk in your midst, and I will be God for you, and you shall be a people for me.

13 I am Yahweh your God, who brought you out from the land of Egypt, from being slaves to them, and I broke the bars of your yoke, and made you walk upright. {פ}

14 But if you do not listen to me, and do not do all these commandments,

15 and if you reject my statutes, and if your soul abhors my ordinances, so that you do not do all my commandments, by your breaking my covenant,

16 I also will do this to you: I will appoint over you terror, consumption and fever, wasting the eyes and pining the soul, and you shall sow your seed in vain, and your enemies shall eat it.

17 And I will set my face against you, and you shall be struck before your enemies, and those who hate you shall rule over you, and you shall flee when no one pursues you. {ס}

18 And if, up to these, you do not listen to me, then I will go on to discipline you sevenfold for your sins.

19 And I will break the pride of your power, and I will make your heavens like iron, and your land like bronze.

20 And your strength shall be spent in vain, and your land shall not give its produce, and the tree of the land shall not give its fruit.

21 And if you walk with me contrary, and are not willing to listen to me, then I will go on to bring a plague on you sevenfold, according to your sins.

22 And I will send among you the beast of the field, and it shall bereave you, and cut off your cattle, and make you few, and your roads shall be desolate.

23 And if by these you are not disciplined toward me, and you walk with me contrary,

24 then I also will walk with you contrary, and I will strike you, I also, sevenfold for your sins.

25 And I will bring on you a sword, avenging the vengeance of the covenant, and you shall be gathered into your cities, and I will send pestilence in your midst, and you shall be given into the hand of an enemy.

26 When I break for you the staff of bread, ten women shall bake your bread in one oven, and they shall return your bread by weight, and you shall eat and not be satisfied. {ס}

27 And if in spite of this you do not listen to me, and you walk with me contrary,

28 then I will walk with you in the wrath of contrary, and I will discipline you, I also, sevenfold for your sins.

29 And you shall eat the flesh of your sons, and the flesh of your daughters you shall eat.

30 And I will destroy your high places, and cut down your sun-pillars, and put your carcasses on the carcasses of your idols, and my soul shall abhor you.

31 And I will make your cities a waste, and I will make your sanctuaries desolate, and I will not smell the scent of your soothing aroma.

32 And I myself will make the land desolate, and your enemies who dwell in it shall be appalled at it.

33 And you I will scatter among the nations, and I will draw out a sword after you, and your land shall be a desolation, and your cities shall be a waste.

34 Then the land shall make up its Sabbaths, all the days of its desolation, while you are in the land of your enemies. Then the land shall rest, and shall make up its Sabbaths.

35 All the days of its desolation it shall rest, the rest that it did not rest in your Sabbaths, when you dwelt on it.

36 And as for those who remain among you, I will bring faintness into their heart in the lands of their enemies, and the sound of a driven leaf shall pursue them, and they shall flee the flight of a sword, and fall when no one pursues.

37 And they shall stumble, each man on his brother, as before a sword, when no one pursues, and you shall have no standing before your enemies.

38 And you shall perish among the nations, and the land of your enemies shall eat you.

39 And those who remain among you shall rot away in their iniquity in the lands of your enemies, and also in the iniquities of their fathers, with them, they shall rot away.

40 And they shall confess their iniquity and the iniquity of their fathers, in their treachery that they committed against me, and also that they walked with me contrary.

41 I also walked with them contrary, and brought them into the land of their enemies. Or then their uncircumcised heart shall be humbled, and then they shall make up their iniquity.

42 And I will remember my covenant with Jacob, and also my covenant with Isaac, and also my covenant with Abraham I will remember, and I will remember the land.

43 And the land shall be left by them, and shall make up its Sabbaths in its desolation apart from them, and they shall make up their iniquity, because, and because, they rejected my ordinances, and their soul abhorred my statutes.

44 And yet, even this: when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them, and I will not abhor them, to destroy them, to break my covenant with them, for I am Yahweh their God.

45 And I will remember for them the covenant of the former ones, whom I brought out from the land of Egypt before the eyes of the nations, to be God for them. I am Yahweh.

46 These are the statutes and the ordinances and the laws that Yahweh gave between himself and the children of Israel on Mount Sinai, by the hand of Moses. {פ}

Leviticus 27

1 And Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying:

2 Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them: When a man makes a special vow, of persons to Yahweh, according to your valuation,

3 then your valuation shall be: for the male, from twenty years old to sixty years old, your valuation shall be fifty shekels of silver, by the shekel of the sanctuary.

4 And if it is a female, then your valuation shall be thirty shekels.

5 And if it is from five years old to twenty years old, then your valuation for the male shall be twenty shekels, and for the female ten shekels.

6 And if it is from a month old to five years old, then your valuation for the male shall be five shekels of silver, and for the female your valuation shall be three shekels of silver.

7 And if it is from sixty years old and upward, if it is a male, then your valuation shall be fifteen shekels, and for the female ten shekels.

8 And if he is too poor for your valuation, then he shall be set before the priest, and the priest shall value him. According to what the hand of the one who vowed attains, the priest shall value him. {ס}

9 And if it is an animal of which they bring an offering to Yahweh, all that a man gives of it to Yahweh shall be holy.

10 He shall not exchange it, and he shall not substitute it, good for bad or bad for good. And if he surely substitutes animal for animal, then it and its substitute shall be holy.

11 And if it is any unclean animal, of which they do not bring an offering to Yahweh, then he shall set the animal before the priest,

12 and the priest shall value it, between good and bad. As your valuation, the priest's, so it shall be.

13 And if he surely redeems it, then he shall add its fifth to your valuation.

14 And when a man makes his house holy, a holy thing to Yahweh, then the priest shall value it, between good and bad. As the priest values it, so it shall stand.

15 And if the one who makes it holy redeems his house, then he shall add a fifth of the money of your valuation to it, and it shall be his.

16 And if a man makes holy to Yahweh part of the field of his possession, then your valuation shall be according to its seed: the seed of a homer of barley at fifty shekels of silver.

17 If he makes his field holy from the year of jubilee, according to your valuation it shall stand.

18 And if he makes his field holy after the jubilee, then the priest shall reckon for him the money according to the years that remain until the year of jubilee, and it shall be deducted from your valuation.

19 And if the one who made the field holy surely redeems it, then he shall add a fifth of the money of your valuation to it, and it shall stand as his.

20 And if he does not redeem the field, and if he sells the field to another man, it shall not be redeemed again.

21 And the field, when it goes out in the jubilee, shall be holy to Yahweh, as a field devoted. Its possession shall be the priest's.

22 And if he makes holy to Yahweh a field of his purchase, which is not from the field of his possession,

23 then the priest shall reckon for him the amount of your valuation until the year of jubilee, and he shall give your valuation on that day, holy to Yahweh.

24 In the year of jubilee the field shall return to the one from whom he bought it, to the one to whom the possession of the land belongs.

25 And all your valuation shall be by the shekel of the sanctuary. Twenty gerahs shall be the shekel. {ס}

26 But a firstborn that is made a firstborn to Yahweh among the animals, no man shall make it holy. Whether ox or sheep, it is Yahweh's.

27 And if it is among the unclean animals, then he shall redeem it according to your valuation, and shall add its fifth to it. And if it is not redeemed, then it shall be sold according to your valuation.

28 But every devoted thing that a man devotes to Yahweh, from all that is his, from man and animal and from the field of his possession, shall not be sold and shall not be redeemed. Every devoted thing is a holy of holies to Yahweh.

29 Every devoted person who is devoted from among mankind shall not be ransomed. He shall surely be put to death.

30 And all the tithe of the land, from the seed of the land, from the fruit of the tree, is Yahweh's. It is holy to Yahweh.

31 And if a man surely redeems any of his tithe, he shall add its fifth to it.

32 And all the tithe of herd and flock, all that passes under the rod, the tenth shall be holy to Yahweh.

33 He shall not examine between good and bad, and he shall not substitute it. And if he surely substitutes it, then it and its substitute shall be holy. It shall not be redeemed.

34 These are the commandments that Yahweh commanded Moses for the children of Israel on Mount Sinai.

Clear English Bible — Numbers (Chapters 1–36): A Clear English Translation

COMPLETE — This book of the Clear English Bible is complete. This is a fresh translation made directly from the Hebrew: the Masoretic text of the Westminster Leningrad Codex, verified letter by letter against the Mechon Mamre edition. It was inserted into this edition on 23 November 2026, under the editor's ruling that the Torah of this Bible rests on the Hebrew, replacing the clear-English modernization of the World English Bible Classic that stood here before. This text was prepared with AI assistance. Robert Tilford is the editor.

Draft history — 25 October 2026. Numbers chapters 1–36 were all internally audited (AUDITED), formerly stood as drafts awaiting Robert's read-through, and were formerly labeled a partial draft, unpublished. The completion statement above was substituted for the former draft header in the final handling under Ruling 20, after the campaign's rulings had been applied and verified; the former header's history is preserved here and in the repository history.

Insertion record — 23 November 2026. The text of Numbers in this file was replaced by the fresh translation from the Hebrew described above (36 chapters, 1288 verses), in the master-insertion carried out under the editor's rulings of 22–23 November 2026. The text it replaced stands in the repository history. The differences between the two texts, each with its Hebrew ground stated, are recorded in the translation's working papers.

Numbers 1

1 Yahweh spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the Tent of Meeting, on the first day of the second month, in the second year after they had come out of the land of Egypt, saying,

2 “Take the sum of all the congregation of the children of Israel, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, every male, head by head,

3 from twenty years old and upward, all who go out to the host in Israel. You and Aaron shall count them by their hosts.

4 And with you there shall be a man of every tribe, each man the head of his fathers’ house.

5 And these are the names of the men who shall stand with you: Of Reuben: Elizur the son of Shedeur.

6 Of Simeon: Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai.

7 Of Judah: Nahshon the son of Amminadab.

8 Of Issachar: Nethanel the son of Zuar.

9 Of Zebulun: Eliab the son of Helon.

10 Of the children of Joseph: of Ephraim: Elishama the son of Ammihud; of Manasseh: Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur.

11 Of Benjamin: Abidan the son of Gideoni.

12 Of Dan: Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai.

13 Of Asher: Pagiel the son of Ochran.

14 Of Gad: Eliasaph the son of Deuel.

15 Of Naphtali: Ahira the son of Enan.”

16 These are the summoned ones of the congregation, the princes of the tribes of their fathers; they are the heads of the thousands of Israel.

17 And Moses and Aaron took these men who were designated by name.

18 And they assembled all the congregation together on the first day of the second month, and they registered their descent by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, head by head.

19 As Yahweh commanded Moses, so he counted them in the wilderness of Sinai.

20 And the children of Reuben, Israel’s firstborn, were these: their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, head by head, every male from twenty years old and upward, all who go out to the host:

21 those who were counted of them, of the tribe of Reuben, were forty-six thousand five hundred.

22 Of the children of Simeon, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, those who were counted of it, according to the number of the names, head by head, every male from twenty years old and upward, all who go out to the host:

23 those who were counted of them, of the tribe of Simeon, were fifty-nine thousand three hundred.

24 Of the children of Gad, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, all who go out to the host:

25 those who were counted of them, of the tribe of Gad, were forty-five thousand six hundred and fifty.

26 Of the children of Judah, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, all who go out to the host:

27 those who were counted of them, of the tribe of Judah, were seventy-four thousand six hundred.

28 Of the children of Issachar, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, all who go out to the host:

29 those who were counted of them, of the tribe of Issachar, were fifty-four thousand four hundred.

30 Of the children of Zebulun, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, all who go out to the host:

31 those who were counted of them, of the tribe of Zebulun, were fifty-seven thousand four hundred.

32 Of the children of Joseph, of the children of Ephraim, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, all who go out to the host:

33 those who were counted of them, of the tribe of Ephraim, were forty thousand five hundred.

34 Of the children of Manasseh, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, all who go out to the host:

35 those who were counted of them, of the tribe of Manasseh, were thirty-two thousand two hundred.

36 Of the children of Benjamin, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, all who go out to the host:

37 those who were counted of them, of the tribe of Benjamin, were thirty-five thousand four hundred.

38 Of the children of Dan, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, all who go out to the host:

39 those who were counted of them, of the tribe of Dan, were sixty-two thousand seven hundred.

40 Of the children of Asher, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, all who go out to the host:

41 those who were counted of them, of the tribe of Asher, were forty-one thousand five hundred.

42 The children of Naphtali, their generations, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, all who go out to the host:

43 those who were counted of them, of the tribe of Naphtali, were fifty-three thousand four hundred.

44 These are those who were counted, whom Moses and Aaron counted, and the princes of Israel, twelve men; each one was for his fathers’ house.

45 And all those who were counted of the children of Israel by their fathers’ houses, from twenty years old and upward, all who go out to the host in Israel, were—

46 all those who were counted were six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty.

47 But the Levites, by the tribe of their fathers, were not counted among them.

48 And Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

49 “Only the tribe of Levi you shall not count, and their sum you shall not take among the children of Israel;

50 but you shall appoint the Levites over the tabernacle of the testimony, and over all its vessels, and over all that belongs to it. They shall carry the tabernacle and all its vessels, and they shall minister to it, and they shall encamp around the tabernacle.

51 And when the tabernacle sets out, the Levites shall take it down; and when the tabernacle encamps, the Levites shall set it up. And the outsider who comes near shall be put to death.

52 And the children of Israel shall encamp, every man by his own camp, and every man by his own standard, by their hosts.

53 But the Levites shall encamp around the tabernacle of the testimony, so that there shall be no wrath on the congregation of the children of Israel. And the Levites shall keep the charge of the tabernacle of the testimony.”

54 And the children of Israel did so. According to all that Yahweh commanded Moses, so they did.

Numbers 2

1 And Yahweh spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,

2 “The children of Israel shall encamp, every man by his own standard, with the signs of their fathers’ houses. Opposite, around the Tent of Meeting, they shall encamp.

3 And those who encamp in front, eastward, shall be the standard of the camp of Judah, by their hosts. And the prince of the children of Judah is Nahshon the son of Amminadab.

4 And his host, and those who were counted of them, were seventy-four thousand six hundred.

5 And those who encamp next to him are the tribe of Issachar. And the prince of the children of Issachar is Nethanel the son of Zuar.

6 And his host, and those who were counted of it, were fifty-four thousand four hundred.

7 The tribe of Zebulun: and the prince of the children of Zebulun is Eliab the son of Helon.

8 And his host, and those who were counted of it, were fifty-seven thousand four hundred.

9 All who were counted of the camp of Judah were one hundred and eighty-six thousand four hundred, by their hosts. They shall set out first.

10 The standard of the camp of Reuben shall be southward, by their hosts. And the prince of the children of Reuben is Elizur the son of Shedeur.

11 And his host, and those who were counted of it, were forty-six thousand five hundred.

12 And those who encamp next to him are the tribe of Simeon. And the prince of the children of Simeon is Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai.

13 And his host, and those who were counted of them, were fifty-nine thousand three hundred.

14 And the tribe of Gad: and the prince of the children of Gad is Eliasaph the son of Reuel.

15 And his host, and those who were counted of them, were forty-five thousand six hundred and fifty.

16 All who were counted of the camp of Reuben were one hundred and fifty-one thousand four hundred and fifty, by their hosts. And they shall set out second.

17 Then the Tent of Meeting shall set out, with the camp of the Levites in the middle of the camps. As they encamp, so they shall set out, every man in his place, by their standards.

18 The standard of the camp of Ephraim shall be westward, by their hosts. And the prince of the children of Ephraim is Elishama the son of Ammihud.

19 And his host, and those who were counted of them, were forty thousand five hundred.

20 And next to him is the tribe of Manasseh. And the prince of the children of Manasseh is Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur.

21 And his host, and those who were counted of them, were thirty-two thousand two hundred.

22 And the tribe of Benjamin: and the prince of the children of Benjamin is Abidan the son of Gideoni.

23 And his host, and those who were counted of them, were thirty-five thousand four hundred.

24 All who were counted of the camp of Ephraim were one hundred and eight thousand one hundred, by their hosts. And they shall set out third.

25 The standard of the camp of Dan shall be northward, by their hosts. And the prince of the children of Dan is Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai.

26 And his host, and those who were counted of them, were sixty-two thousand seven hundred.

27 And those who encamp next to him are the tribe of Asher. And the prince of the children of Asher is Pagiel the son of Ochran.

28 And his host, and those who were counted of them, were forty-one thousand five hundred.

29 And the tribe of Naphtali: and the prince of the children of Naphtali is Ahira the son of Enan.

30 And his host, and those who were counted of them, were fifty-three thousand four hundred.

31 All who were counted of the camp of Dan were one hundred and fifty-seven thousand six hundred. They shall set out last, by their standards.”

32 These are those who were counted of the children of Israel by their fathers’ houses. All who were counted of the camps, by their hosts, were six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty.

33 But the Levites were not counted among the children of Israel, as Yahweh commanded Moses.

34 And the children of Israel did so. According to all that Yahweh commanded Moses, so they encamped by their standards, and so they set out, every man by his families, according to his fathers’ house.

Numbers 3

1 And these are the generations of Aaron and Moses on the day Yahweh spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai.

2 And these are the names of the sons of Aaron: Nadab the firstborn, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.

3 These are the names of the sons of Aaron, the anointed priests, whose hand he filled to serve as priests.

4 And Nadab and Abihu died before Yahweh when they brought near strange fire before Yahweh in the wilderness of Sinai, and they had no children. And Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests before Aaron their father.

5 And Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

6 “Bring the tribe of Levi near, and you shall make them stand before Aaron the priest, and they shall minister to him.

7 And they shall keep his charge and the charge of the whole congregation before the Tent of Meeting, to do the service of the tabernacle.

8 And they shall keep all the vessels of the Tent of Meeting and the charge of the children of Israel, to do the service of the tabernacle.

9 And you shall give the Levites to Aaron and to his sons. They are given, wholly given to him from the children of Israel.

10 And Aaron and his sons you shall appoint, and they shall keep their priesthood. And the outsider who comes near shall be put to death.”

11 And Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

12 “And I, behold, I have taken the Levites from among the children of Israel in place of every firstborn who opens the womb among the children of Israel, and the Levites shall be mine,

13 for every firstborn is mine. On the day I struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I made holy to me every firstborn in Israel, from man to animal. They shall be mine. I am Yahweh.”

14 And Yahweh spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, saying,

15 “Count the children of Levi by their fathers’ houses, by their families. Every male from a month old and upward you shall count.”

16 And Moses counted them at the mouth of Yahweh, as he was commanded.

17 And these were the sons of Levi by their names: Gershon, and Kohath, and Merari.

18 And these are the names of the sons of Gershon by their families: Libni and Shimei.

19 And the sons of Kohath by their families: Amram, and Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.

20 And the sons of Merari by their families: Mahli and Mushi. These are the families of the Levites by their fathers’ houses.

21 Of Gershon: the family of the Libnites and the family of the Shimeites. These are the families of the Gershonites.

22 Those who were counted of them, in the number of every male from a month old and upward, those who were counted of them were seven thousand five hundred.

23 The families of the Gershonites shall encamp behind the tabernacle, westward.

24 And the prince of the fathers’ house of the Gershonites is Eliasaph the son of Lael.

25 And the charge of the sons of Gershon in the Tent of Meeting is the tabernacle and the tent, its covering, and the screen for the entrance of the Tent of Meeting,

26 and the hangings of the court, and the screen for the entrance of the court, which is around the tabernacle and around the altar, and its cords, for all its service.

27 And of Kohath: the family of the Amramites, and the family of the Izharites, and the family of the Hebronites, and the family of the Uzzielites. These are the families of the Kohathites.

28 In the number of every male from a month old and upward, eight thousand six hundred, keeping the charge of the sanctuary.

29 The families of the sons of Kohath shall encamp on the side of the tabernacle, southward.

30 And the prince of the fathers’ house of the families of the Kohathites is Elizaphan the son of Uzziel.

31 And their charge is the ark, and the table, and the lampstand, and the altars, and the vessels of the sanctuary with which they minister, and the screen, and all its service.

32 And the prince of the princes of the Levites is Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest, appointed over those who keep the charge of the sanctuary.

33 Of Merari: the family of the Mahlites and the family of the Mushites. These are the families of Merari.

34 And those who were counted of them, in the number of every male from a month old and upward, were six thousand two hundred.

35 And the prince of the fathers’ house of the families of Merari is Zuriel the son of Abihail. On the side of the tabernacle they shall encamp, northward.

36 And the appointed charge of the sons of Merari is the boards of the tabernacle, and its bars, and its pillars, and its sockets, and all its vessels, and all its service,

37 and the pillars of the court around, and their sockets, and their pins, and their cords.

38 And those who encamp before the tabernacle, in front, before the Tent of Meeting eastward, are Moses, and Aaron, and his sons, keeping the charge of the sanctuary for the charge of the children of Israel. And the outsider who comes near shall be put to death.

39 All who were counted of the Levites, whom Moses and Aaron counted at the mouth of Yahweh, by their families, every male from a month old and upward, were twenty-two thousand.

40 And Yahweh said to Moses, “Count every firstborn male of the children of Israel from a month old and upward, and take the number of their names.

41 And you shall take the Levites for me—I am Yahweh—in place of every firstborn among the children of Israel, and the animals of the Levites in place of every firstborn among the animals of the children of Israel.”

42 And Moses counted, as Yahweh commanded him, every firstborn among the children of Israel.

43 And every firstborn male, in the number of names from a month old and upward, of those who were counted of them, was twenty-two thousand two hundred and seventy-three.

44 And Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

45 “Take the Levites in place of every firstborn among the children of Israel, and the animals of the Levites in place of their animals, and the Levites shall be mine. I am Yahweh.

46 And for the redeemed of the two hundred and seventy-three who are over and above the Levites, from the firstborn of the children of Israel,

47 you shall take five shekels for each head; by the shekel of the sanctuary you shall take it—twenty gerahs is the shekel.

48 And you shall give the silver to Aaron and to his sons, the redeemed of those who are over among them.”

49 And Moses took the silver of the redemption from those who were over and above those redeemed by the Levites;

50 from the firstborn of the children of Israel he took the silver, one thousand three hundred and sixty-five, by the shekel of the sanctuary;

51 and Moses gave the silver of the redeemed to Aaron and to his sons, at the mouth of Yahweh, as Yahweh commanded Moses.

Numbers 4

1 And Yahweh spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,

2 “Take the sum of the sons of Kohath from among the sons of Levi, by their families, by their fathers’ houses,

3 from thirty years old and upward, and until fifty years old, everyone who comes to the host, to do work in the Tent of Meeting.

4 This is the service of the sons of Kohath in the Tent of Meeting: the most holy things.

5 And Aaron and his sons shall come, when the camp sets out, and they shall take down the veil, the screen, and they shall cover the ark of the testimony with it,

6 and they shall put on it a covering of tachash skin, and they shall spread a cloth wholly of blue above, and they shall set its poles.

7 And on the table of the Presence they shall spread a cloth of blue, and they shall put on it the dishes, and the spoons, and the bowls, and the jars for pouring out, and the continual bread shall be on it.

8 And they shall spread on them a cloth of scarlet worm, and they shall cover it with a covering of tachash skin, and they shall set its poles.

9 And they shall take a cloth of blue and cover the lampstand of the light, and its lamps, and its tongs, and its trays, and all its oil vessels with which they minister to it.

10 And they shall put it and all its vessels into a covering of tachash skin, and they shall put it on the carrying bar.

11 And on the golden altar they shall spread a cloth of blue, and they shall cover it with a covering of tachash skin, and they shall set its poles.

12 And they shall take all the vessels of ministry with which they minister in the sanctuary, and they shall put them into a cloth of blue, and they shall cover them with a covering of tachash skin, and they shall put them on the carrying bar.

13 And they shall remove the fat ashes from the altar, and they shall spread on it a cloth of purple.

14 And they shall put on it all its vessels with which they minister on it—the trays, the forks, and the shovels, and the basins, all the vessels of the altar—and they shall spread on it a covering of tachash skin, and they shall set its poles.

15 And when Aaron and his sons have finished covering the sanctuary and all the vessels of the sanctuary, when the camp sets out, after that the sons of Kohath shall come to carry, and they shall not touch the sanctuary, lest they die. These are the burden of the sons of Kohath in the Tent of Meeting.

16 And the charge of Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest is the oil for the light, and the incense of spices, and the continual grain offering, and the anointing oil—the charge of the whole tabernacle and all that is in it, in the sanctuary and in its vessels.”

17 And Yahweh spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying,

18 “Do not cut off the tribe of the families of the Kohathites from among the Levites;

19 but do this for them, and they shall live and not die, when they come near the most holy things: Aaron and his sons shall come and set them, every man to his service and to his burden;

20 and they shall not come in to see, as the sanctuary is swallowed up, and die.”

21 And Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

22 “Take the sum of the sons of Gershon also, by their fathers’ houses, by their families;

23 from thirty years old and upward until fifty years old you shall count them, everyone who comes to serve the service, to do service in the Tent of Meeting.

24 This is the service of the families of the Gershonites, to serve and to bear burdens:

25 they shall carry the curtains of the tabernacle, and the Tent of Meeting, its covering, and the covering of tachash that is on it above, and the screen for the entrance of the Tent of Meeting,

26 and the hangings of the court, and the screen for the entrance of the gate of the court, which is around the tabernacle and around the altar, and their cords, and all the vessels of their service, and all that is done for them, and they shall serve.

27 At the mouth of Aaron and his sons shall be all the service of the sons of the Gershonites, for all their burden and for all their service; and you shall appoint over them, as a charge, all their burden.

28 This is the service of the families of the sons of the Gershonites in the Tent of Meeting, and their charge is under the hand of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest.”

29 “The sons of Merari, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, you shall count them;

30 from thirty years old and upward and until fifty years old you shall count them, everyone who comes to the host, to do the service of the Tent of Meeting.

31 And this is the charge of their burden, for all their service in the Tent of Meeting: the boards of the tabernacle, and its bars, and its pillars, and its sockets,

32 and the pillars of the court around, and their sockets, and their pins, and their cords, for all their vessels and for all their service. And by names you shall appoint the vessels of the charge of their burden.

33 This is the service of the families of the sons of Merari, for all their service in the Tent of Meeting, under the hand of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest.”

34 And Moses and Aaron and the princes of the congregation counted the sons of the Kohathites, by their families and by their fathers’ houses,

35 from thirty years old and upward and until fifty years old, everyone who comes to the host, to do service in the Tent of Meeting.

36 And those who were counted of them, by their families, were two thousand seven hundred and fifty.

37 These are those who were counted of the families of the Kohathites, everyone who serves in the Tent of Meeting, whom Moses and Aaron counted at the mouth of Yahweh, by the hand of Moses.

38 And those who were counted of the sons of Gershon, by their families and by their fathers’ houses,

39 from thirty years old and upward and until fifty years old, everyone who comes to the host, to do service in the Tent of Meeting,

40 those who were counted of them, by their families, by their fathers’ houses, were two thousand six hundred and thirty.

41 These are those who were counted of the families of the sons of Gershon, everyone who serves in the Tent of Meeting, whom Moses and Aaron counted at the mouth of Yahweh.

42 And those who were counted of the families of the sons of Merari, by their families, by their fathers’ houses,

43 from thirty years old and upward and until fifty years old, everyone who comes to the host, to do service in the Tent of Meeting,

44 those who were counted of them, by their families, were three thousand two hundred.

45 These are those who were counted of the families of the sons of Merari, whom Moses and Aaron counted at the mouth of Yahweh, by the hand of Moses.

46 All those who were counted, whom Moses and Aaron and the princes of Israel counted—the Levites—by their families and by their fathers’ houses,

47 from thirty years old and upward and until fifty years old, everyone who comes to do the work of service and the work of bearing burdens in the Tent of Meeting,

48 those who were counted of them were eight thousand five hundred and eighty.

49 At the mouth of Yahweh they counted them, by the hand of Moses, every man to his service and to his burden, and so they were counted, as Yahweh commanded Moses.

Numbers 5

1 And Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

2 “Command the children of Israel, and they shall send out from the camp everyone who has a scaly skin disease, and everyone who has a discharge, and everyone who is unclean by a dead person.

3 From male to female you shall send them out; to outside the camp you shall send them, so that they do not defile their camp, in the midst of which I dwell.”

4 And the children of Israel did so, and sent them out to outside the camp; as Yahweh spoke to Moses, so the children of Israel did.

5 And Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

6 “Speak to the children of Israel: When a man or a woman commits any of all the sins of mankind, acting unfaithfully against Yahweh, and that person is guilty,

7 then they shall confess their sin that they have done, and he shall make restitution for his guilt in full, and shall add a fifth of it to it, and shall give it to the one against whom he has been guilty.

8 But if the man has no redeemer to whom restitution may be made for the guilt, the restitution for guilt that is restored to Yahweh shall be the priest’s, besides the ram of the atonement, by which atonement shall be made for him.

9 And every contribution of all the holy things of the children of Israel, which they bring near to the priest, shall be his.

10 And a man’s holy things shall be his; whatever a man gives to the priest, it shall be his.”

11 And Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

12 “Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them: If any man’s wife goes astray, and acts unfaithfully against him,

13 and a man lies with her, a lying of seed, and it is hidden from the eyes of her husband, and she is concealed, and she has been defiled, and there is no witness against her, and she has not been caught,

14 and a spirit of jealousy passes over him, and he is jealous of his wife, and she has been defiled; or a spirit of jealousy passes over him, and he is jealous of his wife, and she has not been defiled;

15 then the man shall bring his wife to the priest, and shall bring her offering for her: a tenth of an ephah of barley flour. He shall pour no oil on it, and shall put no frankincense on it, for it is a grain offering of jealousy, a grain offering of remembrance, bringing iniquity to remembrance.

16 And the priest shall bring her near, and shall set her before Yahweh.

17 And the priest shall take holy water in an earthen vessel; and from the dust that is on the floor of the tabernacle the priest shall take, and shall put it into the water.

18 And the priest shall set the woman before Yahweh, and shall loosen the hair of the woman’s head, and shall put into her hands the grain offering of remembrance, which is the grain offering of jealousy. And in the priest’s hand shall be the bitter water that brings the curse.

19 And the priest shall make her swear, and shall say to the woman, ‘If no man has lain with you, and if you have not gone astray into uncleanness under your husband, be clear from this bitter water that brings the curse.

20 But you, if you have gone astray under your husband, and if you have been defiled, and a man has given his lying with you, besides your husband—’

21 then the priest shall make the woman swear with the oath of the curse, and the priest shall say to the woman, ‘Yahweh shall make you a curse and an oath among your people, when Yahweh makes your thigh fall away and your belly swell;

22 and this water that brings the curse shall go into your inward parts, to make the belly swell and the thigh fall away.’ And the woman shall say, ‘Amen, Amen.’

23 ‘And the priest shall write these curses in the book, and shall wipe them out into the bitter water.

24 And he shall make the woman drink the bitter water that brings the curse; and the water that brings the curse shall enter into her, and become bitter.

25 And the priest shall take the grain offering of jealousy from the woman’s hand, and shall wave the grain offering before Yahweh, and shall bring it near to the altar.

26 And the priest shall take a handful from the grain offering, its remembrance portion, and shall burn it on the altar, and afterwards shall make the woman drink the water.

27 And when he has made her drink the water, then it shall be, if she has been defiled and has acted unfaithfully against her husband, that the water that brings the curse shall enter into her and become bitter, and her belly shall swell, and her thigh shall fall away; and the woman shall be a curse in the midst of her people.

28 And if the woman has not been defiled, but is clean, then she shall be clear, and shall be sown with seed.

29 ‘This is the law of jealousy, when a wife goes astray under her husband, and has been defiled,

30 or when a spirit of jealousy passes over a man, and he is jealous of his wife; then he shall set the woman before Yahweh, and the priest shall do to her all this law.

31 And the man shall be clear from iniquity, and that woman shall bear her iniquity.’”

Numbers 6

1 And Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

2 “Speak to the children of Israel, and say to them: When a man or a woman makes a special vow, the vow of a Nazirite, to consecrate himself to Yahweh,

3 he shall abstain from wine and strong drink. He shall drink no vinegar of wine and no vinegar of strong drink, and he shall drink no liquor of grapes, and he shall eat no grapes, fresh or dried.

4 All the days of his Nazirite vow he shall eat nothing that is made from the vine of the wine, from the kernels to the skin.

5 ‘All the days of the vow of his Nazirite consecration no razor shall pass over his head; until the days are fulfilled in which he consecrates himself to Yahweh, he shall be holy; he shall let the locks of the hair of his head grow long.

6 ‘All the days of his consecrating himself to Yahweh he shall not come near a dead person.

7 For his father and for his mother, for his brother and for his sister, he shall not defile himself for them when they die, because the consecration of his God is on his head.

8 All the days of his Nazirite vow he is holy to Yahweh.

9 ‘And if someone dies beside him very suddenly, and he defiles his consecrated head, then he shall shave his head on the day of his cleansing; on the seventh day he shall shave it.

10 And on the eighth day he shall bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest, to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

11 And the priest shall prepare one for a sin offering and one for a burnt offering, and shall make atonement for him for what he sinned by the dead person, and shall sanctify his head on that same day.

12 And he shall consecrate to Yahweh the days of his Nazirite vow, and shall bring a lamb in its first year for a guilt offering; and the former days shall fall away, because his consecration was defiled.

13 ‘And this is the law of the Nazirite: on the day the days of his Nazirite vow are fulfilled, he shall bring him to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting,

14 and he shall bring near his offering to Yahweh: one lamb in its first year without defect for a burnt offering, and one ewe lamb in its first year without defect for a sin offering, and one ram without defect for peace offerings,

15 and a basket of unleavened bread, cakes of fine flour mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers anointed with oil, and their grain offering and their drink offerings.

16 And the priest shall bring them near before Yahweh, and shall prepare his sin offering and his burnt offering.

17 And the ram he shall prepare as a sacrifice of peace offerings to Yahweh, with the basket of unleavened bread; and the priest shall prepare its grain offering and its drink offering.

18 And the Nazirite shall shave, at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, the head of his consecration, and shall take the hair of the head of his consecration and put it on the fire that is under the sacrifice of the peace offerings.

19 And the priest shall take the boiled shoulder from the ram, and one unleavened cake from the basket, and one unleavened wafer, and shall put them into the hands of the Nazirite after his shaving of his consecration;

20 and the priest shall wave them as a wave offering before Yahweh. It is holy for the priest, together with the breast of the wave offering and together with the thigh of the contribution. And afterwards the Nazirite may drink wine.

21 ‘This is the law of the Nazirite who vows, his offering to Yahweh for his Nazirite vow, besides what his hand can reach. According to his vow that he vows, so shall he do, according to the law of his Nazirite vow.’”

22 And Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

23 “Speak to Aaron and to his sons, saying, ‘Thus you shall bless the children of Israel.’ Say to them,

24 ‘Yahweh bless you and keep you.

25 Yahweh make his face shine on you and be gracious to you.

26 Yahweh lift up his face to you and set peace for you.’

27 “And they shall put my name on the children of Israel, and I shall bless them.”

Numbers 7

1 And it came to pass on the day that Moses finished setting up the tabernacle, he anointed it and sanctified it and all its vessels, and the altar and all its vessels, and he anointed them and sanctified them.

2 And the princes of Israel, the heads of their fathers’ houses, offered. They were the princes of the tribes; they were those who stood over those who were counted.

3 And they brought their offering before Yahweh: six covered wagons and twelve oxen — a wagon for two of the princes, and an ox for each one — and they brought them near before the tabernacle.

4 And Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

5 “Take them from them, and they shall be for doing the service of the Tent of Meeting; and you shall give them to the Levites, to each man according to his service.”

6 And Moses took the wagons and the oxen, and gave them to the Levites.

7 The two wagons and the four oxen he gave to the sons of Gershon, according to their service.

8 And the four wagons and the eight oxen he gave to the sons of Merari, according to their service, under the hand of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest.

9 And to the sons of Kohath he gave none, because the service of the holy things was on them; they shall bear them on the shoulder.

10 And the princes brought near the dedication offering of the altar on the day that it was anointed, and the princes brought their offering near before the altar.

89 And when Moses went into the Tent of Meeting to speak with him, he heard the voice speaking to him from above the cover that was on the ark of the testimony, from between the two cherubim; and he spoke to him.

Numbers 8

1 And Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

2 “Speak to Aaron, and say to him: ‘When you raise the lamps, the seven lamps shall give light toward the front of the lampstand.’”

3 And Aaron did so: toward the front of the lampstand he raised its lamps, as Yahweh commanded Moses.

4 And this was the work of the lampstand: beaten work of gold; from its base to its flower it was beaten work. According to the pattern that Yahweh showed Moses, so he made the lampstand.

5 And Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

6 “Take the Levites from among the children of Israel, and cleanse them.

7 And thus you shall do to them, to cleanse them: sprinkle on them the water of purification, and they shall pass a razor over all their flesh, and shall wash their clothes, and shall cleanse themselves.

8 And they shall take a young bull and its grain offering, fine flour mixed with oil; and a second young bull you shall take for a sin offering.

9 And you shall bring the Levites near before the Tent of Meeting, and you shall assemble the whole congregation of the children of Israel.

10 And you shall bring the Levites near before Yahweh, and the children of Israel shall lay their hands on the Levites,

11 and Aaron shall wave the Levites as a wave offering before Yahweh, from the children of Israel, and they shall be to do the service of Yahweh.

12 “And the Levites shall lay their hands on the heads of the bulls; and you shall prepare the one as a sin offering and the one as a burnt offering to Yahweh, to make atonement for the Levites.

13 And you shall set the Levites before Aaron and before his sons, and shall wave them as a wave offering to Yahweh.

14 And you shall separate the Levites from among the children of Israel, and the Levites shall be mine.

15 “And after that the Levites shall come to serve the Tent of Meeting; and you shall cleanse them, and shall wave them as a wave offering.

16 For they are given, given to me from among the children of Israel; in place of every first issue of the womb, the firstborn of all from the children of Israel, I have taken them to myself.

17 For mine is every firstborn among the children of Israel, among man and among beast. On the day I struck every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I sanctified them to myself.

18 And I have taken the Levites in place of every firstborn among the children of Israel.

19 And I have given the Levites, given to Aaron and to his sons, from among the children of Israel, to do the service of the children of Israel in the Tent of Meeting, and to make atonement for the children of Israel; and there shall be no plague among the children of Israel when the children of Israel come near to the sanctuary.”

20 And Moses and Aaron and the whole congregation of the children of Israel did so to the Levites: according to all that Yahweh commanded Moses about the Levites, so the children of Israel did to them.

21 And the Levites purified themselves, and washed their clothes; and Aaron waved them as a wave offering before Yahweh, and Aaron made atonement for them, to cleanse them.

22 And after that the Levites came to do their service in the Tent of Meeting before Aaron and before his sons: as Yahweh commanded Moses about the Levites, so they did to them.

23 And Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

24 “This is what is for the Levites: from twenty-five years old and upward he shall come to serve in the service-host in the work of the Tent of Meeting;

25 and from fifty years old he shall return from the service-host of the work, and shall serve no more,

26 but he shall minister with his brothers in the Tent of Meeting, to keep the charge, and service he shall not do. So you shall do to the Levites in their charges.”

Numbers 9

1 Yahweh spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the second year after they came out of the land of Egypt, in the first month, saying,

2 “And the children of Israel shall keep the Passover at its appointed time.

3 On the fourteenth day in this month, between the evenings, you shall keep it at its appointed time; according to all its statutes and according to all its ordinances you shall keep it.”

4 And Moses spoke to the children of Israel to keep the Passover.

5 And they kept the Passover in the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, between the evenings, in the wilderness of Sinai; according to all that Yahweh commanded Moses, so the children of Israel did.

6 And there were men who were unclean by a dead person, and they could not keep the Passover on that day; and they came near before Moses and before Aaron on that day.

7 And those men said to him, “We are unclean by a dead person. Why shall we be kept back, so as not to bring near the offering of Yahweh at its appointed time among the children of Israel?”

8 And Moses said to them, “Stand, and I will hear what Yahweh will command concerning you.”

9 And Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

10 “Speak to the children of Israel, saying, ‘Any man, any man who is unclean by a dead person, or is on a far journey, for you or for your generations, he shall keep a Passover to Yahweh.

11 In the second month, on the fourteenth day, between the evenings, they shall keep it; with unleavened bread and bitter herbs they shall eat it.

12 They shall leave none of it until morning, and they shall not break a bone in it; according to all the statute of the Passover they shall keep it.

13 And the man who is clean, and was not on a journey, and refrains from keeping the Passover, that person shall be cut off from his people, because he did not bring near the offering of Yahweh at its appointed time; that man shall bear his sin.

14 And when a sojourner sojourns with you and keeps a Passover to Yahweh, according to the statute of the Passover and according to its ordinance, so he shall do; one statute shall be for you, and for the sojourner, and for the native of the land.’ ”

15 And on the day the tabernacle was raised up, the cloud covered the tabernacle, for the Tent of the Testimony; and in the evening it was on the tabernacle like the appearance of fire until morning.

16 So it shall be always: the cloud shall cover it, and the appearance of fire by night.

17 And according to the lifting up of the cloud from over the Tent, after that the children of Israel journeyed; and in the place where the cloud dwelt, there the children of Israel encamped.

18 At the mouth of Yahweh the children of Israel journeyed, and at the mouth of Yahweh they encamped; all the days that the cloud dwelt on the tabernacle they encamped.

19 And when the cloud prolonged on the tabernacle many days, the children of Israel kept the charge of Yahweh and did not journey.

20 And there were times when the cloud was a number of days on the tabernacle; at the mouth of Yahweh they encamped, and at the mouth of Yahweh they journeyed.

21 And there were times when the cloud was from evening until morning, and the cloud was lifted up in the morning, and they journeyed; or a day and a night, and the cloud was lifted up, and they journeyed.

22 Or two days, or a month, or a year, when the cloud prolonged on the tabernacle, dwelling on it, the children of Israel encamped and did not journey; and when it was lifted up, they journeyed.

23 At the mouth of Yahweh they encamped, and at the mouth of Yahweh they journeyed; they kept the charge of Yahweh, at the mouth of Yahweh by the hand of Moses.

Numbers 10

1 And Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

2 “Make for yourself two trumpets of silver; of beaten work you shall make them, and they shall be for you for calling the congregation and for causing the camps to journey.

3 And when they blow with them, all the congregation shall gather to you at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

4 And if they blow with one, the princes, the heads of the thousands of Israel, shall gather to you.

5 And when you blow a blast, the camps encamped on the east shall journey.

6 And when you blow a blast a second time, the camps encamped on the south shall journey; a blast they shall blow for their journeys.

7 And when the assembly is gathered, you shall blow, but you shall not sound a blast.

8 And the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall blow with the trumpets, and they shall be for you as a statute forever, for your generations.

9 And when you go to war in your land against the adversary who oppresses you, you shall sound a blast with the trumpets, and you shall be remembered before Yahweh your God, and you shall be saved from your enemies.

10 And on the day of your gladness, and at your appointed times, and at the heads of your months, you shall blow with the trumpets over your burnt offerings and over the sacrifices of your peace offerings, and they shall be for you as a memorial before your God; I am Yahweh your God.”

11 And it happened in the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth of the month, the cloud was lifted up from over the tabernacle of the Testimony.

12 And the children of Israel journeyed by their journeys from the wilderness of Sinai, and the cloud dwelt in the wilderness of Paran.

13 And they journeyed first, at the mouth of Yahweh by the hand of Moses.

14 And the standard of the camp of the children of Judah journeyed first, by their hosts, and over his host was Nahshon son of Amminadab.

15 And over the host of the tribe of the children of Issachar was Nethanel son of Zuar.

16 And over the host of the tribe of the children of Zebulun was Eliab son of Helon.

17 And the tabernacle was taken down, and the sons of Gershon and the sons of Merari, bearers of the tabernacle, journeyed.

18 And the standard of the camp of Reuben journeyed by their hosts, and over his host was Elizur son of Shedeur.

19 And over the host of the tribe of the children of Simeon was Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.

20 And over the host of the tribe of the children of Gad was Eliasaph son of Deuel.

21 And the Kohathites journeyed, bearers of the sanctuary, and they set up the tabernacle before they came.

22 And the standard of the camp of the children of Ephraim journeyed by their hosts, and over his host was Elishama son of Ammihud.

23 And over the host of the tribe of the children of Manasseh was Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.

24 And over the host of the tribe of the children of Benjamin was Abidan son of Gideoni.

25 And the standard of the camp of the children of Dan, gatherer for all the camps, journeyed by their hosts, and over his host was Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.

26 And over the host of the tribe of the children of Asher was Pagiel son of Ochran.

27 And over the host of the tribe of the children of Naphtali was Ahira son of Enan.

28 These are the journeys of the children of Israel by their hosts, and they journeyed.

29 And Moses said to Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses’ father-in-law, “We are journeying to the place of which Yahweh said, ‘I will give it to you.’ Come with us, and we will do good to you, for Yahweh has spoken good concerning Israel.”

30 And he said to him, “I will not go, but I will go to my land and to my birthplace.”

31 And he said, “Please do not leave us, because you know our encamping in the wilderness, and you will be eyes for us.

32 And it shall be, if you go with us, it shall be that the good that Yahweh will do for us, we will do for you.”

33 And they journeyed from the mountain of Yahweh a journey of three days, and the ark of the covenant of Yahweh journeyed before them a journey of three days, to seek out a resting place for them.

34 And the cloud of Yahweh was over them by day when they journeyed from the camp.

35 And it happened when the ark journeyed, Moses said, “Rise, Yahweh, and let your enemies be scattered, and let those who hate you flee from before you.”

36 And when it rested, he said, “Return, Yahweh, to the ten thousands of the thousands of Israel.”

Numbers 11

1 And the people were as complainers, evil in the ears of Yahweh; and Yahweh heard, and his anger burned, and the fire of Yahweh burned among them and consumed at the edge of the camp.

2 And the people cried out to Moses, and Moses prayed to Yahweh, and the fire sank down.

3 And he called the name of that place Taberah, because the fire of Yahweh burned among them.

4 And the mixed crowd that was among them craved a craving, and the children of Israel also wept again and said, “Who will feed us meat?

5 We remember the fish that we ate in Egypt for nothing, the cucumbers and the melons and the leeks and the onions and the garlic;

6 and now our soul is dried up; there is nothing at all; only to the manna are our eyes.”

7 And the manna was like coriander seed, and its appearance was like the appearance of bdellium.

8 The people went about and gathered and ground in the mills, or crushed in the mortar, and boiled in the pot, and made it into cakes, and its taste was like the taste of a cake of oil.

9 And when the dew came down on the camp at night, the manna came down on it.

10 And Moses heard the people weeping by their families, each man at the entrance of his tent, and Yahweh’s anger burned greatly, and in Moses’ eyes it was evil.

11 And Moses said to Yahweh, “Why have you done evil to your slave, and why have I not found favour in your eyes, to put the burden of all this people on me?

12 Did I conceive all this people? Did I give birth to him, that you say to me, ‘Carry him in your bosom, as the nurse carries the sucking child,’ to the ground that you swore to their fathers?

13 From where have I meat to give to all this people? For they weep against me, saying, ‘Give us meat, and let us eat.’

14 I alone cannot carry all this people, because it is too heavy for me.

15 And if you are doing thus to me, please kill me outright, if I have found favour in your eyes, and let me not see my evil.”

16 And Yahweh said to Moses, “Gather for me seventy men from the elders of Israel, whom you know that they are elders of the people and its officers, and take them to the Tent of Meeting, and they shall stand there with you.

17 And I will come down and speak with you there, and I will take from the spirit that is on you and put on them, and they will bear with you the burden of the people, and you will not bear it, you alone.

18 And to the people you shall say, ‘Sanctify yourselves for tomorrow, and you shall eat meat, for you wept in the ears of Yahweh, saying, “Who will feed us meat? For it was good for us in Egypt.” And Yahweh will give you meat, and you shall eat.

19 You shall not eat one day, and not two days, and not five days, and not ten days, and not twenty days,

20 but a month of days, until it comes out from your nostrils and becomes loathsome to you, because you rejected Yahweh who is among you and wept before him, saying, ‘Why did we come out of Egypt?’ ”

21 And Moses said, “Six hundred thousand on foot are the people among whom I am, and you have said, ‘I will give meat to them, and they shall eat a month of days.’

22 Shall flocks and herds be slaughtered for them and suffice for them? Or shall all the fish of the sea be gathered for them and suffice for them?”

23 And Yahweh said to Moses, “Is Yahweh’s hand short? Now you shall see whether my word happens to you or not.”

24 And Moses went out and spoke to the people the words of Yahweh, and he gathered seventy men from the elders of the people and set them around the Tent.

25 And Yahweh came down in the cloud and spoke to him, and took from the spirit that was on him and gave on the seventy men, the elders; and when the spirit rested on them, they prophesied, and did not continue.

26 And two men remained in the camp; the name of the one was Eldad, and the name of the second was Medad, and the spirit rested on them — and they were among those written, but they had not gone out to the Tent — and they prophesied in the camp.

27 And the young man ran and told Moses and said, “Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp.”

28 And Joshua son of Nun, Moses’ attendant from his youth, answered and said, “My lord Moses, restrain them.”

29 And Moses said to him, “Are you jealous for me? Would that all Yahweh’s people were prophets, that Yahweh would put his spirit on them!”

30 And Moses was gathered to the camp, he and the elders of Israel.

31 And a wind went out from Yahweh and drove quails from the sea and let them fall on the camp, about a day’s journey this way and about a day’s journey that way, around the camp, and about two cubits over the face of the ground.

32 And the people rose all that day and all the night and all the next day and gathered the quails; the one who gathered least gathered ten homers, and they spread them out for themselves, spreading them out, around the camp.

33 The meat was still between their teeth, before it was cut off, and Yahweh’s anger burned against the people, and Yahweh struck the people with a very great blow.

34 And he called the name of that place Kibroth Hattaavah, because there they buried the people who craved.

35 From Kibroth Hattaavah the people journeyed to Hazeroth, and they were at Hazeroth.

Numbers 12

1 And Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses concerning the Cushite woman whom he had taken, for he had taken a Cushite woman.

2 And they said, “Has Yahweh indeed spoken only through Moses? Has he not spoken also through us?” And Yahweh heard.

3 And the man Moses was very humble, more than any man who was on the face of the ground.

4 And Yahweh said suddenly to Moses and to Aaron and to Miriam, “Come out, you three, to the Tent of Meeting.” And the three of them went out.

5 And Yahweh came down in a pillar of cloud and stood at the entrance of the Tent and called Aaron and Miriam, and the two of them went out.

6 And he said, “Hear, please, my words: If there is a prophet among you, I, Yahweh, make myself known to him in a vision; in a dream I speak with him.

7 Not so my slave Moses; in all my house he is faithful.

8 Mouth to mouth I speak with him, and plainly, and not in riddles, and he looks at the form of Yahweh. And why were you not afraid to speak against my slave, against Moses?”

9 And Yahweh’s anger burned against them, and he went.

10 And the cloud turned away from over the Tent, and behold, Miriam was leprous like snow; and Aaron turned to Miriam, and behold, she was leprous.

11 And Aaron said to Moses, “Please, my lord, please do not lay on us the sin in which we acted foolishly and in which we sinned.

12 Please let her not be like the dead, whose flesh is half consumed when he comes out from his mother’s womb.”

13 And Moses cried out to Yahweh, saying, “God, please, heal her, please.”

14 And Yahweh said to Moses, “And if her father had actually spit in her face, would she not be ashamed seven days? She shall be shut up seven days outside the camp, and afterwards she shall be gathered in.”

15 And Miriam was shut up outside the camp seven days, and the people did not journey until Miriam was gathered in.

16 And afterwards the people journeyed from Hazeroth and encamped in the wilderness of Paran.

Numbers 13

1 And Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

2 “Send men for yourself, and they shall explore the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the children of Israel. You shall send one man, one man for the tribe of his fathers, every one a prince among them.”

3 And Moses sent them from the wilderness of Paran at the mouth of Yahweh. All of them were men, heads of the children of Israel.

4 And these are their names: for the tribe of Reuben, Shammua son of Zaccur.

5 For the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat son of Hori.

6 For the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh.

7 For the tribe of Issachar, Igal son of Joseph.

8 For the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Nun.

9 For the tribe of Benjamin, Palti son of Raphu.

10 For the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel son of Sodi.

11 For the tribe of Joseph, for the tribe of Manasseh, Gaddi son of Susi.

12 For the tribe of Dan, Ammiel son of Gemalli.

13 For the tribe of Asher, Sethur son of Michael.

14 For the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi son of Vophsi.

15 For the tribe of Gad, Geuel son of Machi.

16 These are the names of the men whom Moses sent to explore the land. And Moses called Hoshea son of Nun Joshua.

17 And Moses sent them to explore the land of Canaan, and said to them, “Go up this way in the Negev, and go up into the hill country.

18 And see the land, what it is, and the people who dwell on it — is he strong or weak, is he few or many?

19 And what is the land in which he dwells — is it good or bad? And what are the cities in which he dwells — in camps, or in strongholds?
