Joshua 1

1 After Moses, the servant of Yahweh, had died, Yahweh said to Joshua son of Nun, who had attended Moses:

2 "Moses my servant is dead. So now get up and cross this Jordan, you and all this people, into the land I am giving them, to the children of Israel.

3 Every place where the sole of your foot steps, I have given it to you, just as I promised Moses.

4 From the wilderness and this Lebanon as far as the great river, the river Euphrates, all the land of the Hittites, and as far as the Great Sea where the sun goes down, that will be your territory.

5 No one will be able to stand against you all the days of your life. As I was with Moses, so I will be with you; I will not let you go, and I will not abandon you.

6 Be strong and courageous, for you will give this people possession of the land that I swore to their fathers to give them.

7 Only be strong and very courageous, taking care to act according to all the Torah that Moses my servant commanded you. Do not turn aside from it to the right or to the left, so that you may succeed wherever you go.

8 This book of the Torah must not leave your mouth; you shall recite it quietly day and night, so that you take care to do all that is written in it. For then you will make your way prosper, and then you will succeed.

9 Have I not commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Do not tremble and do not be dismayed, for Yahweh your God is with you wherever you go."

10 Then Joshua gave orders to the officers of the people:

11 "Go through the camp and order the people: Prepare provisions for yourselves, for in three days you will cross this Jordan, to enter and take possession of the land that Yahweh your God is giving you to possess."

12 And to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh, Joshua said:

13 "Remember what Moses, the servant of Yahweh, commanded you: Yahweh your God is giving you rest, and he will give you this land.

14 Your wives, your little ones, and your livestock will stay in the land Moses gave you beyond the Jordan. But you will cross ahead of your brothers, armed for battle, all you fighting men, and you will help them,

15 until Yahweh gives your brothers rest, as he has given you, and they too take possession of the land that Yahweh your God is giving them. Then you may return to the land of your possession and possess it, the land Moses, the servant of Yahweh, gave you beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise."

16 They answered Joshua: "All that you command us we will do, and wherever you send us we will go.

17 Just as we obeyed Moses in everything, so we will obey you. Only may Yahweh your God be with you, as he was with Moses.

18 Anyone who defies your word and does not obey your commands in all that you order him shall be put to death. Only be strong and courageous."

Joshua 2

1 Joshua son of Nun sent two men secretly from Shittim as spies, saying, "Go and look over the land, and Jericho." They went and entered the house of a prostitute named Rahab, and spent the night there.

2 The king of Jericho was told: "Look, men from the children of Israel came here tonight to search out the land."

3 So the king of Jericho sent word to Rahab: "Bring out the men who came to you and entered your house, for they have come to search out the whole land."

4 But the woman had taken the two men and hidden them. She said, "Yes, the men did come to me, but I did not know where they were from.

5 When the gate was about to be shut, at dark, the men went out. I do not know where they went. Chase after them quickly, and you will catch them."

6 In fact she had brought them up to the roof and hidden them among the stalks of flax that she had laid out on the roof.

7 The men pursued them on the road to the Jordan, as far as the fords, and the gate was shut as soon as the pursuers had gone out after them.

8 Before the spies lay down to sleep, she came up to them on the roof

9 and said to the men: "I know that Yahweh has given you the land, that dread of you has fallen on us, and that all who live in the land melt away before you.

10 For we have heard how Yahweh dried up the waters of the Sea of Reeds before you when you came out of Egypt, and what you did to the two kings of the Amorites beyond the Jordan, to Sihon and to Og, whom you devoted to destruction.

11 When we heard it, our hearts melted, and no spirit remained in anyone because of you, for Yahweh your God — he is God in heaven above and on earth below.

12 So now, please swear to me by Yahweh: as I have shown you loyal love, you in turn will show loyal love to my father's house, and you will give me a trustworthy sign,

13 and you will keep alive my father and my mother, my brothers and my sisters, and all who belong to them, and you will rescue our lives from death."

14 The men said to her, "Our lives in place of yours, even to death, if you do not tell this business of ours. And when Yahweh gives us the land, we will show you loyal love and faithfulness."

15 Then she lowered them by a rope through the window, for her house was set into the city wall, and she lived within the wall.

16 She told them, "Go into the hill country, so the pursuers do not come upon you. Hide there for three days, until the pursuers return, and afterward go on your way."

17 The men said to her, "We will be free of this oath of yours that you made us swear:

18 When we come into the land, you must tie this cord of scarlet thread in the window through which you lowered us, and gather your father, your mother, your brothers, and all your father's household to you in the house.

19 Anyone who goes out of the doors of your house into the street, his blood will be on his own head, and we will be guiltless. But anyone who stays with you in the house, his blood will be on our head if a hand is laid on him.

20 And if you tell this business of ours, we will be free of your oath that you made us swear."

21 She said, "Let it be as you say." She sent them away, and they left, and she tied the scarlet cord in the window.

22 They went and reached the hill country, and stayed there three days until the pursuers returned. The pursuers searched all along the road and did not find them.

23 Then the two men turned back, came down from the hill country, crossed over, and came to Joshua son of Nun, and told him everything that had happened to them.

24 They said to Joshua, "Surely Yahweh has given the whole land into our hands, and all who live in the land melt away before us."

Joshua 3

1 Joshua rose early in the morning, and they set out from Shittim and came to the Jordan, he and all the children of Israel, and they lodged there before crossing.

2 At the end of three days, the officers went through the camp

3 and ordered the people: "When you see the ark of the covenant of Yahweh your God, with the Levitical priests carrying it, you shall set out from your place and follow it.

4 But keep a distance between you and it, about two thousand cubits by measure. Do not come near it, so that you may know the way you must go, for you have not passed this way before."

5 Joshua said to the people, "Make yourselves holy, for tomorrow Yahweh will do wonders among you."

6 Then Joshua said to the priests, "Take up the ark of the covenant and cross ahead of the people." So they took up the ark of the covenant and went ahead of the people.

7 Yahweh said to Joshua, "Today I will begin to make you great in the eyes of all Israel, so that they may know that as I was with Moses, so I will be with you.

8 You shall order the priests who carry the ark of the covenant: When you reach the edge of the waters of the Jordan, stand still in the Jordan."

9 Joshua said to the children of Israel, "Come here and listen to the words of Yahweh your God."

10 And Joshua said, "By this you will know that the living God is among you, and that he will surely drive out before you the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Hivites, the Perizzites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, and the Jebusites.

11 See, the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth is crossing ahead of you into the Jordan.

12 So now choose twelve men from the tribes of Israel, one man for each tribe.

13 And when the soles of the feet of the priests who carry the ark of Yahweh, the Lord of all the earth, come to rest in the waters of the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan will be cut off — the waters flowing down from above — and they will stand in a single heap."

14 So when the people set out from their tents to cross the Jordan, the priests carrying the ark of the covenant were ahead of the people.

15 When those carrying the ark reached the Jordan and the feet of the priests carrying the ark dipped into the edge of the water — now the Jordan overflows all its banks throughout the days of harvest —

16 the waters flowing down from above stopped and rose in a single heap a long way off, at Adam, the city beside Zarethan, while the waters flowing down to the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, were completely cut off. And the people crossed opposite Jericho.

17 The priests who carried the ark of the covenant of Yahweh stood firm on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan, while all Israel crossed on dry ground, until the whole nation had finished crossing the Jordan.

Joshua 4

1 When the whole nation had finished crossing the Jordan, Yahweh said to Joshua:

2 "Take twelve men from the people, one man from each tribe,

3 and order them: Take up twelve stones from here, from the middle of the Jordan, from the place where the priests' feet stood firm, carry them across with you, and set them down at the camp where you will spend this night."

4 So Joshua called the twelve men he had appointed from the children of Israel, one man from each tribe,

5 and Joshua said to them, "Cross ahead of the ark of Yahweh your God into the middle of the Jordan, and each of you lift a stone onto his shoulder, according to the number of the tribes of the children of Israel,

6 so that this may be a sign among you. When your children ask in days to come, 'What are these stones to you?'

7 you shall tell them: The waters of the Jordan were cut off before the ark of the covenant of Yahweh. When it crossed the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan were cut off. And these stones will be a memorial for the children of Israel forever."

8 The children of Israel did as Joshua commanded. They took up twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan, as Yahweh had told Joshua, according to the number of the tribes of the children of Israel, carried them across with them to the camp, and set them down there.

9 Joshua also set up twelve stones in the middle of the Jordan, in the place where the feet of the priests who carried the ark of the covenant had stood, and they are there to this day.

10 The priests who carried the ark stood in the middle of the Jordan until everything was completed that Yahweh had commanded Joshua to tell the people, according to all that Moses had commanded Joshua. And the people hurried across.

11 When all the people had finished crossing, the ark of Yahweh and the priests crossed over in front of the people.

12 The children of Reuben, the children of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh crossed, armed for battle, ahead of the children of Israel, as Moses had told them.

13 About forty thousand men equipped for the army crossed before Yahweh for battle, to the plains of Jericho.

14 On that day Yahweh made Joshua great in the eyes of all Israel, and they held him in awe, as they had held Moses in awe, all the days of his life.

15 Yahweh said to Joshua:

16 "Order the priests who carry the ark of the testimony to come up out of the Jordan."

17 So Joshua ordered the priests: "Come up out of the Jordan."

18 When the priests who carried the ark of the covenant of Yahweh came up from the middle of the Jordan, and the soles of the priests' feet were lifted onto dry ground, the waters of the Jordan returned to their place and flowed over all its banks as before.

19 The people came up from the Jordan on the tenth day of the first month and camped at Gilgal, on the eastern edge of Jericho.

20 And those twelve stones that they had taken from the Jordan, Joshua set up at Gilgal.

21 He said to the children of Israel, "When your children ask their fathers in days to come, 'What are these stones?'

22 you shall make it known to your children: Israel crossed this Jordan on dry land.

23 For Yahweh your God dried up the waters of the Jordan before you until you had crossed, just as Yahweh your God did to the Sea of Reeds, which he dried up before us until we had crossed,

24 so that all the peoples of the earth may know the hand of Yahweh, that it is mighty, and so that you may fear Yahweh your God all your days."

Joshua 5

1 When all the kings of the Amorites who were west of the Jordan and all the kings of the Canaanites who were by the sea heard that Yahweh had dried up the waters of the Jordan before the children of Israel until they had crossed over, their hearts melted, and there was no spirit left in them because of the children of Israel.

2 At that time Yahweh said to Joshua, "Make knives of flint for yourself, and circumcise the children of Israel again, a second time."

3 So Joshua made knives of flint and circumcised the children of Israel at the Hill of the Foreskins.

4 This is the reason Joshua circumcised them: all the people who came out of Egypt, the males, all the men of war, had died in the wilderness on the way after they came out of Egypt.

5 For all the people who came out had been circumcised, but all the people who were born in the wilderness on the way as they came out of Egypt had not been circumcised.

6 For the children of Israel walked in the wilderness for forty years, until the whole nation, the men of war who came out of Egypt, had perished, because they did not listen to the voice of Yahweh. Yahweh had sworn to them that he would not let them see the land that Yahweh had sworn to their fathers to give us, a land flowing with milk and honey.

7 And he raised up their children in their place; Joshua circumcised them, for they were uncircumcised, because they had not been circumcised on the way.

8 When the whole nation had finished being circumcised, they stayed where they were in the camp until they had recovered.

9 And Yahweh said to Joshua, "Today I have rolled the reproach of Egypt away from you." So the name of that place was called Gilgal, and it is so to this day.

10 The children of Israel camped at Gilgal, and they kept the Passover on the fourteenth day of the month, in the evening, on the plains of Jericho.

11 On the day after the Passover, on that very day, they ate from the produce of the land, unleavened cakes and parched grain.

12 The manna stopped the next day, when they ate from the produce of the land, and the children of Israel had manna no longer; that year they ate from the yield of the land of Canaan.

13 When Joshua was near Jericho, he lifted his eyes and looked, and there a man was standing in front of him with his sword drawn in his hand. Joshua went to him and said to him, "Are you for us, or for our enemies?"

14 He said, "No; I have now come as commander of the host of Yahweh." Joshua fell on his face to the ground and bowed down, and he said to him, "What message does my lord have for his servant?"

15 The commander of the host of Yahweh said to Joshua, "Take your sandal off your foot, for the place where you stand is holy." And Joshua did so.

Joshua 6

1 Now Jericho was shut up tight because of the children of Israel; no one went out and no one came in.

2 Yahweh said to Joshua, "See, I have given Jericho into your hand, and its king, and its mighty men of valor."

3 "You shall march around the city, all the men of war, going around the city once; this you shall do for six days."

4 "Seven priests shall carry seven trumpets of rams' horns before the ark, and on the seventh day you shall march around the city seven times, and the priests shall blow the trumpets."

5 "When they sound a long blast on the ram's horn, when you hear the sound of the trumpet, all the people shall shout with a great shout; then the wall of the city will fall down flat, and the people shall go up, each man straight ahead."

6 Joshua son of Nun called the priests and said to them, "Take up the ark of the covenant, and let seven priests carry seven trumpets of rams' horns before the ark of Yahweh."

7 And he said to the people, "Move forward and march around the city, and let the armed force pass on before the ark of Yahweh."

8 When Joshua had spoken to the people, the seven priests carrying the seven trumpets of rams' horns before Yahweh passed on and blew the trumpets, and the ark of the covenant of Yahweh followed after them.

9 The armed force went before the priests who blew the trumpets, and the rear guard went after the ark, going on and blowing the trumpets as they went.

10 Joshua had commanded the people, "You shall not shout and you shall not let your voice be heard, and no word shall come out of your mouth, until the day I say to you, 'Shout!' Then you shall shout."

11 So he had the ark of Yahweh go around the city, circling it once; then they came into the camp and spent the night in the camp.

12 Joshua rose early in the morning, and the priests took up the ark of Yahweh.

13 The seven priests carrying the seven trumpets of rams' horns before the ark of Yahweh went on continually and blew the trumpets; the armed force went before them, and the rear guard came after the ark of Yahweh, going on and blowing the trumpets as they went.

14 On the second day they marched around the city once and returned to the camp; so they did for six days.

15 On the seventh day they rose early, at the rising of the dawn, and marched around the city in the same way seven times; only on that day did they march around the city seven times.

16 At the seventh time, when the priests blew the trumpets, Joshua said to the people, "Shout, for Yahweh has given you the city!"

17 "The city and all that is in it shall be devoted to destruction to Yahweh. Only Rahab the prostitute shall live, she and all who are with her in the house, because she hid the messengers we sent."

18 "But you, keep yourselves from the things devoted to destruction, lest you take from what is devoted to destruction and so make the camp of Israel itself a thing devoted to destruction and bring trouble on it."

19 "All the silver and gold and the vessels of bronze and iron are holy to Yahweh; they shall go into the treasury of Yahweh."

20 So the people shouted, and the trumpets were blown. When the people heard the sound of the trumpet, the people shouted with a great shout, and the wall fell down flat, and the people went up into the city, each man straight ahead, and they captured the city.

21 They devoted to destruction all that was in the city, both man and woman, young and old, and ox and sheep and donkey, with the edge of the sword.

22 To the two men who had spied out the land Joshua said, "Go into the house of the prostitute and bring out from there the woman and all who belong to her, as you swore to her."

23 The young men, the spies, went in and brought out Rahab and her father and her mother and her brothers and all who belonged to her; they brought out all her relatives, and they placed them outside the camp of Israel.

24 They burned the city with fire, and all that was in it; only the silver and the gold and the vessels of bronze and iron they put into the treasury of the house of Yahweh.

25 Rahab the prostitute and her father's household and all who belonged to her Joshua kept alive, and she has lived in the midst of Israel to this day, because she hid the messengers whom Joshua sent to spy out Jericho.

26 Joshua swore an oath at that time, saying, "Cursed before Yahweh is the man who rises up and rebuilds this city, Jericho; at the cost of his firstborn he shall lay its foundation, and at the cost of his youngest son he shall set up its gates."

27 Yahweh was with Joshua, and his fame spread through all the land.

Joshua 7

1 The children of Israel broke faith in regard to the things devoted to destruction: Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took some of the things devoted to destruction, and the anger of Yahweh burned against the children of Israel.

2 Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, which is beside Beth-aven, east of Bethel, and he said to them, "Go up and spy out the land." The men went up and spied out Ai.

3 They returned to Joshua and said to him, "Do not let all the people go up; let about two thousand or three thousand men go up and strike Ai. Do not weary all the people there, for they are few."

4 So about three thousand men of the people went up there, and they fled before the men of Ai.

5 The men of Ai struck down about thirty-six of them, and chased them from before the gate as far as Shebarim and struck them on the slope; and the heart of the people melted and became like water.

6 Joshua tore his clothes and fell on his face to the ground before the ark of Yahweh until the evening, he and the elders of Israel, and they put dust on their heads.

7 Joshua said, "Ah, Lord Yahweh, why did you bring this people across the Jordan at all, to give us into the hand of the Amorites, to destroy us? If only we had been content to stay on the other side of the Jordan!"

8 "Please, Lord, what can I say, now that Israel has turned its back before its enemies?"

9 "The Canaanites and all the inhabitants of the land will hear of it and will surround us and cut off our name from the earth; and what will you do for your great name?"

10 Yahweh said to Joshua, "Get up! Why are you fallen on your face like this?"

11 "Israel has sinned; they have also transgressed my covenant that I commanded them. They have also taken from the things devoted to destruction, and they have also stolen, and they have also deceived, and they have also put it among their own belongings."

12 "Therefore the children of Israel cannot stand before their enemies; they turn their backs before their enemies, because they have become a thing devoted to destruction. I will no longer be with you unless you destroy the things devoted to destruction from among you."

13 "Get up, consecrate the people, and say: Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow, for thus says Yahweh, the God of Israel: There is a thing devoted to destruction in your midst, Israel; you cannot stand before your enemies until you remove the thing devoted to destruction from among you."

14 "In the morning you shall come near by your tribes; the tribe that Yahweh takes shall come near by families, the family that Yahweh takes shall come near by households, and the household that Yahweh takes shall come near man by man."

15 "The one who is taken with the things devoted to destruction shall be burned with fire, he and all that belongs to him, because he has transgressed the covenant of Yahweh and because he has done a disgraceful thing in Israel."

16 Joshua rose early in the morning and brought Israel near by its tribes, and the tribe of Judah was taken.

17 He brought near the family of Judah, and the family of the Zerahites was taken; he brought near the family of the Zerahites man by man, and Zabdi was taken.

18 He brought near his household man by man, and Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, was taken.

19 Joshua said to Achan, "My son, please give glory to Yahweh, the God of Israel, and give him confession; tell me now what you have done; do not hide it from me."

20 Achan answered Joshua and said, "Truly, I have sinned against Yahweh, the God of Israel, and this is what I did."

21 "When I saw among the spoil a fine mantle from Shinar, and two hundred shekels of silver, and a bar of gold weighing fifty shekels, I coveted them and took them; and see, they are hidden in the ground in the middle of my tent, with the silver under it."

22 Joshua sent messengers, and they ran to the tent; and see, it was hidden in his tent, with the silver under it.

23 They took them from the middle of the tent and brought them to Joshua and to all the children of Israel, and they laid them out before Yahweh.

24 Joshua, and all Israel with him, took Achan son of Zerah, and the silver and the mantle and the bar of gold, and his sons and his daughters, and his oxen and his donkeys and his sheep, and his tent and all that belonged to him, and they brought them up to the Valley of Achor.

25 Joshua said, "How you have troubled us! Yahweh will trouble you this day." And all Israel stoned him with stones; they burned them with fire and stoned them with stones.

26 They raised over him a great heap of stones, which stands to this day, and Yahweh turned from the fierceness of his anger. Therefore the name of that place has been called the Valley of Achor to this day.

Joshua 8

1 Yahweh said to Joshua, "Do not fear and do not be dismayed. Take with you all the people of war, and arise, go up to Ai. See, I have given into your hand the king of Ai and his people and his city and his land."

2 "You shall do to Ai and its king as you did to Jericho and its king, except that its spoil and its livestock you may take as plunder for yourselves. Place an ambush for the city behind it."

3 Joshua arose, and all the people of war with him, to go up to Ai; Joshua chose thirty thousand men, mighty men of valor, and sent them out by night.

4 He commanded them, "See, you are to lie in ambush against the city, behind the city; do not go very far from the city, but all of you be ready."

5 "I and all the people who are with me will approach the city; when they come out against us as they did the first time, we will flee before them."

6 "They will come out after us until we have drawn them away from the city, for they will say, 'They are fleeing before us as the first time.' So we will flee before them."

7 "Then you shall rise from the ambush and take possession of the city, for Yahweh your God will give it into your hand."

8 "When you have seized the city, you shall set the city on fire; you shall do according to the word of Yahweh. See, I have commanded you."

9 Joshua sent them out, and they went to the place of ambush and stayed between Bethel and Ai, west of Ai, while Joshua spent that night among the people.

10 Joshua rose early in the morning and mustered the people, and he went up, he and the elders of Israel, before the people to Ai.

11 All the people of war who were with him went up and drew near and came in front of the city, and they camped north of Ai, with the valley between them and Ai.

12 He took about five thousand men and set them in ambush between Bethel and Ai, west of the city.

13 The people placed the whole camp that was north of the city and its rear guard west of the city, and Joshua went that night into the middle of the valley.

14 When the king of Ai saw it, they hurried and rose early, and the men of the city went out against Israel to battle, he and all his people, at the appointed place in front of the Arabah; but he did not know that there was an ambush against him behind the city.

15 Joshua and all Israel let themselves seem beaten before them and fled by the way of the wilderness.

16 All the people who were in Ai were called out to pursue after them; they pursued after Joshua and were drawn away from the city.

17 There was not a man left in Ai or Bethel who did not go out after Israel; they left the city open and pursued after Israel.

18 Yahweh said to Joshua, "Stretch out the javelin that is in your hand toward Ai, for I will give it into your hand." Joshua stretched out the javelin that was in his hand toward the city.

19 The ambush rose quickly from its place and ran as soon as he stretched out his hand, and they entered the city and captured it, and they hurried and set the city on fire.

20 When the men of Ai turned behind them, they saw, and there the smoke of the city was going up to heaven, and they had no strength to flee this way or that way; and the people who had fled toward the wilderness turned back against the pursuers.

21 When Joshua and all Israel saw that the ambush had captured the city and that the smoke of the city was going up, they turned back and struck down the men of Ai.

22 The others came out from the city against them, so they were in the midst of Israel, some on this side and some on that side; and they struck them down until no survivor or fugitive was left to them.

23 They captured the king of Ai alive and brought him to Joshua.

24 When Israel had finished killing all the inhabitants of Ai in the field, in the wilderness where they had pursued them, and they had all fallen by the edge of the sword until they were finished, all Israel returned to Ai and struck it with the edge of the sword.

25 All who fell that day, both men and women, were twelve thousand, all the people of Ai.

26 Joshua did not draw back his hand, which he had stretched out with the javelin, until he had devoted all the inhabitants of Ai to destruction.

27 Only the livestock and the spoil of that city Israel took as plunder for themselves, according to the word of Yahweh that he commanded Joshua.

28 Joshua burned Ai and made it a heap forever, a desolation to this day.

29 He hanged the king of Ai on a tree until the evening; at the going down of the sun Joshua commanded, and they took his corpse down from the tree and threw it at the entrance of the gate of the city, and raised over it a great heap of stones, which stands to this day.

30 Then Joshua built an altar to Yahweh, the God of Israel, on Mount Ebal,

31 as Moses the servant of Yahweh had commanded the children of Israel, as it is written in the book of the Torah of Moses: an altar of whole stones on which no iron had been lifted. On it they offered burnt offerings to Yahweh and sacrificed peace offerings.

32 There, on the stones, he wrote a copy of the Torah of Moses, which he wrote in the presence of the children of Israel.

33 All Israel, and its elders and officers and its judges, stood on this side and on that side of the ark, in front of the priests, the Levites, who carried the ark of the covenant of Yahweh, the stranger as well as the native-born, half of them in front of Mount Gerizim and half of them in front of Mount Ebal, as Moses the servant of Yahweh had commanded at first, to bless the people of Israel.

34 Afterward he read all the words of the Torah, the blessing and the curse, according to all that is written in the book of the Torah.

35 There was not a word of all that Moses commanded that Joshua did not read in front of all the assembly of Israel, and the women and the little ones and the stranger who walked among them.

Joshua 9

1 When all the kings on the other side of the Jordan heard of it — in the hill country, in the lowland, and along the whole shore of the Great Sea facing Lebanon: the Hittite, the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite —

2 they assembled together to make war on Joshua and on Israel, with one accord.

3 But the inhabitants of Gibeon heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and to Ai,

4 and they too acted with cunning: they set out and posed as envoys, taking worn-out sacks for their donkeys and wineskins that were worn out, split, and patched,

5 with worn-out, patched sandals on their feet and worn-out clothes on their backs, and all the bread they took for the journey was dry and crumbled.

6 They came to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal and said to him and to the men of Israel, "We have come from a distant land, so now make a covenant with us."

7 Then the man of Israel said to the Hivite, "Perhaps you are living right among us; how then can I make a covenant with you?"

8 They said to Joshua, "We are your servants." And Joshua said to them, "Who are you, and where do you come from?"

9 They answered him, "Your servants have come from a very distant land because of the name of Yahweh your God, for we have heard the report of him and all that he did in Egypt,

10 and all that he did to the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan — to Sihon king of Heshbon and to Og king of Bashan, who was at Ashtaroth.

11 Our elders and all the inhabitants of our land said to us, 'Take provisions in hand for the journey, go to meet them, and say to them: We are your servants; now make a covenant with us.'

12 This is our bread: we took it warm from our houses as our provision on the day we set out to come to you, and now, see, it is dry and crumbled.

13 And these wineskins, which we filled when they were new — see, they have burst. And these clothes and sandals of ours have worn out because the journey was so very long."

14 So the men took some of their provisions, but they did not ask for the word of Yahweh.

15 Joshua made peace with them and made a covenant with them, to let them live, and the leaders of the congregation swore an oath to them.

16 Three days after they had made the covenant with them, they heard that these people were near them and were living among them.

17 The children of Israel set out and on the third day reached their cities; their cities were Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath-jearim.

18 But the children of Israel did not strike them down, because the leaders of the congregation had sworn to them by Yahweh, the God of Israel, and the whole congregation grumbled against the leaders.

19 All the leaders said to the whole congregation, "We ourselves have sworn to them by Yahweh, the God of Israel, so now we cannot touch them.

20 This is what we will do to them: we will let them live, so that wrath does not come on us because of the oath we swore to them."

21 The leaders said to them, "Let them live." So they became woodcutters and water carriers for the whole congregation, as the leaders had told them.

22 Joshua summoned them and spoke to them, saying, "Why did you deceive us, saying, 'We are very far from you,' when you live among us?

23 Now therefore you are cursed, and there will never cease to be from among you a slave — woodcutters and water carriers for the house of my God."

24 They answered Joshua and said, "Because your servants were told, and told plainly, what Yahweh your God commanded Moses his servant: to give you the whole land and to destroy all the inhabitants of the land before you. We were very much afraid for our lives because of you, and so we did this thing.

25 Now, see, we are in your hand; do to us whatever seems good and right in your eyes."

26 So he did that to them: he rescued them from the hand of the children of Israel, and they did not kill them.

27 That day Joshua made them woodcutters and water carriers for the congregation and for the altar of Yahweh, to this day, in the place that he would choose.

Joshua 10

1 When Adonizedek king of Jerusalem heard that Joshua had captured Ai and devoted it to destruction — as he had done to Jericho and its king, so he had done to Ai and its king — and that the inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace with Israel and were among them,

2 they were greatly afraid, because Gibeon was a large city, like one of the royal cities, greater than Ai, and all its men were warriors.

3 So Adonizedek king of Jerusalem sent word to Hoham king of Hebron, to Piram king of Jarmuth, to Japhia king of Lachish, and to Debir king of Eglon, saying,

4 "Come up to me and help me, and let us strike Gibeon, for it has made peace with Joshua and with the children of Israel."

5 The five kings of the Amorites — the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon — gathered and went up, they and all their camps, and they encamped against Gibeon and fought against it.

6 The men of Gibeon sent word to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal, saying, "Do not withdraw your hand from your servants; come up to us quickly, save us, and help us, for all the kings of the Amorites who live in the hill country have gathered against us."

7 So Joshua went up from Gilgal, he and all the people of war with him, and all the mighty warriors.

8 Yahweh said to Joshua, "Do not fear them, for I have given them into your hand; not one man of them will stand before you."

9 Joshua came upon them suddenly, having marched up from Gilgal all night.

10 Yahweh threw them into confusion before Israel, and Israel struck them with a great blow at Gibeon, pursued them by the road of the ascent of Beth-horon, and struck them as far as Azekah and Makkedah.

11 As they fled before Israel, while they were on the descent of Beth-horon, Yahweh hurled great stones from the sky on them as far as Azekah, and they died; more died by the hailstones than the children of Israel killed by the sword.

12 Then Joshua spoke to Yahweh, on the day Yahweh gave the Amorites over before the children of Israel, and he said in the sight of Israel: "Sun, stand still at Gibeon, and moon, in the valley of Aijalon."

13 And the sun stood still and the moon stopped, until the nation took vengeance on its enemies. Is this not written in the Book of Jashar? The sun stood in the middle of the sky and did not hurry to set for about a whole day.

14 There has been no day like it before it or after it, when Yahweh listened to the voice of a man, for Yahweh fought for Israel.

15 Then Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, to the camp at Gilgal.

16 Those five kings fled and hid in the cave at Makkedah.

17 It was told to Joshua, saying, "The five kings have been found hiding in the cave at Makkedah."

18 Joshua said, "Roll large stones against the mouth of the cave, and station men over it to guard them;

19 but as for you, do not stand still — pursue your enemies and cut off their rear; do not let them enter their cities, for Yahweh your God has given them into your hand."

20 When Joshua and the children of Israel had finished striking them with a very great blow until they were finished off, and the survivors who remained of them had entered the fortified cities,

21 all the people returned in peace to the camp, to Joshua at Makkedah; no one sharpened his tongue against any of the children of Israel.

22 Then Joshua said, "Open the mouth of the cave and bring those five kings out of the cave to me."

23 They did so, and brought those five kings out of the cave to him: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon.

24 When they brought those kings out to Joshua, Joshua called all the men of Israel and said to the commanders of the men of war who had gone with him, "Come near; put your feet on the necks of these kings." They came near and put their feet on their necks.

25 Joshua said to them, "Do not fear and do not be dismayed; be strong and courageous, for this is what Yahweh will do to all your enemies against whom you fight."

26 Afterward Joshua struck them down, put them to death, and hung them on five trees, and they hung on the trees until evening.

27 At the time of the setting of the sun, Joshua gave the command, and they took them down from the trees, threw them into the cave where they had hidden, and placed large stones over the mouth of the cave, to this very day.

28 Joshua captured Makkedah that day and struck it with the edge of the sword; its king he devoted to destruction, them and every person in it — he left no survivor — and he did to the king of Makkedah as he had done to the king of Jericho.

29 Joshua crossed over, and all Israel with him, from Makkedah to Libnah, and fought against Libnah.

30 Yahweh gave it too, and its king, into the hand of Israel, and he struck it with the edge of the sword, and every person in it; he left no survivor in it, and he did to its king as he had done to the king of Jericho.

31 Joshua crossed over, and all Israel with him, from Libnah to Lachish, encamped against it, and fought against it.

32 Yahweh gave Lachish into the hand of Israel; he captured it on the second day and struck it with the edge of the sword, and every person in it, according to all that he had done to Libnah.

33 Then Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lachish, and Joshua struck him and his people until he had left him no survivor.

34 Joshua crossed over, and all Israel with him, from Lachish to Eglon; they encamped against it and fought against it.

35 They captured it that day and struck it with the edge of the sword, and every person in it he devoted to destruction that day, according to all that he had done to Lachish.

36 Joshua went up, and all Israel with him, from Eglon to Hebron, and they fought against it.

37 They captured it and struck it with the edge of the sword — its king, all its towns, and every person in it; he left no survivor, according to all that he had done to Eglon, and he devoted it to destruction, and every person in it.

38 Joshua turned back, and all Israel with him, to Debir, and fought against it.

39 He captured it, its king, and all its towns; they struck them with the edge of the sword and devoted to destruction every person in it; he left no survivor. As he had done to Hebron, so he did to Debir and its king, and as he had done to Libnah and its king.

40 Joshua struck the whole land — the hill country, the Negeb, the lowland, and the slopes — and all their kings; he left no survivor, and everything that breathed he devoted to destruction, as Yahweh, the God of Israel, had commanded.

41 Joshua struck them from Kadesh-barnea as far as Gaza, and the whole land of Goshen as far as Gibeon.

42 All these kings and their land Joshua captured at one time, because Yahweh, the God of Israel, fought for Israel.

43 Then Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, to the camp at Gilgal.

Joshua 11

1 When Jabin king of Hazor heard of it, he sent word to Jobab king of Madon, to the king of Shimron, and to the king of Achshaph,

2 and to the kings in the north, in the hill country and in the Arabah south of Chinneroth, in the lowland, and in the heights of Dor to the west,

3 to the Canaanite in the east and in the west, the Amorite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, and the Jebusite in the hill country, and the Hivite below Hermon in the land of Mizpah.

4 They came out, they and all their camps with them, a numerous people, like the sand on the seashore in multitude, with very many horses and chariots.

5 All these kings assembled, came, and encamped together at the waters of Merom, to fight against Israel.

6 Yahweh said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid before them, for tomorrow at this time I myself will give them all over, slain, before Israel; you shall hamstring their horses and burn their chariots with fire."

7 Joshua came suddenly against them at the waters of Merom, he and all the people of war with him, and fell upon them.

8 Yahweh gave them into the hand of Israel, and they struck them and pursued them as far as Great Sidon, as far as Misrephoth-maim, and as far as the valley of Mizpah to the east; they struck them until they had left them no survivor.

9 Joshua did to them as Yahweh had told him: he hamstrung their horses and burned their chariots with fire.

10 Joshua turned back at that time, captured Hazor, and struck its king with the sword, for Hazor had formerly been the head of all those kingdoms.

11 They struck every person in it with the edge of the sword, devoting them to destruction; nothing that breathed was left, and Hazor he burned with fire.

12 All the cities of those kings, and all their kings, Joshua captured, and he struck them with the edge of the sword and devoted them to destruction, as Moses the servant of Yahweh had commanded.

13 Only, Israel burned none of the cities that stood on their mounds, except Hazor alone, which Joshua burned.

14 All the spoil of these cities and the livestock the children of Israel took as plunder for themselves; but every human being they struck with the edge of the sword until they had destroyed them — they left nothing that breathed.

15 As Yahweh had commanded Moses his servant, so Moses commanded Joshua, and so Joshua did; he left out nothing of all that Yahweh had commanded Moses.

16 Joshua took all this land: the hill country, all the Negeb, all the land of Goshen, the lowland, the Arabah, the hill country of Israel, and its lowland,

17 from Mount Halak, which rises toward Seir, as far as Baal-gad in the valley of Lebanon below Mount Hermon; and all their kings he captured, struck down, and put to death.

18 For many days Joshua made war with all those kings.

19 There was no city that made peace with the children of Israel, except the Hivites, the inhabitants of Gibeon; they took everything in battle.

20 For it was from Yahweh to strengthen their hearts to meet Israel in battle, so that they might be devoted to destruction, with no favour shown to them, but so that they might be destroyed, as Yahweh had commanded Moses.

21 Joshua came at that time and cut off the Anakim from the hill country — from Hebron, from Debir, from Anab, and from all the hill country of Judah and all the hill country of Israel; with their cities Joshua devoted them to destruction.

22 No Anakim were left in the land of the children of Israel; only in Gaza, in Gath, and in Ashdod did some remain.

23 Joshua took the whole land, according to all that Yahweh had spoken to Moses, and Joshua gave it as an inheritance to Israel according to their divisions by their tribes, and the land rested from war.

Joshua 12

1 These are the kings of the land whom the children of Israel struck down and whose land they took possession of beyond the Jordan, toward the rising of the sun, from the Arnon valley as far as Mount Hermon, and all the Arabah to the east:

2 Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon and ruled from Aroer, which is on the bank of the Arnon valley, and from the middle of the valley, and half of Gilead, as far as the Jabbok valley, the border of the children of Ammon;

3 and the Arabah as far as the Sea of Chinneroth to the east, and as far as the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, to the east, by the way to Beth-jeshimoth, and to the south, below the slopes of Pisgah;

4 and the territory of Og king of Bashan, one of the remnant of the Rephaim, who lived at Ashtaroth and at Edrei,

5 and ruled over Mount Hermon, Salcah, and all Bashan, as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and half of Gilead, to the border of Sihon king of Heshbon.

6 Moses the servant of Yahweh and the children of Israel struck them down, and Moses the servant of Yahweh gave it as a possession to the Reubenites, to the Gadites, and to the half-tribe of Manasseh.

7 These are the kings of the land whom Joshua and the children of Israel struck down beyond the Jordan to the west, from Baal-gad in the valley of Lebanon as far as Mount Halak, which rises toward Seir; and Joshua gave it to the tribes of Israel as a possession according to their divisions,

8 in the hill country, in the lowland, in the Arabah, in the slopes, in the wilderness, and in the Negeb — the Hittite, the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite:

9 the king of Jericho, one; the king of Ai, which is beside Bethel, one;

10 the king of Jerusalem, one; the king of Hebron, one;

11 the king of Jarmuth, one; the king of Lachish, one;

12 the king of Eglon, one; the king of Gezer, one;

13 the king of Debir, one; the king of Geder, one;

14 the king of Hormah, one; the king of Arad, one;

15 the king of Libnah, one; the king of Adullam, one;

16 the king of Makkedah, one; the king of Bethel, one;

17 the king of Tappuah, one; the king of Hepher, one;

18 the king of Aphek, one; the king of Lassharon, one;

19 the king of Madon, one; the king of Hazor, one;

20 the king of Shimron-meron, one; the king of Achshaph, one;

21 the king of Taanach, one; the king of Megiddo, one;

22 the king of Kedesh, one; the king of Jokneam by Carmel, one;

23 the king of Dor, in the heights of Dor, one; the king of Goiim at Gilgal, one;

24 the king of Tirzah, one — all the kings, thirty-one.

Joshua 13

1 Joshua was old, advanced in years, and Yahweh said to him, "You are old, advanced in years, and a very great deal of land still remains to be taken in possession."

2 "This is the land that remains: all the districts of the Philistines, and all the Geshurites;

3 from the Shihor, which faces Egypt, as far north as the border of Ekron — it is reckoned as Canaanite — the five rulers of the Philistines: those of Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron; and the Avvim;

4 in the south, all the land of the Canaanites, and Mearah, which belongs to the Sidonians, as far as Aphek, up to the border of the Amorites;

5 and the land of the Gebalites, and all Lebanon toward the rising of the sun, from Baal Gad below Mount Hermon as far as the entrance to Hamath;

6 all who live in the hill country from Lebanon to Misrephoth Maim, all the Sidonians. I myself will drive them out before the children of Israel. Only allot this land to Israel as an inheritance, as I commanded you.

7 Now divide this land as an inheritance among the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh."

8 With him, the Reubenites and the Gadites had received their inheritance, which Moses gave them beyond the Jordan to the east, just as Moses, the servant of Yahweh, gave it to them:

9 from Aroer, which stands on the edge of the Arnon valley, and the city in the middle of the valley, and the whole plateau from Medeba to Dibon;

10 and all the cities of Sihon, king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, as far as the border of the children of Ammon;

11 and Gilead, and the territory of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and all Mount Hermon, and all Bashan as far as Salcah;

12 the whole kingdom of Og in Bashan, who reigned in Ashtaroth and in Edrei — he remained of what was left of the Rephaim — and Moses struck them down and drove them out.

13 But the children of Israel did not drive out the Geshurites or the Maacathites, and Geshur and Maacath have lived in the midst of Israel to this day.

14 Only to the tribe of Levi did he give no inheritance; the fire offerings of Yahweh, the God of Israel, are his inheritance, as he had spoken to him.

15 Moses gave to the tribe of the children of Reuben, according to their families.

16 Their border ran from Aroer, which stands on the edge of the Arnon valley, and the city in the middle of the valley, and the whole plateau beside Medeba;

17 Heshbon and all its cities on the plateau; Dibon, Bamoth Baal, and Beth Baal Meon;

18 Jahaz, Kedemoth, and Mephaath;

19 Kiriathaim, Sibmah, and Zereth Shahar on the mountain of the valley;

20 Beth Peor, the slopes of Pisgah, and Beth Jeshimoth;

21 all the cities of the plateau and the whole kingdom of Sihon, king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, whom Moses struck down, together with the chiefs of Midian — Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, the princes of Sihon, who lived in the land.

22 Balaam son of Beor, the diviner, the children of Israel also killed with the sword, among those they had slain.

23 And the border of the children of Reuben was the Jordan, as a border. This was the inheritance of the children of Reuben according to their families, the cities and their villages.

24 Moses gave to the tribe of Gad, to the children of Gad, according to their families.

25 Their border was Jazer, all the cities of Gilead, and half the land of the children of Ammon, as far as Aroer, which faces Rabbah;

26 and from Heshbon to Ramath Mizpeh and Betonim, and from Mahanaim to the border of Debir;

27 and in the valley, Beth Haram, Beth Nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon, the rest of the kingdom of Sihon, king of Heshbon, with the Jordan as its border, as far as the end of the Sea of Chinnereth beyond the Jordan to the east.

28 This is the inheritance of the children of Gad according to their families, the cities and their villages.

29 Moses gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh, and it belonged to the half-tribe of the children of Manasseh according to their families.

30 Their border ran from Mahanaim: all Bashan, the whole kingdom of Og, king of Bashan, and all the settlements of Jair in Bashan, sixty cities;

31 and half of Gilead, and Ashtaroth and Edrei, cities of Og's kingdom in Bashan, for the children of Machir son of Manasseh, for half of the children of Machir according to their families.

32 These are what Moses allotted as inheritances in the plains of Moab, beyond the Jordan at Jericho, to the east.

33 But to the tribe of Levi Moses gave no inheritance; Yahweh, the God of Israel, is their inheritance, as he had spoken to them.

Joshua 14

1 These are what the children of Israel inherited in the land of Canaan, which Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers of the tribes of the children of Israel gave them as their inheritance,

2 their inheritance by lot, as Yahweh had commanded through Moses, for the nine tribes and the half-tribe.

3 For Moses had given the inheritance of the two tribes and the half-tribe beyond the Jordan, but to the Levites he gave no inheritance among them.

4 For the children of Joseph were two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim, and no share in the land was given to the Levites, only cities to live in, with their pasture lands for their livestock and their property.

5 As Yahweh had commanded Moses, so the children of Israel did, and they divided the land.

6 Then the children of Judah came to Joshua at Gilgal, and Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said to him, "You know the word that Yahweh spoke to Moses, the man of God, about me and about you at Kadesh Barnea.

7 I was forty years old when Moses, the servant of Yahweh, sent me from Kadesh Barnea to spy out the land, and I brought back a report to him as it was in my heart.

8 My brothers who went up with me made the people's heart melt, but I followed Yahweh my God fully.

9 And Moses swore on that day, saying, 'The land on which your foot has trodden shall surely be yours as an inheritance, and your children's, forever, because you followed Yahweh my God fully.'

10 And now, see, Yahweh has kept me alive, as he spoke, these forty-five years, from the time Yahweh spoke this word to Moses, while Israel walked in the wilderness; and now, see, I am today eighty-five years old.

11 I am still as strong today as I was on the day Moses sent me; as my strength was then, so is my strength now, for battle, and for going out and coming in.

12 So now give me this hill country of which Yahweh spoke on that day, for you yourself heard on that day that Anakim are there, and great fortified cities. Perhaps Yahweh will be with me, and I will drive them out, as Yahweh spoke."

13 Joshua blessed him, and gave Hebron to Caleb son of Jephunneh as an inheritance.

14 Therefore Hebron became the inheritance of Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite to this day, because he followed Yahweh, the God of Israel, fully.

15 Now the name of Hebron before was Kiriath Arba; Arba was the greatest man among the Anakim. And the land rested from war.

Joshua 15

1 The lot for the tribe of the children of Judah, according to their families, reached to the border of Edom, to the wilderness of Zin in the Negev, at the far southern end.

2 Their southern border began at the end of the Salt Sea, at the bay that turns toward the south,

3 and it went out south of the ascent of Akrabbim, crossed to Zin, went up south of Kadesh Barnea, crossed to Hezron, went up to Addar, and turned toward Karka.

4 It crossed to Azmon, went out at the Brook of Egypt, and the border ended at the sea. This shall be your southern border.

5 The eastern border was the Salt Sea, as far as the end of the Jordan. And the border on the northern side ran from the bay of the sea at the end of the Jordan,

6 and the border went up to Beth Hoglah, crossed north of Beth Arabah, and went up to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben.

7 The border went up toward Debir from the Valley of Achor, and turned northward toward Gilgal, which faces the ascent of Adummim, south of the valley; then the border crossed to the waters of En Shemesh, and ended at En Rogel.

8 The border went up the Valley of Ben Hinnom to the southern slope of the Jebusite — that is, Jerusalem — and went up to the top of the mountain that faces the Valley of Hinnom to the west, at the northern end of the Valley of Rephaim.

9 The border curved from the top of the mountain to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah, went out to the cities of Mount Ephron, and curved to Baalah — that is, Kiriath Jearim.

10 The border turned from Baalah westward to Mount Seir, crossed to the northern slope of Mount Jearim — that is, Chesalon — went down to Beth Shemesh, and crossed to Timnah.

11 The border went out to the northern slope of Ekron, curved to Shikkeron, crossed Mount Baalah, went out at Jabneel, and the border ended at the sea.

12 For the western border, the Great Sea was the border. This is the border of the children of Judah all around, according to their families.

13 To Caleb son of Jephunneh he gave a share among the children of Judah, according to the commandment of Yahweh to Joshua: Kiriath Arba — Arba was the father of Anak — that is, Hebron.

14 Caleb drove out from there the three sons of Anak: Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai, the descendants of Anak.

15 From there he went up against the inhabitants of Debir; the name of Debir before was Kiriath Sepher.

16 Caleb said, "Whoever strikes Kiriath Sepher and takes it, to him I will give Achsah my daughter as wife."

17 Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's brother, took it, and he gave him Achsah his daughter as wife.

18 When she came, she urged him to ask her father for a field. She dismounted from the donkey, and Caleb said to her, "What do you want?"

19 She said, "Give me a blessing. Since you have set me in the land of the Negev, give me springs of water as well." And he gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.

20 This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Judah, according to their families.

21 The cities at the far end of the tribe of the children of Judah, toward the border of Edom in the Negev, were Kabzeel, Eder, and Jagur;

22 Kinah, Dimonah, and Adadah;

23 Kedesh, Hazor, and Ithnan;

24 Ziph, Telem, and Bealoth;

25 Hazor Hadattah, and Kerioth Hezron — that is, Hazor;

26 Amam, Shema, and Moladah;

27 Hazar Gaddah, Heshmon, and Beth Pelet;

28 Hazar Shual, Beersheba, and Biziothiah;

29 Baalah, Iim, and Ezem;

30 Eltolad, Chesil, and Hormah;

31 Ziklag, Madmannah, and Sansannah;

32 Lebaoth, Shilhim, Ain, and Rimmon — all the cities were twenty-nine, with their villages.

33 In the lowland: Eshtaol, Zorah, and Ashnah;

34 Zanoah, En Gannim, Tappuah, and Enam;

35 Jarmuth, Adullam, Socoh, and Azekah;

36 Shaaraim, Adithaim, Gederah, and Gederothaim — fourteen cities, with their villages.

37 Zenan, Hadashah, and Migdal Gad;

38 Dilean, Mizpeh, and Joktheel;

39 Lachish, Bozkath, and Eglon;

40 Cabbon, Lahmas, and Chitlish;

41 Gederoth, Beth Dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah — sixteen cities, with their villages.

42 Libnah, Ether, and Ashan;

43 Iphtah, Ashnah, and Nezib;

44 Keilah, Achzib, and Mareshah — nine cities, with their villages.

45 Ekron, with its towns and its villages;

46 from Ekron westward to the sea, all that lay beside Ashdod, with their villages;

47 Ashdod, its towns and its villages; Gaza, its towns and its villages, as far as the Brook of Egypt, and the Great Sea as its border.

48 And in the hill country: Shamir, Jattir, and Socoh;

49 Dannah, and Kiriath Sannah — that is, Debir;

50 Anab, Eshtemoh, and Anim;

51 Goshen, Holon, and Giloh — eleven cities, with their villages.

52 Arab, Rumah, and Eshan;

53 Janum, Beth Tappuah, and Aphekah;

54 Humtah, and Kiriath Arba — that is, Hebron — and Zior — nine cities, with their villages.

55 Maon, Carmel, Ziph, and Juttah;

56 Jezreel, Jokdeam, and Zanoah;

57 Kain, Gibeah, and Timnah — ten cities, with their villages.

58 Halhul, Beth Zur, and Gedor;

59 Maarath, Beth Anoth, and Eltekon — six cities, with their villages.

60 Kiriath Baal — that is, Kiriath Jearim — and Rabbah — two cities, with their villages.

61 In the wilderness: Beth Arabah, Middin, and Secacah;

62 Nibshan, the City of Salt, and En Gedi — six cities, with their villages.

63 As for the Jebusites, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the children of Judah could not drive them out, and the Jebusites have lived with the children of Judah in Jerusalem to this day.

Joshua 16

1 The lot came out for the children of Joseph from the Jordan at Jericho, at the waters of Jericho to the east, the wilderness going up from Jericho through the hill country to Bethel.

2 It went out from Bethel to Luz, and crossed to the border of the Archites at Ataroth.

3 It went down westward to the border of the Japhletites, as far as the border of Lower Beth Horon and on to Gezer, and it ended at the sea.

4 The children of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, received their inheritance.

5 The border of the children of Ephraim, according to their families, was this: the border of their inheritance on the east was Ataroth Addar, as far as Upper Beth Horon.

6 The border went out to the sea, with Michmethath on the north; then the border turned eastward to Taanath Shiloh, and crossed it on the east of Janoah.

7 It went down from Janoah to Ataroth and to Naarah, reached Jericho, and went out at the Jordan.

8 From Tappuah the border went westward to the Kanah valley, and it ended at the sea. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Ephraim, according to their families,

9 together with the cities set apart for the children of Ephraim in the midst of the inheritance of the children of Manasseh, all the cities with their villages.

10 They did not drive out the Canaanites who lived in Gezer, and the Canaanites have lived in the midst of Ephraim to this day, and have become forced labourers.

Joshua 17

1 This was the lot for the tribe of Manasseh, for he was Joseph's firstborn. Machir, Manasseh's firstborn and the father of Gilead, was a man of war, so Gilead and Bashan became his.

2 The rest of Manasseh's descendants received their share by their families: the descendants of Abiezer, the descendants of Helek, the descendants of Asriel, the descendants of Shechem, the descendants of Hepher, and the descendants of Shemida. These were the male descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, by their families.

3 Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, had no sons, only daughters. His daughters' names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

4 They came before Eleazar the priest, before Joshua son of Nun, and before the leaders, and said, "Yahweh commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brothers." So, at Yahweh's word, he gave them an inheritance among their father's brothers.

5 Ten portions fell to Manasseh, besides the land of Gilead and Bashan, which lies beyond the Jordan,

6 because Manasseh's daughters received an inheritance among his sons, while the land of Gilead belonged to the rest of Manasseh's descendants.

7 Manasseh's border ran from Asher to Michmethath, which faces Shechem. Then the border went southward to the inhabitants of En Tappuah.

8 The land of Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, but Tappuah itself, on Manasseh's border, belonged to the descendants of Ephraim.

9 The border went down to the Kanah Ravine, south of the ravine. These cities belonged to Ephraim, though they lay among Manasseh's cities. Manasseh's border was north of the ravine, and it ended at the sea.

10 The land to the south was Ephraim's and the land to the north was Manasseh's, and the sea was its border. It touched Asher on the north and Issachar on the east.

11 Within Issachar and Asher, Manasseh held Beth Shean and its villages, Ibleam and its villages, the inhabitants of Dor and its villages, the inhabitants of En Dor and its villages, the inhabitants of Taanach and its villages, and the inhabitants of Megiddo and its villages — the three heights.

12 But Manasseh's descendants could not drive out the inhabitants of those cities, and the Canaanites were determined to stay in that land.

13 When Israel grew strong, they put the Canaanites to forced labour, but they did not drive them out completely.

14 Joseph's descendants spoke to Joshua and said, "Why have you given me only one lot and one portion as an inheritance? We are a numerous people, for Yahweh has blessed us this far."

15 Joshua said to them, "If you are a numerous people, go up into the forest and clear ground for yourselves there, in the land of the Perizzites and the Rephaim, since the hill country of Ephraim is too narrow for you."

16 Joseph's descendants said, "The hill country is not enough for us, and all the Canaanites who live in the valley land have iron chariots, both those in Beth Shean and its villages and those in the Valley of Jezreel."

17 Joshua spoke to the house of Joseph, to Ephraim and to Manasseh, and said, "You are a numerous people and you have great strength. You shall not have only one lot,

18 for the hill country shall be yours. Though it is forest, you shall clear it, and its farthest reaches shall be yours, for you shall drive out the Canaanites, even though they have iron chariots and even though they are strong."

Joshua 18

1 The whole congregation of Israel assembled at Shiloh and set up the tent of meeting there, and the land lay subdued before them.

2 Seven tribes remained among Israel who had not yet received their inheritance divided to them.

3 Joshua said to Israel, "How long will you put off going in to take possession of the land that Yahweh, the God of your fathers, has given you?

4 Choose three men from each tribe, and I will send them out. They shall set out, go through the land, and write a description of it with a view to their inheritances, and then come back to me.

5 They shall divide it into seven portions. Judah shall stay within its border in the south, and the house of Joseph shall stay within its border in the north.

6 You shall write a description of the land in seven portions and bring it here to me, and I will cast lots for you here before Yahweh our God.

7 The Levites have no portion among you, for the priesthood of Yahweh is their inheritance. Gad, Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have already received their inheritance beyond the Jordan to the east, which Moses, Yahweh's servant, gave them."

8 The men rose and set out, and Joshua charged those who were going to write the description of the land, saying, "Go, walk through the land, write its description, and return to me, and here in Shiloh I will cast lots for you before Yahweh."

9 So the men went, passed through the land, and wrote its description by its cities in a book, in seven portions, and they came to Joshua at the camp at Shiloh.

10 Joshua cast lots for them at Shiloh before Yahweh, and there Joshua divided the land among Israel according to their divisions.

11 The lot came up for the tribe of Benjamin, by their families, and the territory of their lot lay between the descendants of Judah and the descendants of Joseph.

12 Their border on the north side began at the Jordan. The border went up to the slope of Jericho on the north, went up through the hill country westward, and ended at the wilderness of Beth Aven.

13 From there the border passed to Luz, to the southern slope of Luz — that is, Bethel. Then the border went down to Ataroth Addar, by the mountain that lies south of Lower Beth Horon.

14 The border curved and turned on the west side southward, from the mountain that faces Beth Horon to the south, and it ended at Kiriath Baal — that is, Kiriath Jearim — a city of Judah's descendants. This was the west side.

15 The south side began at the edge of Kiriath Jearim. The border went out westward and came out at the spring of the waters of Nephtoah.

16 The border went down to the foot of the mountain that faces the Valley of Ben Hinnom, which is at the north end of the Valley of Rephaim. It went down the Valley of Hinnom to the southern slope of the Jebusite, and went down to En Rogel.

17 It curved northward, came out at En Shemesh, and came out at Geliloth, which is opposite the Ascent of Adummim. Then it went down to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben.

18 It passed along to the slope opposite the Arabah, northward, and went down into the Arabah.

19 The border passed along to the northern slope of Beth Hoglah, and the border ended at the northern bay of the Salt Sea, at the southern end of the Jordan. This was the south border.

20 The Jordan bounded it on the east side. This was the inheritance of Benjamin's descendants, with its borders all around, by their families.

21 The cities of the tribe of Benjamin, by their families, were Jericho, Beth Hoglah, and Emek Keziz,

22 Beth Arabah, Zemaraim, and Bethel,

23 Avvim, Parah, and Ophrah,

24 Chephar Ammoni, Ophni, and Geba — twelve cities with their villages.

25 Gibeon, Ramah, and Beeroth,

26 Mizpeh, Chephirah, and Mozah,

27 Rekem, Irpeel, and Taralah,

28 Zela, Eleph, and the Jebusite city — that is, Jerusalem — Gibeah, and Kiriath — fourteen cities with their villages. This was the inheritance of Benjamin's descendants, by their families.

Joshua 19

1 The second lot came out for Simeon, for the tribe of Simeon's descendants, by their families, and their inheritance lay within the inheritance of Judah's descendants.

2 In their inheritance they had Beersheba, Sheba, and Moladah,

3 Hazar Shual, Balah, and Ezem,

4 Eltolad, Bethul, and Hormah,

5 Ziklag, Beth Marcaboth, and Hazar Susah,

6 Beth Lebaoth, and Sharuhen — thirteen cities with their villages.

7 Ain, Rimmon, Ether, and Ashan — four cities with their villages,
