18 The king answered and said to the woman, "Please do not hide from me the thing I am about to ask you." The woman said, "Let my lord the king speak."

19 The king said, "Is the hand of Joab with you in all this?" The woman answered and said, "As your soul lives, my lord the king, no one can turn to the right or to the left from anything my lord the king has spoken. Your servant Joab commanded me, and he put all these words in the mouth of your servant.

20 Your servant Joab did this thing to change the face of the matter. My lord is wise, with the wisdom of an angel of God, knowing everything that is on the earth."

21 The king said to Joab, "See, I have done this thing. Go and bring back the young man Absalom."

22 Joab fell on his face to the ground, bowed down, and blessed the king. Joab said, "Today your servant knows that I have found favor in your eyes, my lord the king, because the king has done what his servant asked."

23 Joab rose, went to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.

24 The king said, "Let him turn aside to his own house, and let him not see my face." So Absalom turned aside to his own house and did not see the king's face.

25 In all Israel there was no man praised for beauty like Absalom; from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him.

26 When he cut the hair of his head — it was at the end of every year that he cut it, because it was heavy on him, so he cut it — he weighed the hair of his head at two hundred shekels by the king's weight.

27 Three sons were born to Absalom, and one daughter, whose name was Tamar; she was a woman beautiful in appearance.

28 Absalom lived in Jerusalem two full years and did not see the king's face.

29 Absalom sent for Joab, to send him to the king, but he would not come to him. He sent again a second time, but he would not come.

30 He said to his servants, "See, Joab's plot is beside mine, and he has barley there. Go and set it on fire." Absalom's servants set the plot on fire.

31 Joab rose and came to Absalom's house, and said to him, "Why have your servants set my plot on fire?"

32 Absalom said to Joab, "See, I sent to you, saying, 'Come here, so that I may send you to the king, to say, "Why have I come from Geshur? It would be better for me still to be there." Now let me see the king's face, and if there is guilt in me, let him put me to death.'"

33 Joab came to the king and told him. He called Absalom, and he came to the king and bowed on his face to the ground before the king, and the king kissed Absalom.

2 Samuel 15

1 After this, Absalom made himself a chariot and horses, and fifty men to run before him.

2 Absalom would rise early and stand beside the road at the gate. Whenever a man who had a dispute came to the king for judgment, Absalom would call to him and say, "From which city are you?" He would say, "Your servant is from one of the tribes of Israel."

3 Absalom would say to him, "See, your claims are good and right, but there is no one from the king to hear you."

4 Absalom would say, "If only I were made judge in the land, so that everyone who has a dispute or a case might come to me, and I would give him justice!"

5 When a man came near to bow down to him, he would stretch out his hand, take hold of him, and kiss him.

6 Absalom did this to all Israel who came to the king for judgment, and Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.

7 At the end of forty years, Absalom said to the king, "Please let me go and pay my vow in Hebron, which I vowed to Yahweh.

8 For your servant vowed a vow while I lived at Geshur in Aram, saying, 'If Yahweh truly brings me back to Jerusalem, then I will serve Yahweh.'"

9 The king said to him, "Go in peace." He rose and went to Hebron.

10 Absalom sent agents through all the tribes of Israel, saying, "As soon as you hear the sound of the horn, say, 'Absalom is king in Hebron.'"

11 Two hundred men from Jerusalem went with Absalom; they were invited and went in their innocence, knowing nothing of the matter.

12 Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David's counselor, from his city, from Giloh, while he was offering the sacrifices. The conspiracy grew strong, and the people with Absalom kept increasing.

13 A messenger came to David, saying, "The hearts of the men of Israel are after Absalom."

14 David said to all his servants who were with him in Jerusalem, "Rise, let us flee, or none of us will escape from Absalom. Hurry to go, or he will quickly overtake us, bring disaster down on us, and strike the city with the edge of the sword."

15 The king's servants said to the king, "See, your servants are ready for whatever my lord the king chooses."

16 The king went out, and all his household after him, on foot. The king left ten women, concubines, to keep the house.

17 The king went out, and all the people after him, on foot, and they stopped at the farthest house.

18 All his servants passed by at his side, and all the Cherethites and all the Pelethites, and all the Gittites, six hundred men who had followed him from Gath, passed on before the king.

19 The king said to Ittai the Gittite, "Why do you also go with us? Return and stay with the king, for you are a foreigner and also an exile from your own place.

20 You came only yesterday; should I today make you wander with us, when I go wherever I go? Return, and take your brothers back with you. May loyal love and truth be with you."

21 Ittai answered the king and said, "As Yahweh lives, and as my lord the king lives, in the place where my lord the king is — whether for death or for life — there your servant will be."

22 David said to Ittai, "Go and pass on." Ittai the Gittite passed on, and all his men, and all the little ones who were with him.

23 The whole land wept with a loud voice as all the people passed on. The king crossed the Kidron valley, and all the people crossed on toward the road to the wilderness.

24 And there was Zadok also, and all the Levites with him, carrying the ark of the covenant of God. They set down the ark of God, and Abiathar went up, until all the people had finished passing out of the city.

25 The king said to Zadok, "Carry the ark of God back into the city. If I find favor in the eyes of Yahweh, he will bring me back and let me see it and its dwelling place.

26 But if he says, 'I have no pleasure in you,' here I am; let him do to me what is good in his eyes."

27 The king said to Zadok the priest, "Are you not a seer? Return to the city in peace, and your two sons with you, Ahimaaz your son and Jonathan the son of Abiathar.

28 See, I will wait at the fords of the wilderness until word comes from you to tell me."

29 Zadok and Abiathar carried the ark of God back to Jerusalem, and they stayed there.

30 David went up the ascent of the Mount of Olives, weeping as he went up, his head covered, and he went barefoot. All the people who were with him each covered his head, and they went up, weeping as they went up.

31 David was told, "Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom." David said, "Yahweh, please make the counsel of Ahithophel foolishness."

32 When David came to the summit, where one worships God, there was Hushai the Archite coming to meet him, his tunic torn and earth on his head.

33 David said to him, "If you pass on with me, you will be a burden to me.

34 But if you return to the city and say to Absalom, 'I will be your servant, O king; I was your father's servant in the past, and now I am your servant,' then you can frustrate the counsel of Ahithophel for me.

35 Are not Zadok and Abiathar the priests there with you? Whatever you hear from the king's house, tell it to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.

36 See, their two sons are there with them, Ahimaaz for Zadok and Jonathan for Abiathar; by them you shall send to me everything you hear."

37 Hushai, David's friend, came into the city, and Absalom came into Jerusalem.

2 Samuel 16

1 When David had passed a little beyond the summit, there was Ziba, the servant of Mephibosheth, coming to meet him, with a pair of saddled donkeys, and on them two hundred loaves of bread, a hundred clusters of raisins, a hundred summer fruits, and a skin of wine.

2 The king said to Ziba, "What are these for you?" Ziba said, "The donkeys are for the king's household to ride on; the bread and the summer fruit are for the young men to eat; and the wine is for the one who is faint in the wilderness to drink."

3 The king said, "Where is your lord's son?" Ziba said to the king, "See, he is staying in Jerusalem, for he said, 'Today the house of Israel will restore to me my father's kingdom.'"

4 The king said to Ziba, "See, everything that belongs to Mephibosheth is yours." Ziba said, "I bow down; let me find favor in your eyes, my lord the king."

5 King David came to Bahurim, and there a man came out from there, from the family of the house of Saul, whose name was Shimei the son of Gera; he came out, cursing as he came.

6 He threw stones at David and at all the servants of King David, while all the people and all the mighty men were at his right and at his left.

7 Shimei said this as he cursed: "Get out, get out, you man of blood, you worthless man!

8 Yahweh has brought back on you all the blood of the house of Saul, in whose place you have reigned, and Yahweh has given the kingdom into the hand of Absalom your son. And here you are in your ruin, for you are a man of blood."

9 Abishai the son of Zeruiah said to the king, "Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Let me go over, please, and take off his head."

10 The king said, "What have I to do with you, sons of Zeruiah? Let him curse, for Yahweh has said to him, 'Curse David.' Who then can say, 'Why have you done so?'"

11 David said to Abishai and to all his servants, "See, my son, who came from my own body, seeks my life; how much more now this Benjaminite? Leave him alone and let him curse, for Yahweh has told him to.

12 Perhaps Yahweh will look on my affliction, and Yahweh will repay me good in place of his cursing me today."

13 David and his men went on by the road, while Shimei went along on the side of the hill opposite him, cursing as he went, throwing stones opposite him and throwing dust.

14 The king and all the people who were with him came weary, and he refreshed himself there.

15 Absalom and all the people, the men of Israel, came to Jerusalem, and Ahithophel with him.

16 When Hushai the Archite, David's friend, came to Absalom, Hushai said to Absalom, "Long live the king! Long live the king!"

17 Absalom said to Hushai, "Is this your loyal love toward your friend? Why did you not go with your friend?"

18 Hushai said to Absalom, "No — the one whom Yahweh and this people and all the men of Israel have chosen, I will be his, and with him I will stay.

19 And second, whom should I serve? Is it not before his son? As I served before your father, so I will be before you."

20 Absalom said to Ahithophel, "Give your counsel: what shall we do?"

21 Ahithophel said to Absalom, "Go in to your father's concubines, whom he left to keep the house, and all Israel will hear that you have made yourself odious to your father, and the hands of all who are with you will be strengthened."

22 They pitched a tent for Absalom on the roof, and Absalom went in to his father's concubines in the sight of all Israel.

23 The counsel of Ahithophel, which he counseled in those days, was as if a man inquired of the word of God; so was all the counsel of Ahithophel regarded, both by David and by Absalom.

2 Samuel 17

1 Ahithophel said to Absalom, "Let me choose twelve thousand men, and I will rise and pursue David tonight.

2 I will come upon him while he is weary and his hands hang slack, and I will throw him into panic; all the people with him will flee, and I will strike down the king alone.

3 Then I will bring all the people back to you. When the man you are seeking is gone, as if all had returned, all the people will be at peace."

4 The plan seemed right in the eyes of Absalom and in the eyes of all the elders of Israel.

5 But Absalom said, "Call Hushai the Archite as well, and let us hear what he too has to say."

6 When Hushai came to Absalom, Absalom said to him, "Ahithophel has spoken in this way. Should we do as he says? If not, you speak."

7 Hushai said to Absalom, "The counsel Ahithophel has given this time is not good."

8 Hushai went on, "You know your father and his men: they are mighty warriors, and they are embittered in spirit, like a bear robbed of her cubs in the field. Your father is a man of war, and he will not spend the night with the people.

9 Even now he is hidden in one of the pits or in some other place. And if some of our men fall at the first onset, whoever hears of it will say, 'There has been a slaughter among the people who follow Absalom.'

10 Then even the valiant man whose heart is like the heart of a lion will melt away completely, for all Israel knows that your father is a mighty warrior and that those with him are valiant men.

11 My counsel is this: let all Israel be gathered to you, from Dan to Beersheba, as many as the sand by the sea, and go into battle yourself in person.

12 We will come upon him in whatever place he is found, and we will settle on him as the dew falls on the ground; and not one man will be left of him or of all the men who are with him.

13 If he withdraws into a city, all Israel will bring ropes to that city, and we will drag it down into the valley until not even a small stone is found there."

14 Absalom and all the men of Israel said, "The counsel of Hushai the Archite is better than the counsel of Ahithophel." For Yahweh had commanded that the good counsel of Ahithophel be frustrated, so that Yahweh might bring disaster on Absalom.

15 Then Hushai said to Zadok and Abiathar the priests, "Ahithophel counseled Absalom and the elders of Israel in this way and that, and I have counseled in this way and that.

16 Now send quickly and tell David, 'Do not spend tonight at the fords of the wilderness, but cross over by all means, or the king and all the people with him will be swallowed up.'"

17 Jonathan and Ahimaaz were waiting at En-rogel, and a servant girl would go and tell them, and they would go and tell King David, for they could not risk being seen entering the city.

18 But a boy saw them and told Absalom. The two of them hurried away and came to the house of a man in Bahurim who had a well in his courtyard, and they went down into it.

19 The man's wife took a covering, spread it over the mouth of the well, and scattered crushed grain on it, and nothing was known of the matter.

20 Absalom's servants came to the woman at the house and said, "Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?" The woman said to them, "They have crossed over the stream of water." They searched and did not find them, and returned to Jerusalem.

21 After they had gone, the two came up out of the well, went and told King David, and said to David, "Rise and cross the water quickly, for Ahithophel has counseled against you in this way."

22 David rose, and all the people with him, and they crossed the Jordan. By morning light there was not one left who had not crossed the Jordan.

23 When Ahithophel saw that his counsel had not been carried out, he saddled the donkey, rose, and went home to his own city. He set his household in order, hanged himself, and died, and was buried in his father's tomb.

24 David came to Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan, he and all the men of Israel with him.

25 Absalom had set Amasa over the army in place of Joab. Amasa was the son of a man named Ithra the Israelite, who had gone in to Abigail daughter of Nahash, the sister of Zeruiah, Joab's mother.

26 Israel and Absalom camped in the land of Gilead.

27 When David came to Mahanaim, Shobi son of Nahash from Rabbah of the Ammonites, Machir son of Ammiel from Lo-debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite from Rogelim

28 brought beds, basins, earthenware vessels, wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils, and more roasted grain,

29 and honey, curds, sheep, and cheese from the herd, for David and the people with him to eat, for they said, "The people are hungry, weary, and thirsty in the wilderness."

2 Samuel 18

1 David mustered the people who were with him and set commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds over them.

2 David sent the people out, a third under Joab, a third under Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother, and a third under Ittai the Gittite. The king said to the people, "I myself will surely go out with you as well."

3 But the people said, "You must not go out. If we flee, they will pay no attention to us, and if half of us die, they will pay no attention to us; but you are worth ten thousand of us. So it is better that you be ready to help us from the city."

4 The king said to them, "I will do whatever seems best in your eyes." The king stood beside the gate, and all the people went out by hundreds and by thousands.

5 The king commanded Joab, Abishai, and Ittai, saying, "Deal gently, for my sake, with the young man Absalom." All the people heard the king command all the commanders concerning Absalom.

6 The people went out into the field against Israel, and the battle took place in the forest of Ephraim.

7 The people of Israel were defeated there before David's servants, and the slaughter there that day was great, twenty thousand men.

8 The battle spread over the face of the whole country, and the forest devoured more people that day than the sword devoured.

9 Absalom happened to meet David's servants. Absalom was riding on the mule, and the mule went under the thick branches of a great oak. His head caught fast in the oak, and he was left hanging between heaven and earth, while the mule under him went on.

10 A man saw it and told Joab, saying, "Look, I saw Absalom hanging in an oak."

11 Joab said to the man who told him, "Look, you saw him! Why did you not strike him to the ground there? It would have been my part to give you ten pieces of silver and a belt."

12 The man said to Joab, "Even if I were weighing a thousand pieces of silver into my own hands, I would not stretch out my hand against the king's son, for in our hearing the king commanded you, Abishai, and Ittai, saying, 'Let whoever will, take care of the young man Absalom.'

13 If I had acted treacherously against my own life — and nothing is hidden from the king — you yourself would have stood aloof.

14 Joab said, "I will not wait like this before you." He took three spears in his hand and thrust them into Absalom's heart while he was still alive in the middle of the oak.

15 Ten young men who carried Joab's armor surrounded Absalom, struck him, and killed him.

16 Joab blew the trumpet, and the people returned from pursuing Israel, for Joab held the people back.

17 They took Absalom, threw him into a great pit in the forest, and raised a very great heap of stones over him. All Israel fled, each man to his tent.

18 In his lifetime Absalom had taken the pillar that stands in the King's Valley and set it up for himself, for he said, "I have no son to keep my name in remembrance." He called the pillar by his own name, and it is called Absalom's Monument to this day.

19 Ahimaaz son of Zadok said, "Let me run and bring the king news, because Yahweh has delivered judgment for him against his enemies."

20 Joab said to him, "You will not be a bearer of news today; you may bear news another day, but today you will bear no news, because the king's son is dead."

21 Joab said to the Cushite, "Go, tell the king what you have seen." The Cushite bowed to Joab and ran.

22 Ahimaaz son of Zadok said again to Joab, "Come what may, let me also run after the Cushite." Joab said, "Why do you want to run, my son, when you will have no reward for the news?"

23 "Come what may, I will run," he said. He said to him, "Run." Ahimaaz ran by the way of the plain and passed the Cushite.

24 David was sitting between the two gates. The watchman went up to the roof of the gate, to the wall, lifted his eyes, and looked, and there was a man running alone.

25 The watchman called out and told the king. The king said, "If he is alone, there is news in his mouth." He kept coming closer and closer.

26 The watchman saw another man running, and the watchman called to the gatekeeper and said, "Look, a man running alone." The king said, "He too brings news."

27 The watchman said, "I see that the running of the first is like the running of Ahimaaz son of Zadok." The king said, "He is a good man, and he comes with good news."

28 Ahimaaz called out and said to the king, "Peace!" He bowed before the king with his face to the ground and said, "Blessed be Yahweh your God, who has handed over the men who raised their hand against my lord the king."

29 The king said, "Is it well with the young man Absalom?" Ahimaaz answered, "When Joab sent the king's servant — your servant — I saw a great tumult, but I did not know what it was."

30 The king said, "Turn aside and stand here." He turned aside and stood still.

31 Then the Cushite came, and the Cushite said, "Let my lord the king receive the news: Yahweh has delivered judgment for you today against all who rose up against you."

32 The king said to the Cushite, "Is it well with the young man Absalom?" The Cushite answered, "May the enemies of my lord the king, and all who rise against you for harm, be as that young man is."

2 Samuel 19

1 The king was shaken. He went up to the chamber over the gate and wept, and as he went he said, "My son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! Would that I had died instead of you, Absalom my son, my son!"

2 It was told to Joab, "Look, the king is weeping and mourning for Absalom."

3 The victory that day turned into mourning for all the people, for the people heard it said that day, "The king is grieved over his son."

4 The people stole into the city that day, as people who are ashamed steal away when they flee in battle.

5 The king had covered his face, and the king cried out with a loud voice, "My son Absalom! Absalom, my son, my son!"

6 Joab came to the king in the house and said, "Today you have shamed the faces of all your servants, who today saved your life and the lives of your sons and daughters, the lives of your wives and the lives of your concubines,

7 by loving those who hate you and hating those who love you. For today you have made clear that commanders and servants are nothing to you. Today I know that if Absalom were alive and all of us were dead today, then it would be right in your eyes.

8 Now rise, go out, and speak to the heart of your servants, for I swear by Yahweh: if you do not go out, not a man will stay with you tonight, and this will be worse for you than all the harm that has come on you from your youth until now."

9 The king rose and sat in the gate. All the people were told, "Look, the king is sitting in the gate," and all the people came before the king. Israel had fled, each man to his tent.

10 All the people were disputing throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, "The king rescued us from the hand of our enemies and delivered us from the hand of the Philistines, and now he has fled from the land because of Absalom.

11 Absalom, whom we anointed over us, has died in battle. Now why do you say nothing about bringing the king back?"

12 King David sent word to Zadok and Abiathar the priests, saying, "Speak to the elders of Judah, saying, 'Why should you be the last to bring the king back to his house, when the word of all Israel has come to the king, to his house?

13 You are my brothers; you are my bone and my flesh. Why should you be the last to bring back the king?'

14 And say to Amasa, 'Are you not my bone and my flesh? So may God do to me, and more besides, if you are not commander of the army before me all your days in place of Joab.'"

15 He turned the heart of all the men of Judah as one man, and they sent to the king, "Return, you and all your servants."

16 The king returned and came to the Jordan. Judah came to Gilgal to go and meet the king and bring the king across the Jordan.

17 Shimei son of Gera, the Benjaminite from Bahurim, hurried and came down with the men of Judah to meet King David.

18 A thousand men of Benjamin were with him, and Ziba, the servant of the house of Saul, with his fifteen sons and his twenty servants. They rushed through the Jordan before the king.

19 The ferry crossed back and forth to bring the king's household over and to do what was good in his eyes. Shimei son of Gera fell down before the king as he was about to cross the Jordan

20 and said to the king, "Let my lord not hold guilt against me, and do not remember how your servant acted wrongly on the day my lord the king went out of Jerusalem, so that the king takes it to heart.

21 For your servant knows that I have sinned, and look, I have come today, the first of all the house of Joseph, to come down and meet my lord the king."

22 Abishai son of Zeruiah answered and said, "Should Shimei not be put to death for this, because he cursed Yahweh's anointed?"

23 David said, "What have I to do with you, sons of Zeruiah, that you should be an adversary to me today? Should any man be put to death in Israel today? Do I not know that today I am king over Israel?"

24 The king said to Shimei, "You will not die." And the king swore to him.

25 Mephibosheth son of Saul came down to meet the king. He had not cared for his feet, trimmed his mustache, or washed his clothes from the day the king departed until the day he came home in peace.

26 When he came to Jerusalem to meet the king, the king said to him, "Why did you not go with me, Mephibosheth?"

27 He answered, "My lord the king, my servant deceived me. Your servant said, 'Let me saddle the donkey so I may ride on it and go with the king,' for your servant is lame.

28 He slandered your servant to my lord the king. But my lord the king is like an angel of God; do what is good in your eyes.

29 For all my father's house were nothing but men deserving death before my lord the king, yet you set your servant among those who eat at your table. What right do I still have, that I should cry out any more to the king?"

30 The king said to him, "Why do you speak of your matters any more? I say: you and Ziba shall divide the field."

31 Mephibosheth said to the king, "Let him take it all, since my lord the king has come home in peace."

32 Barzillai the Gileadite came down from Rogelim and crossed the Jordan with the king, to send him on his way at the Jordan.

33 Barzillai was very old, eighty years old. He had provided for the king during his stay at Mahanaim, for he was a very great man.

34 The king said to Barzillai, "Cross over with me, and I will provide for you with me in Jerusalem."

35 Barzillai said to the king, "How many are the days of the years of my life, that I should go up with the king to Jerusalem?

36 I am eighty years old today. Can I discern between good and bad? Can your servant taste what I eat and what I drink? Can I still hear the voice of singing men and singing women? Why should your servant be a further burden to my lord the king?

37 Your servant will cross the Jordan with the king only a little way. Why should the king repay me with such a reward?

38 Let your servant turn back, please, and die in my own city, beside the grave of my father and my mother. But here is your servant Chimham; let him cross over with my lord the king, and do for him what is good in your eyes."

39 The king said, "Chimham shall cross over with me, and I will do for him what is good in your eyes, and whatever you choose for me to do, I will do for you."

40 All the people crossed the Jordan, and the king crossed. The king kissed Barzillai and blessed him, and he returned to his own place.

41 The king crossed over to Gilgal, and Chimham crossed over with him. All the people of Judah brought the king across, and also half the people of Israel.

42 Then all the men of Israel came to the king and said to the king, "Why have our brothers, the men of Judah, stolen you away and brought the king and his household across the Jordan, and all David's men with him?"

43 All the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, "Because the king is close kin to us. Why are you angry over this matter? Have we eaten anything at the king's expense? Has any gift been taken for us?"

44 The men of Israel answered the men of Judah and said, "I have ten shares in the king, and in David too I have more than you. Why did you slight me, so that my word was not first in bringing back my king?" The words of the men of Judah were harsher than the words of the men of Israel.

2 Samuel 20

1 There happened to be there a worthless man named Sheba son of Bichri, a Benjaminite. He blew the trumpet and said, "We have no portion in David, and no inheritance in the son of Jesse. Each man to his tents, Israel!"

2 All the men of Israel went up from following David and followed Sheba son of Bichri, but the men of Judah clung to their king from the Jordan to Jerusalem.

3 David came to his house in Jerusalem. The king took the ten concubines he had left to keep the house, put them in a house under guard, and provided for them, but he did not go in to them. They were shut up until the day of their death, living as widows.

4 The king said to Amasa, "Summon the men of Judah to me within three days, and you be present here."

5 Amasa went to summon Judah, but he delayed beyond the appointed time set for him.

6 David said to Abishai, "Now Sheba son of Bichri will do us more harm than Absalom. Take your lord's servants and pursue him, or he may find fortified cities for himself and slip from our sight."

7 Joab's men went out after him, with the Cherethites, the Pelethites, and all the mighty men. They went out from Jerusalem to pursue Sheba son of Bichri.

8 They were at the great stone in Gibeon when Amasa came to meet them. Joab was wearing his military garment, and over it a belt with a sword fastened at his waist in its sheath; as he stepped forward, it fell out.

9 Joab said to Amasa, "Is it well with you, my brother?" Joab took hold of Amasa's beard with his right hand to kiss him.

10 Amasa paid no attention to the sword in Joab's hand. Joab struck him with it in the belly, spilled his entrails to the ground, and did not strike him a second time, and he died. Joab and Abishai his brother pursued Sheba son of Bichri.

11 One of Joab's young men stood over him and said, "Whoever favors Joab, and whoever is for David, follow Joab."

12 Amasa lay wallowing in his blood in the middle of the highway. When the man saw that all the people were stopping, he moved Amasa from the highway into the field and threw a garment over him, because he saw that everyone who came to him stopped.

13 When he had been removed from the highway, every man went on after Joab to pursue Sheba son of Bichri.

14 Sheba passed through all the tribes of Israel to Abel of Beth-maacah, and all the Bichrites gathered and also went in after him.

15 They came and besieged him in Abel of Beth-maacah. They threw up a siege mound against the city, and it stood against the outer rampart, and all the people with Joab were battering the wall to bring it down.

16 A wise woman called out from the city, "Listen! Listen! Tell Joab, please, 'Come near here, so I can speak with you.'"

17 He came near to her, and the woman said, "Are you Joab?" He answered, "I am." She said to him, "Hear the words of your servant." He answered, "I am listening."

18 She spoke, saying, "In former times they used to say, 'Let them ask counsel at Abel,' and so they settled the matter.

19 I am one of the peaceable and faithful in Israel. You are seeking to destroy a city that is a mother in Israel. Why will you swallow up Yahweh's inheritance?"

20 Joab answered and said, "Far be it, far be it from me that I should swallow up or destroy.

21 That is not the matter. A man from the hill country of Ephraim, Sheba son of Bichri by name, has raised his hand against the king, against David. Hand him over alone, and I will withdraw from the city." The woman said to Joab, "Look, his head will be thrown to you over the wall."

22 The woman went to all the people in her wisdom, and they cut off the head of Sheba son of Bichri and threw it out to Joab. He blew the trumpet, and they dispersed from the city, each man to his tent. Joab returned to Jerusalem, to the king.

23 Joab was over all the army of Israel. Benaiah son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites.

24 Adoram was over the forced labor, and Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was the recorder.

25 Sheva was scribe, and Zadok and Abiathar were priests.

26 Ira the Jairite was also a priest to David.

2 Samuel 21

1 There was a famine in the days of David for three years, year after year, and David sought the face of Yahweh. And Yahweh said, "It is because of Saul and his house of blood, because he put the Gibeonites to death."

2 The king called the Gibeonites and said to them — now the Gibeonites were not of the children of Israel but of the remnant of the Amorites, and the children of Israel had sworn to them, and Saul had sought to strike them down in his zeal for the children of Israel and Judah —

3 and David said to the Gibeonites, "What shall I do for you? And with what shall I make atonement, so that you may bless the inheritance of Yahweh?"

4 The Gibeonites said to him, "It is no matter of silver or gold between us and Saul or his house, and it is not for us to put any man to death in Israel." And he said, "What do you say I should do for you?"

5 They said to the king, "The man who consumed us and who plotted against us — we have been destroyed, so that we cannot stand anywhere in all the territory of Israel;

6 let seven men from among his sons be given to us, and we will hang them before Yahweh in Gibeah of Saul, the chosen of Yahweh." And the king said, "I will give them."

7 But the king spared Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan the son of Saul, because of the oath of Yahweh that was between them, between David and Jonathan the son of Saul.

8 The king took the two sons of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, whom she bore to Saul, Armoni and Mephibosheth, and the five sons of Michal the daughter of Saul, whom she bore to Adriel the son of Barzillai the Meholathite.

9 He gave them into the hand of the Gibeonites, and they hanged them on the mountain before Yahweh, and all seven of them fell together. They were put to death in the days of harvest, in the first days, at the beginning of the barley harvest.

10 Rizpah the daughter of Aiah took sackcloth and spread it for herself on the rock, from the beginning of harvest until water poured down on them from the heavens, and she did not let the birds of the heavens rest on them by day, nor the beasts of the field by night.

11 David was told what Rizpah the daughter of Aiah, the concubine of Saul, had done.

12 David went and took the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son from the men of Jabesh-gilead, who had stolen them from the square of Beth-shan, where the Philistines had hanged them there, on the day the Philistines struck down Saul at Gilboa.

13 He brought up from there the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son, and they gathered the bones of those who had been hanged.

14 They buried the bones of Saul and Jonathan his son in the land of Benjamin at Zela, in the tomb of Kish his father, and they did all that the king commanded. After that, God answered prayer for the land.

15 There was war again between the Philistines and Israel, and David went down, and his servants with him, and they fought the Philistines, and David grew faint.

16 Ishbi-benob, who was among the descendants of the giant — the weight of his spear was three hundred shekels of bronze, and he was girded with a new weapon — intended to strike down David.

17 But Abishai the son of Zeruiah helped him, and struck the Philistine and killed him. Then David's men swore to him, saying, "You shall not go out with us to battle anymore, so that you do not quench the lamp of Israel."

18 After this there was war again with the Philistines at Gob, and Sibbecai the Hushathite struck down Saph, who was among the descendants of the giant.

19 There was war again with the Philistines at Gob, and Elhanan the son of Jaare-oregim the Bethlehemite struck down Goliath the Gittite, whose spear shaft was like a weaver's beam.

20 There was war again at Gath, and there was a man of great stature who had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot, twenty-four in number, and he too was descended from the giant.

21 He defied Israel, and Jonathan the son of Shimeah, David's brother, struck him down.

22 These four were descended from the giant in Gath, and they fell by the hand of David and by the hand of his servants.

2 Samuel 22

1 David spoke to Yahweh the words of this song on the day when Yahweh delivered him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul,

2 and he said: Yahweh is my rock, my fortress, and my deliverer;

3 God is my rock — in him I take refuge — my shield and the horn of my salvation, my stronghold and my refuge, my savior; you save me from violence.

4 I call on Yahweh, who is worthy of praise, and I am saved from my enemies.

5 For the breakers of death surrounded me; the torrents of destruction terrified me.

6 The cords of Sheol surrounded me; the snares of death confronted me.

7 In my distress I called on Yahweh, and I called to my God. He heard my voice from his temple, and my cry for help came into his ears.

8 Then the earth shook and trembled; the foundations of the heavens quaked and shook, because he was angry.

9 Smoke went up from his nostrils, and fire from his mouth devoured; coals blazed from him.

10 He bowed the heavens and came down, and thick darkness was under his feet.

11 He rode on a cherub and flew; he was seen on the wings of the wind.

12 He made darkness shelters around him, a gathering of waters, thick clouds of the skies.

13 From the brightness before him, coals of fire blazed.

14 Yahweh thundered from heaven, and the Most High gave his voice.

15 He sent out arrows and scattered them, lightning, and routed them.

16 The channels of the sea appeared, and the foundations of the world were laid bare at the rebuke of Yahweh, at the blast of the breath of his nostrils.

17 He sent from on high and took me; he drew me out of many waters.

18 He delivered me from my strong enemy, from those who hated me, for they were too mighty for me.

19 They confronted me in the day of my calamity, but Yahweh was my support.

20 He brought me out into a broad place; he rescued me, because he delighted in me.

21 Yahweh rewarded me according to my righteousness; according to the cleanness of my hands he repaid me.

22 For I have kept the ways of Yahweh, and I have not wickedly departed from my God.

23 For all his judgments were before me, and his statutes — I did not turn aside from them.

24 I was blameless toward him, and I kept myself from my iniquity.

25 Yahweh repaid me according to my righteousness, according to my cleanness before his eyes.

26 With the loyal you show yourself loyal; with the blameless man you show yourself blameless.

27 With the pure you show yourself pure, and with the crooked you show yourself shrewd.

28 You save an afflicted people, but your eyes are on the haughty, to bring them down.

29 For you are my lamp, Yahweh; Yahweh lights up my darkness.

30 For by you I can run against a troop; by my God I can leap over a wall.

31 God — his way is perfect; Yahweh's word is proven; he is a shield to all who take refuge in him.

32 For who is God besides Yahweh? And who is a rock besides our God?

33 God is my strong fortress, and he makes my way blameless.

34 He makes my feet like the feet of deer, and sets me on my high places.

35 He trains my hands for war, so that my arms bend a bow of bronze.

36 You have given me the shield of your salvation, and your gentleness has made me great.

37 You enlarged my steps under me, and my ankles did not give way.

38 I pursued my enemies and destroyed them, and I did not turn back until they were finished.

39 I finished them and struck them down, so that they could not rise; they fell under my feet.

40 You girded me with strength for the battle; you bowed down those who rose against me under me.

41 You made my enemies turn their backs to me, and those who hated me — I cut them off.

42 They looked for help, but there was no savior; to Yahweh, but he did not answer them.

43 I beat them fine as the dust of the earth; I crushed them like the mire of the streets and stamped them down.

44 You delivered me from the strivings of my people; you kept me as head of the nations; a people I did not know serve me.

45 Foreigners cringe before me; as soon as they hear of me, they obey me.

46 Foreigners lose heart and come trembling out of their strongholds.

47 Yahweh lives! Blessed be my rock! Exalted be God, the rock of my salvation,

48 God, who gives me vengeance and brings peoples down under me,

49 who brings me out from my enemies; you lift me above those who rise against me; you deliver me from the man of violence.

50 Therefore I will thank you, Yahweh, among the nations, and I will sing praise to your name.

51 He is a tower of salvation for his king, and he shows loyal love to his anointed, to David and to his seed forever.

2 Samuel 23

1 These are the last words of David: the oracle of David the son of Jesse, and the oracle of the man raised on high, the anointed of the God of Jacob, and the sweet singer of Israel:

2 The Spirit of Yahweh spoke by me, and his word was on my tongue.

3 The God of Israel said, the Rock of Israel spoke to me: "One who rules over men in righteousness, who rules in the fear of God,

4 is like the light of the morning when the sun rises, a morning without clouds, when tender grass springs from the earth through brightness after rain."

5 For is not my house so with God? For he has made with me an everlasting covenant, ordered in all things and secure; for all my salvation and all my desire — will he not make it grow?

6 But the worthless are all like thorns thrust away, for they cannot be taken by hand;

7 the man who touches them must arm himself with iron and the shaft of a spear, and they will be utterly burned with fire in their place.

8 These are the names of the mighty men David had: Josheb-basshebeth the Tahchemonite, chief of the captains — he was Adino the Eznite — who struck down eight hundred men at one time.

9 After him was Eleazar the son of Dodo the son of Ahohi, one of the three mighty men with David, when they defied the Philistines who had gathered there for battle, and the men of Israel had withdrawn.

10 He rose and struck down the Philistines until his hand was weary and his hand clung to the sword, and Yahweh worked a great victory that day; and the people returned after him only to take the spoil.

11 After him was Shammah the son of Agee the Hararite. The Philistines had gathered together as a troop, and there was a plot of ground full of lentils, and the people had fled from the Philistines.

12 He took his stand in the middle of the plot and defended it and struck down the Philistines, and Yahweh worked a great victory.

13 Three of the thirty chiefs went down and came at harvest time to David at the cave of Adullam, while a troop of Philistines was encamped in the valley of Rephaim.

14 David was then in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Philistines was then at Bethlehem.

15 David longed and said, "Oh, that someone would give me water to drink from the well of Bethlehem that is by the gate!"

16 The three mighty men broke through the camp of the Philistines and drew water from the well of Bethlehem that is by the gate, and carried it and brought it to David. But he would not drink it, and he poured it out to Yahweh.

17 He said, "Far be it from me, Yahweh, to do this! Is this not the blood of the men who went at the risk of their lives?" So he would not drink it. These things the three mighty men did.

18 Abishai, the brother of Joab the son of Zeruiah, was chief of the three. He raised his spear against three hundred and struck them down, and he had a name among the three.

19 Was he not the most honored of the three? So he became their commander; yet he did not attain to the three.

20 Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the son of a valiant man great in deeds, from Kabzeel — he struck down the two lion-like heroes of Moab; he also went down and struck down a lion in a pit on a day of snow.

21 He struck down an Egyptian, an impressive-looking man; the Egyptian had a spear in his hand, but he went down to him with a staff, snatched the spear from the Egyptian's hand, and killed him with his own spear.

22 These things Benaiah the son of Jehoiada did, and he had a name among the three mighty men.

23 He was more honored than the thirty, but he did not attain to the three. David set him over his bodyguard.

24 Asahel the brother of Joab was among the thirty; Elhanan the son of Dodo of Bethlehem;

25 Shammah the Harodite, Elika the Harodite;

26 Helez the Paltite, Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite;

27 Abiezer the Anathothite, Mebunnai the Hushathite;

28 Zalmon the Ahohite, Maharai the Netophathite;

29 Heleb the son of Baanah the Netophathite, Ittai the son of Ribai from Gibeah of the children of Benjamin;

30 Benaiah the Pirathonite, Hiddai from the brooks of Gaash;

31 Abi-albon the Arbathite, Azmaveth the Barhumite;

32 Eliahba the Shaalbonite, the sons of Jashen, Jonathan;

33 Shammah the Hararite, Ahiam the son of Sharar the Ararite;

34 Eliphelet the son of Ahasbai, the son of the Maacathite, Eliam the son of Ahithophel the Gilonite;

35 Hezrai the Carmelite, Paarai the Arbite;

36 Igal the son of Nathan from Zobah, Bani the Gadite;

37 Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Beerothite, the armor-bearer of Joab the son of Zeruiah;

38 Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite;

39 Uriah the Hittite: thirty-seven in all.

2 Samuel 24

1 Again the anger of Yahweh burned against Israel, and he incited David against them, saying, "Go, count Israel and Judah."

2 The king said to Joab, the commander of the army who was with him, "Go through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan to Beersheba, and count the people, so that I may know the number of the people."

3 Joab said to the king, "May Yahweh your God add to the people a hundred times as many as they are, while the eyes of my lord the king see it; but why does my lord the king delight in this thing?"

4 But the king's word prevailed against Joab and against the commanders of the army, and Joab and the commanders of the army went out from the presence of the king to count the people of Israel.

5 They crossed the Jordan and camped at Aroer, on the right side of the city that is in the middle of the valley of Gad, and on toward Jazer.

6 They came to Gilead and to the land of Tahtim-hodshi, and they came to Dan-jaan and around to Sidon.

7 They came to the stronghold of Tyre and to all the cities of the Hivites and the Canaanites, and they went out to the Negeb of Judah at Beersheba.

8 They went through all the land, and at the end of nine months and twenty days they came to Jerusalem.

9 Joab gave the king the number of the count of the people: in Israel there were eight hundred thousand valiant men who drew the sword, and the men of Judah were five hundred thousand men.

10 David's heart struck him after he had counted the people, and David said to Yahweh, "I have sinned greatly in what I have done. Now, Yahweh, please take away the iniquity of your servant, for I have acted very foolishly."

11 When David rose in the morning, the word of Yahweh came to Gad the prophet, David's seer, saying,

12 "Go and speak to David: Thus says Yahweh: Three things I lay before you; choose one of them for yourself, and I will do it to you."

13 Gad came to David and told him, and said to him, "Shall seven years of famine come to you in your land? Or will you flee three months before your foes while they pursue you? Or shall there be three days of plague in your land? Now consider and decide what answer I shall return to him who sent me."

14 David said to Gad, "I am in great distress. Let us fall into the hand of Yahweh, for his mercies are great; but let me not fall into the hand of man."

15 Yahweh sent a plague on Israel from the morning until the appointed time, and seventy thousand men of the people died, from Dan to Beersheba.

16 When the angel stretched out his hand toward Jerusalem to destroy it, Yahweh relented concerning the disaster and said to the angel who was destroying the people, "Enough! Now withdraw your hand." The angel of Yahweh was by the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.

17 David spoke to Yahweh when he saw the angel who was striking the people, and said, "See, I have sinned, and I have done wrong; but these sheep, what have they done? Please let your hand be against me and against my father's house."

18 Gad came to David that day and said to him, "Go up, set up an altar to Yahweh on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite."

19 David went up according to the word of Gad, as Yahweh had commanded.

20 Araunah looked out and saw the king and his servants crossing over toward him, and Araunah went out and bowed before the king with his face to the ground.

21 Araunah said, "Why has my lord the king come to his servant?" David said, "To buy the threshing floor from you, to build an altar to Yahweh, so that the plague may be stopped from the people."

22 Araunah said to David, "Let my lord the king take and offer up what is good in his eyes. See, the oxen for the burnt offering, and the threshing sledges and the gear of the oxen for the wood.

23 All this, O king, Araunah gives to the king." And Araunah said to the king, "May Yahweh your God accept you."

24 The king said to Araunah, "No, but I will surely buy it from you for a price; I will not offer burnt offerings to Yahweh my God that cost me nothing." So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver.

25 David built there an altar to Yahweh and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. Yahweh answered prayer for the land, and the plague was stopped from Israel.

"The Lord" stands at five seats of the divine name אֲדֹנָי: 2:26 and 8:53 in the collocation אֲדֹנָי יְהוִה, "the Lord Yahweh" (at 2:26, "the ark of the Lord Yahweh"), and 3:10, 3:15 and 22:6 standalone (at 3:15, "the ark of the covenant of the Lord"; at 22:6 on the lips of the four hundred prophets, where Micaiah's answer in the same chapter speaks the name יהוה). Every other "lord" in the book addresses or names a man — "my lord" to David and passim to Solomon the king, "our lord" (1:11; 1:43; 1:47), "your [plural] lord" (1:33), "his lord" of Hadadezer (11:23), "their lord" of Rehoboam (12:27), "the owner of" the hill (16:24), "a master" (22:17) — or is the name Adonijah or Adoniram, and prints lowercase, or as the name it is, throughout. No standalone יהּ seat stands in the book. In chapter 8 alone the name stands 36 times and the designation 14 times. חסד prints "loyal love" at 3:6, 8:23 and 20:31. The directed seats stand as the commission named them: 1–2 entire (Adonijah's bid; Nathan and Bathsheba; Solomon anointed; David's charge at 2:1–9 at full force as the Masoretic text stands, the named blood-debts included; the executions as they stand); 3 entire (the dream at Gibeon, 3:5–15; the judgment of the two mothers, 3:16–28); 5–7 (the temple building, measurements and materials as the Hebrew gives them, no conversions in the text); 8 entire (the cloud at 8:10–11; Solomon's prayer, 8:22–53, at full force); 9:1–9 (the warning as it stands); 10 (the queen of Sheba; the gold and the throne); 11 entire (at full force exactly as the Masoretic text stands); 12 entire (12:10–11 as the Masoretic text stands; Jeroboam's calves at 12:28–33, "behold your gods, O Israel" as the Hebrew gives it); 13 entire (as the Masoretic text stands); 14 (Ahijah; Shishak — the qere at 14:25); 16:23–34 (16:34, Hiel of Bethel rebuilding Jericho, as it stands); 17 entire (the widow's son raised, 17:17–24, as it stands); 18 entire (Carmel at full force; the slaughter at the Kishon at 18:40 exactly as the Masoretic text stands); 19 entire (19:11–13 — the wind, the earthquake, the fire, and at 19:12 קוֹל דְּמָמָה דַקָּה printed in the settled clear form, "a still small voice", its construal recorded in the open seats; Elisha's call, 19:19–21); 20 (Ben-hadad; the man of God and the lion at 20:35–36 as it stands); 21 entire (Naboth's vineyard at full force; Elijah's oracle at 21:19–24 exactly as the Masoretic text stands; Ahab's humbling at 21:27–29 as it stands); and 22 entire (Micaiah's throne vision at 22:19–22 printed exactly as the Masoretic text stands, the lying spirit included, unharmonised and unsoftened; the bow drawn at random; the dogs at 22:38 as it stands). The difference ledger records 703 of the book's 817 verses as differing in wording from both controls (62 differing from JPS 1917 only, 11 from the seated text only, 41 identical to both), and 45 open seats stand recorded, headed by the four Bolls drops, the 44 ketiv/qere seats, the construal at 19:12, and the temple architecture of chapters 6–7 among the reviser seats. The book stands as DRAFT — NOT PUBLISHED.

1 Kings 1

1 King David was old, advanced in years, and they covered him with clothes, but he could not get warm.

2 His servants said to him, "Let a young virgin be sought for my lord the king, and let her stand before the king and attend him, and let her lie in your bosom, so that my lord the king may get warm."

3 So they searched for a beautiful young woman throughout all the territory of Israel, and they found Abishag the Shunammite and brought her to the king.

4 The young woman was very beautiful, and she became the king's attendant and served him, but the king did not know her.

5 Adonijah son of Haggith exalted himself, saying, "I will be king," and he prepared for himself chariots and horsemen and fifty men to run before him.

6 His father had never grieved him at any time by saying, "Why have you done this?" He was also a very handsome man, and he was born after Absalom.

7 He conferred with Joab son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, and they helped Adonijah by following him.

8 But Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and the mighty men who belonged to David were not with Adonijah.

9 Adonijah sacrificed sheep, oxen, and fattened cattle by the stone of Zoheleth, which is beside En-rogel, and he invited all his brothers, the king's sons, and all the men of Judah, the king's servants.

10 But Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, the mighty men, and Solomon his brother he did not invite.

11 Nathan spoke to Bathsheba, Solomon's mother, saying, "Have you not heard that Adonijah son of Haggith has become king, and David our lord does not know it?

12 Now come, let me give you counsel, so that you may save your own life and the life of your son Solomon.

13 Go in to King David and say to him, 'Did you not, my lord the king, swear to your servant, saying, "Solomon your son will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne"? Why then has Adonijah become king?'

14 While you are still speaking there with the king, I will come in after you and confirm your words."

15 Bathsheba went in to the king in the chamber. The king was very old, and Abishag the Shunammite was serving the king.

16 Bathsheba bowed and prostrated herself before the king, and the king said, "What do you wish?"

17 She said to him, "My lord, you swore by Yahweh your God to your servant, 'Solomon your son will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne.'

18 And now, see, Adonijah has become king, and you, my lord the king, do not know it.

19 He has sacrificed oxen, fattened cattle, and sheep in abundance, and has invited all the king's sons, Abiathar the priest, and Joab the commander of the army, but Solomon your servant he has not invited.

20 As for you, my lord the king, the eyes of all Israel are on you, to tell them who will sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.

21 Otherwise, when my lord the king sleeps with his fathers, I and my son Solomon will be counted offenders."

22 While she was still speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet came in.

23 They told the king, saying, "Here is Nathan the prophet." When he came in before the king, he bowed before the king with his face to the ground.

24 Nathan said, "My lord the king, have you said, 'Adonijah will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne'?

25 For he has gone down today and sacrificed oxen, fattened cattle, and sheep in abundance, and has invited all the king's sons, the commanders of the army, and Abiathar the priest, and there they are, eating and drinking before him and saying, 'Long live King Adonijah!'

26 But me, your servant, and Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and Solomon your servant he has not invited.

27 Has this thing been done by my lord the king, and have you not let your servant know who will sit on the throne of my lord the king after him?"

28 King David answered and said, "Call Bathsheba to me." She came into the king's presence and stood before the king.

29 The king swore and said, "As Yahweh lives, who has redeemed my life out of every trouble,

30 just as I swore to you by Yahweh, the God of Israel, saying, 'Solomon your son will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne in my place,' so I will do today."

31 Bathsheba bowed with her face to the ground and prostrated herself before the king, and said, "Let my lord King David live forever."

32 King David said, "Call to me Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada." They came before the king.

33 The king said to them, "Take with you the servants of your lord, and set Solomon my son riding on my own mule, and bring him down to Gihon.

34 There Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet are to anoint him king over Israel, and you are to blow the trumpet and say, 'Long live King Solomon!'

35 Then you will come up after him, and he will come and sit on my throne, for he will be king in my place, and I have appointed him to be ruler over Israel and over Judah."

36 Benaiah son of Jehoiada answered the king and said, "Amen. May Yahweh, the God of my lord the king, say so.

37 As Yahweh has been with my lord the king, so may he be with Solomon, and may he make his throne greater than the throne of my lord King David."

38 Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites went down and set Solomon riding on King David's mule and brought him to Gihon.

39 Zadok the priest took the horn of oil from the tent and anointed Solomon, and they blew the trumpet, and all the people said, "Long live King Solomon!"

40 All the people came up after him, and the people were playing flutes and rejoicing with great joy, so that the earth was split by their sound.

41 Adonijah and all the guests who were with him heard it as they finished eating. Joab heard the sound of the trumpet and said, "Why is the city making this uproar?"

42 While he was still speaking, Jonathan son of Abiathar the priest came in, and Adonijah said, "Come in, for you are a worthy man and you bring good news."

43 Jonathan answered and said to Adonijah, "Indeed, David our lord the king has made Solomon king.

44 The king has sent with him Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and the Cherethites and the Pelethites, and they have set him riding on the king's mule.

45 Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet have anointed him king in Gihon, and they have come up from there rejoicing, so that the city is in an uproar. That is the sound you have heard.

46 Solomon has also sat on the throne of the kingdom.

47 The king's servants have also come to bless David our lord the king, saying, 'May God make Solomon's name greater than your name, and may he make his throne greater than your throne,' and the king bowed down on the bed.

48 The king also said this: 'Blessed be Yahweh, the God of Israel, who has given one to sit on my throne today, with my own eyes seeing it.'"

49 All Adonijah's guests were terrified, and they rose and went, each man his own way.

50 Adonijah was afraid because of Solomon, and he rose and went and took hold of the horns of the altar.

51 It was told to Solomon, saying, "See, Adonijah is afraid of King Solomon, and see, he has taken hold of the horns of the altar, saying, 'Let King Solomon swear to me today that he will not put his servant to death with the sword.'"

52 Solomon said, "If he proves to be a worthy man, not one hair of his will fall to the ground, but if evil is found in him, he will die."

53 King Solomon sent, and they brought him down from the altar. He came and prostrated himself before King Solomon, and Solomon said to him, "Go to your house."

1 Kings 2

1 The days of David drew near for him to die, and he charged Solomon his son, saying,

2 "I am going the way of all the earth. Be strong, and show yourself a man,

3 and keep the charge of Yahweh your God, walking in his ways, keeping his statutes, his commandments, his judgments, and his testimonies, as written in the law of Moses, so that you may prosper in all that you do and everywhere you turn,

4 so that Yahweh may establish his word that he spoke concerning me, saying, 'If your sons take care to walk before me in truth with all their heart and with all their soul, you will not fail to have a man on the throne of Israel.'

5 You also know what Joab son of Zeruiah did to me, what he did to the two commanders of the armies of Israel, Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether, whom he killed, shedding the blood of war in peacetime and putting the blood of war on the belt around his waist and on the sandals on his feet.

6 Act according to your wisdom, and do not let his gray head go down to Sheol in peace.

7 Show loyal love to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite, and let them be among those who eat at your table, for they came to me in that way when I fled from Absalom your brother.

8 See, there is with you Shimei son of Gera, the Benjaminite from Bahurim, who cursed me with a bitter curse on the day I went to Mahanaim. He came down to meet me at the Jordan, and I swore to him by Yahweh, saying, 'I will not put you to death with the sword.'

9 Now do not hold him guiltless, for you are a wise man and you will know what you ought to do to him: bring his gray head down to Sheol with blood."

10 David slept with his fathers and was buried in the city of David.

11 The days that David reigned over Israel were forty years: he reigned seven years in Hebron, and he reigned thirty-three years in Jerusalem.

12 Solomon sat on the throne of David his father, and his kingdom was firmly established.

13 Adonijah son of Haggith came to Bathsheba, Solomon's mother, and she said, "Do you come in peace?" He said, "In peace."

14 He said, "I have something to say to you." She said, "Speak."

15 He said, "You know that the kingdom was mine, and all Israel set their faces on me to reign, but the kingdom has turned about and become my brother's, for it was his from Yahweh.

16 Now I have one request to ask of you; do not refuse me." She said to him, "Speak."

17 He said, "Please speak to King Solomon, for he will not refuse you, that he give me Abishag the Shunammite as wife."

18 Bathsheba said, "Good; I will speak to the king for you."

19 Bathsheba went to King Solomon to speak to him for Adonijah. The king rose to meet her and bowed to her, and he sat on his throne and had a throne set for the king's mother, and she sat at his right hand.

20 She said, "I have one small request to ask of you; do not refuse me." The king said to her, "Ask, my mother, for I will not refuse you."

21 She said, "Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to Adonijah your brother as wife."

22 King Solomon answered and said to his mother, "Why do you ask Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? Ask the kingdom for him too, for he is my brother, older than I — for him, and for Abiathar the priest, and for Joab son of Zeruiah."

23 King Solomon swore by Yahweh, saying, "May God do so to me, and more also, if Adonijah has not spoken this word at the cost of his own life.

24 Now, as Yahweh lives, who has established me and set me on the throne of David my father and has made me a house, as he promised, Adonijah will be put to death today."

25 King Solomon sent by the hand of Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he struck him down, and he died.

26 To Abiathar the priest the king said, "Go to Anathoth, to your fields, for you deserve to die, but I will not put you to death today, because you carried the ark of the Lord Yahweh before David my father and because you were afflicted in all that my father was afflicted."

27 Solomon drove Abiathar out from being a priest to Yahweh, fulfilling the word of Yahweh that he had spoken concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh.

28 The news came to Joab — for Joab had turned after Adonijah, though he had not turned after Absalom — and Joab fled to the tent of Yahweh and took hold of the horns of the altar.

29 It was told to King Solomon that Joab had fled to the tent of Yahweh and was there beside the altar, and Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, saying, "Go, strike him down."

30 Benaiah came to the tent of Yahweh and said to him, "This is what the king says: 'Come out.'" He said, "No, for I will die here." Benaiah brought the king word again, saying, "This is what Joab said, and this is how he answered me."

31 The king said to him, "Do as he has said: strike him down and bury him, and remove from me and from my father's house the blood that Joab shed without cause.

32 Yahweh will return his blood on his own head, because he struck down two men more righteous and better than he and killed them with the sword, while my father David did not know it: Abner son of Ner, commander of the army of Israel, and Amasa son of Jether, commander of the army of Judah.

33 Their blood will return on the head of Joab and on the head of his offspring forever, but for David and his offspring and his house and his throne there will be peace from Yahweh forever."

34 Benaiah son of Jehoiada went up and struck him down and killed him, and he was buried in his own house in the wilderness.

35 The king put Benaiah son of Jehoiada in his place over the army, and the king put Zadok the priest in Abiathar's place.

36 The king sent and called Shimei and said to him, "Build yourself a house in Jerusalem and live there, and do not go out from there anywhere at all.

37 On the day you go out and cross the Kidron valley, know for certain that you will surely die; your blood will be on your own head."

38 Shimei said to the king, "The word is good. As my lord the king has said, so your servant will do." Shimei lived in Jerusalem many days.

39 At the end of three years, two of Shimei's servants ran away to Achish son of Maacah, king of Gath, and they told Shimei, saying, "See, your servants are in Gath."

40 Shimei rose and saddled his donkey and went to Gath, to Achish, to seek his servants, and Shimei went and brought his servants from Gath.

41 It was told to Solomon that Shimei had gone from Jerusalem to Gath and had returned.

42 The king sent and called Shimei and said to him, "Did I not make you swear by Yahweh and warn you, saying, 'On the day you go out and go anywhere at all, know for certain that you will surely die'? And you said to me, 'The word I have heard is good.'

43 Why then have you not kept the oath of Yahweh and the command that I charged you with?"

44 The king said to Shimei, "You know all the evil that your heart knows, which you did to David my father, and Yahweh will return your evil on your own head.

45 But King Solomon will be blessed, and the throne of David will be established before Yahweh forever."

46 The king commanded Benaiah son of Jehoiada, and he went out and struck him down, and he died. The kingdom was established in Solomon's hand.

1 Kings 3

1 Solomon made a marriage alliance with Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he took Pharaoh's daughter and brought her into the city of David until he had finished building his own house, the house of Yahweh, and the wall around Jerusalem.

2 The people were still sacrificing at the high places, because no house had yet been built for the name of Yahweh up to those days.

3 Solomon loved Yahweh, walking in the statutes of David his father, except that he sacrificed and burned incense at the high places.

4 The king went to Gibeon to sacrifice there, for that was the great high place; Solomon offered a thousand burnt offerings on that altar.

5 At Gibeon Yahweh appeared to Solomon in a dream by night, and God said, "Ask what I should give you."

6 Solomon said, "You have shown great loyal love to your servant David my father, as he walked before you in truth, in righteousness, and in uprightness of heart with you, and you have kept this great loyal love for him and have given him a son to sit on his throne, as it is today.

7 Now, Yahweh my God, you have made your servant king in place of David my father, and I am a little child; I do not know how to go out or come in.

8 Your servant is in the midst of your people whom you have chosen, a great people who cannot be numbered or counted for multitude.

9 Give your servant a listening heart to judge your people, to discern between good and evil, for who is able to judge this great people of yours?"

10 The word was good in the eyes of the Lord, that Solomon had asked this thing.

11 God said to him, "Because you have asked this thing, and have not asked for yourself many days, and have not asked for yourself riches, and have not asked for the life of your enemies, but have asked for yourself discernment to hear judgment,

12 see, I have done according to your words. See, I have given you a wise and discerning heart, so that there has been no one like you before you, and after you no one like you will arise.

13 I have also given you what you did not ask, both riches and glory, so that there will be no king like you in all your days.

14 If you walk in my ways, keeping my statutes and my commandments, as David your father walked, I will lengthen your days."

15 Solomon awoke, and see, it was a dream. He came to Jerusalem and stood before the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and he offered burnt offerings and made peace offerings and made a feast for all his servants.

16 Then two women who were prostitutes came to the king and stood before him.

17 One woman said, "Please, my lord, I and this woman live in one house, and I gave birth with her in the house.

18 On the third day after I gave birth, this woman also gave birth, and we were together; there was no stranger with us in the house — only we two were in the house.

19 This woman's son died in the night, because she lay on him.

20 She rose in the middle of the night and took my son from beside me while your servant slept, and laid him in her bosom, and laid her dead son in my bosom.

21 When I rose in the morning to nurse my son, see, he was dead. When I looked closely at him in the morning, see, he was not my son, whom I had borne."

22 The other woman said, "No, for the living one is my son and the dead one is your son." And this one said, "No, for the dead one is your son and the living one is my son." They spoke before the king.

23 The king said, "One says, 'This is my son, the living one, and your son is the dead one,' and the other says, 'No, for your son is the dead one and my son is the living one.'"

24 The king said, "Bring me a sword." They brought the sword before the king.

25 The king said, "Cut the living child in two, and give half to one and half to the other."

26 The woman whose son was the living one spoke to the king, because her compassion burned for her son, and she said, "Please, my lord, give her the living child, and do not put him to death at all." But the other said, "He will be neither mine nor yours; cut him."

27 The king answered and said, "Give her the living child, and do not put him to death at all; she is his mother."

28 All Israel heard of the judgment that the king had judged, and they feared the king, for they saw that the wisdom of God was in him to do justice.

1 Kings 4

1 King Solomon was king over all Israel.

2 These were his officials: Azariah son of Zadok, the priest;

3 Elihoreph and Ahijah, sons of Shisha, scribes; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud, the recorder;

4 Benaiah son of Jehoiada, over the army; Zadok and Abiathar, priests;

5 Azariah son of Nathan, over the officers; Zabud son of Nathan, a priest, the king's friend;

6 Ahishar, over the household; Adoniram son of Abda, over the forced labor.

7 Solomon had twelve officers over all Israel, who provided for the king and his household; each man was to provide for one month in the year.

8 These are their names: Ben-hur, in the hill country of Ephraim;

9 Ben-deker, in Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth-shemesh, and Elon-beth-hanan;

10 Ben-hesed, in Arubboth — Socoh and all the land of Hepher were his;

11 Ben-abinadab, in all the height of Dor — Taphath, Solomon's daughter, was his wife;

12 Baana son of Ahilud, in Taanach and Megiddo and all Beth-shean, which is beside Zarethan below Jezreel, from Beth-shean to Abel-meholah, as far as the other side of Jokmeam;

13 Ben-geber, in Ramoth-gilead — the villages of Jair son of Manasseh, which are in Gilead, were his, and the region of Argob, which is in Bashan, sixty great cities with walls and bronze bars, was his;

14 Ahinadab son of Iddo, in Mahanaim;

15 Ahimaaz, in Naphtali — he too took Basemath, Solomon's daughter, as wife;

16 Baana son of Hushai, in Asher and Bealoth;

17 Jehoshaphat son of Paruah, in Issachar;

18 Shimei son of Ela, in Benjamin;

19 Geber son of Uri, in the land of Gilead, the land of Sihon king of the Amorites and Og king of Bashan; and there was one officer who was in the land.

20 Judah and Israel were many, like the sand by the sea in multitude, eating and drinking and rejoicing.

1 Kings 5

1 Solomon ruled over all the kingdoms from the River to the land of the Philistines and as far as the border of Egypt; they brought tribute and served Solomon all the days of his life.

2 Solomon's provision for one day was thirty cors of fine flour and sixty cors of meal,

3 ten fattened oxen, twenty pasture oxen, and a hundred sheep, besides deer, gazelles, roebucks, and fattened fowl.

4 For he held dominion over all the region beyond the River, from Tiphsah to Gaza, over all the kings beyond the River, and he had peace on every side around him.

5 Judah and Israel lived in safety, each man under his vine and under his fig tree, from Dan to Beersheba, all the days of Solomon.

6 Solomon had forty thousand stalls for the horses of his chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen.

7 Those officers supplied food for King Solomon and for everyone who came to King Solomon's table, each in his month; they let nothing be lacking.

8 They also brought barley and straw for the horses and the swift steeds to the place where each man was stationed, according to his charge.

9 God gave Solomon wisdom and very great understanding, and breadth of heart like the sand on the seashore.

10 Solomon's wisdom surpassed the wisdom of all the people of the east and all the wisdom of Egypt.

11 He was wiser than all other men — than Ethan the Ezrahite, and Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol — and his fame spread among all the nations around.

12 He spoke three thousand proverbs, and his songs were one thousand and five.

13 He spoke about trees, from the cedar in Lebanon to the hyssop that grows out of the wall; he also spoke about animals, birds, creeping things, and fish.

14 People came from all the nations to hear Solomon's wisdom, from all the kings of the earth who had heard of his wisdom.

15 Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants to Solomon, because he heard that they had anointed him king in his father's place, for Hiram had always loved David.

16 Solomon sent word to Hiram, saying:

17 You know that David my father could not build a house for the name of Yahweh his God because of the wars that surrounded him, until Yahweh put them under the soles of his feet.

18 But now Yahweh my God has given me rest on every side; there is no adversary and no misfortune.

19 So I intend to build a house for the name of Yahweh my God, as Yahweh spoke to David my father, saying: Your son, whom I will set on your throne in your place, he will build the house for my name.

20 Now therefore give the order, and let cedars from Lebanon be cut for me; my servants will work with your servants, and I will pay you wages for your servants according to whatever you say, for you know that among us there is no one who knows how to cut timber like the Sidonians.

21 When Hiram heard Solomon's words, he rejoiced greatly and said: Blessed be Yahweh today, who has given David a wise son over this great people.

22 Hiram sent word to Solomon, saying: I have heard what you sent to me; I will do everything you desire concerning cedar timber and cypress timber.

23 My servants will bring them down from Lebanon to the sea, and I will make them into rafts to go by sea to the place you appoint for me, and I will break them up there, and you will take them away; and you will do what I desire, giving food for my household.

24 So Hiram gave Solomon cedar timber and cypress timber, all that he desired.

25 Solomon gave Hiram twenty thousand cors of wheat as food for his household, and twenty cors of beaten oil; this Solomon gave Hiram year by year.

26 Yahweh gave Solomon wisdom, as he had promised him; there was peace between Hiram and Solomon, and the two of them made a covenant.

27 King Solomon raised a levy of forced labor from all Israel, and the levy was thirty thousand men.

28 He sent them to Lebanon, ten thousand a month in relays; one month they were in Lebanon and two months at home, and Adoniram was over the levy.

29 Solomon had seventy thousand burden-bearers and eighty thousand stonecutters in the mountains,

30 besides Solomon's chief officers who were over the work, three thousand three hundred, who supervised the people doing the work.

31 The king commanded, and they quarried large stones, costly stones, to lay the foundation of the house with hewn stones.

32 Solomon's builders, Hiram's builders, and the Gebalites shaped them, and prepared the timber and the stones for building the house.

1 Kings 6

1 In the four hundred and eightieth year after the children of Israel came out of the land of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon's reign over Israel, in the month of Ziv, which is the second month, he began to build the house of Yahweh.

2 The house that King Solomon built for Yahweh was sixty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high.

3 The porch in front of the main hall of the house was twenty cubits long, across the width of the house, and ten cubits deep in front of the house.

4 He made for the house windows that were recessed and latticed.

5 Against the wall of the house he built a side structure all around, against the walls of the house all around, both the main hall and the inner sanctuary, and he made side chambers all around.
