26 At the turn of the year, Ben-hadad mustered Aram and went up to Aphek to fight against Israel.

27 The children of Israel were mustered and supplied with provisions, and they went out against them. The children of Israel camped opposite them like two small flocks of goats, while Aram filled the land.

28 A man of God came near and spoke to the king of Israel, saying, "Yahweh says this: 'Because Aram has said, Yahweh is a god of the hills, but he is not a god of the valleys, I will give all this great multitude into your hand, and you will know that I am Yahweh.'"

29 They camped opposite one another for seven days. On the seventh day the battle was joined, and the children of Israel struck down one hundred thousand foot soldiers of Aram in one day.

30 The rest fled to Aphek, into the city, and the wall fell on twenty-seven thousand of the men who remained. Ben-hadad fled and came into the city, into an inner room.

31 His servants said to him, "Behold, we have heard that the kings of the house of Israel are kings of loyal love. Let us put sackcloth around our waists and ropes on our heads and go out to the king of Israel; perhaps he will let you live."

32 So they girded sackcloth around their waists and put ropes on their heads, and came to the king of Israel and said, "Your servant Ben-hadad says, 'Please let me live.'" He said, "Is he still alive? He is my brother."

33 The men took it as an omen, and hurried to seize on whether it came from him, and they said, "Your brother Ben-hadad!" He said, "Go, bring him." Then Ben-hadad came out to him, and he had him come up into his chariot.

34 Ben-hadad said to him, "The cities my father took from your father I will restore, and you may make streets for yourself in Damascus, as my father made in Samaria." "And I," said Ahab, "will send you away under this covenant." So he made a covenant with him and sent him away.

35 A certain man of the sons of the prophets said to his fellow, by the word of Yahweh, "Strike me, please." But the man refused to strike him.

36 He said to him, "Because you have not obeyed the voice of Yahweh, behold, as soon as you leave me, a lion will strike you." As soon as he had left him, a lion found him and struck him.

37 Then he found another man and said, "Strike me, please." The man struck him, striking and wounding him.

38 So the prophet went and waited for the king by the road, and disguised himself with a bandage over his eyes.

39 As the king passed by, he cried out to the king and said, "Your servant went out into the thick of the battle, and behold, a man turned aside and brought a man to me and said, 'Guard this man. If he goes missing, your life shall be for his life, or you shall pay a talent of silver.'

40 While your servant was busy here and there, he was gone." The king of Israel said to him, "So shall your judgment be; you yourself have decided it."

41 He hurried and removed the bandage from his eyes, and the king of Israel recognized him, that he was one of the prophets.

42 He said to him, "Yahweh says this: 'Because you have let go from your hand the man devoted to destruction for me, your life shall be for his life, and your people for his people.'"

43 The king of Israel went to his house sullen and vexed, and came to Samaria.

1 Kings 21

1 After these things, Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard in Jezreel, beside the palace of Ahab king of Samaria.

2 Ahab spoke to Naboth, saying, "Give me your vineyard, so that I may have it as a vegetable garden, because it is close beside my house. I will give you a better vineyard than it in exchange; or, if it seems good to you, I will give you its price in silver."

3 Naboth said to Ahab, "Yahweh forbid that I should give you the inheritance of my fathers."

4 Ahab came into his house sullen and vexed because of the word Naboth the Jezreelite had spoken to him, for he had said, "I will not give you the inheritance of my fathers." He lay down on his bed, turned away his face, and ate no food.

5 Jezebel his wife came to him and said to him, "Why is your spirit so sullen, and why do you eat no food?"

6 He said to her, "Because I spoke to Naboth the Jezreelite and said to him, 'Give me your vineyard for silver; or, if you prefer, I will give you a vineyard in exchange for it,' and he answered, 'I will not give you my vineyard.'"

7 Jezebel his wife said to him, "You now exercise kingship over Israel! Rise, eat food, and let your heart be glad. I myself will give you the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite."

8 So she wrote letters in Ahab's name, sealed them with his seal, and sent the letters to the elders and the nobles who were in his city, who lived with Naboth.

9 She wrote in the letters, saying, "Proclaim a fast, and seat Naboth at the head of the people.

10 Seat two worthless men opposite him, and let them testify against him, saying, 'You cursed God and the king.' Then take him out, stone him, and let him die."

11 The men of his city, the elders and the nobles who lived in his city, did as Jezebel had sent to them, as it was written in the letters she had sent to them.

12 They proclaimed a fast, and seated Naboth at the head of the people.

13 The two worthless men came in and sat opposite him, and the worthless men testified against Naboth in the presence of the people, saying, "Naboth cursed God and the king." Then they took him outside the city and stoned him with stones, and he died.

14 Then they sent to Jezebel, saying, "Naboth has been stoned, and he is dead."

15 When Jezebel heard that Naboth had been stoned and was dead, Jezebel said to Ahab, "Rise, take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, which he refused to give you for silver, for Naboth is not alive but dead."

16 When Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, Ahab rose to go down to the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, to take possession of it.

17 Then the word of Yahweh came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,

18 "Rise, go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who is in Samaria. Behold, he is in the vineyard of Naboth, where he has gone down to take possession of it.

19 You shall speak to him, saying, 'Yahweh says this: Have you murdered, and also taken possession?' And you shall speak to him, saying, 'Yahweh says this: In the place where dogs licked the blood of Naboth, dogs will lick your blood, even yours.'"

20 Ahab said to Elijah, "Have you found me, my enemy?" He answered, "I have found you, because you have sold yourself to do what is evil in the eyes of Yahweh.

21 Behold, I will bring disaster on you, and I will sweep away after you, and I will cut off from Ahab every male, both bound and free, in Israel.

22 I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah, because of the provocation with which you have provoked me and have made Israel sin."

23 And of Jezebel also Yahweh spoke, saying, "The dogs will eat Jezebel by the rampart of Jezreel.

24 Whoever of Ahab's dies in the city, the dogs will eat; and whoever dies in the field, the birds of the sky will eat."

25 There was no one like Ahab, who sold himself to do what is evil in the eyes of Yahweh, whom Jezebel his wife incited.

26 He acted very abominably in going after idols, according to all that the Amorites did, whom Yahweh drove out before the children of Israel.

27 When Ahab heard these words, he tore his clothes, put sackcloth on his flesh, and fasted. He lay in sackcloth, and went about subdued.

28 Then the word of Yahweh came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,

29 "Have you seen how Ahab has humbled himself before me? Because he has humbled himself before me, I will not bring the disaster in his days; in his son's days I will bring the disaster on his house."

1 Kings 22

1 They remained three years with no war between Aram and Israel.

2 In the third year, Jehoshaphat king of Judah came down to the king of Israel.

3 The king of Israel said to his servants, "Do you know that Ramoth-gilead is ours, and yet we are doing nothing to take it from the hand of the king of Aram?"

4 He said to Jehoshaphat, "Will you go with me to battle at Ramoth-gilead?" Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses."

5 Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "Please inquire today for the word of Yahweh."

6 Then the king of Israel gathered the prophets together, about four hundred men, and said to them, "Shall I go against Ramoth-gilead to battle, or shall I hold back?" They said, "Go up, for the Lord will give it into the hand of the king."

7 But Jehoshaphat said, "Is there no prophet of Yahweh here besides, that we may inquire of him?"

8 The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "There is still one man by whom we may inquire of Yahweh — Micaiah son of Imlah — but I hate him, for he does not prophesy good concerning me, but evil." Jehoshaphat said, "Let not the king say so."

9 Then the king of Israel called an officer and said, "Bring Micaiah son of Imlah quickly."

10 Now the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting, each on his throne, clothed in their robes, on a threshing floor at the entrance of the gate of Samaria, and all the prophets were prophesying before them.

11 Zedekiah son of Chenaanah made himself horns of iron and said, "Yahweh says this: 'With these you shall gore Aram until they are finished.'"

12 All the prophets prophesied so, saying, "Go up to Ramoth-gilead and prosper, for Yahweh will give it into the hand of the king."

13 The messenger who had gone to call Micaiah spoke to him, saying, "Behold, the words of the prophets with one mouth declare good to the king. Please let your word be like the word of one of them, and speak good."

14 Micaiah said, "As Yahweh lives, what Yahweh says to me, that I will speak."

15 When he came to the king, the king said to him, "Micaiah, shall we go to Ramoth-gilead to battle, or shall we hold back?" He said to him, "Go up and prosper, and Yahweh will give it into the hand of the king."

16 The king said to him, "How many times shall I put you under oath to speak to me nothing but the truth in the name of Yahweh?"

17 He said, "I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains, like sheep that have no shepherd. And Yahweh said, 'These have no master; let each return to his house in peace.'"

18 The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Did I not tell you that he would not prophesy good concerning me, but evil?"

19 He said, "Therefore hear the word of Yahweh. I saw Yahweh sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven standing beside him on his right hand and on his left.

20 Yahweh said, 'Who will entice Ahab, so that he may go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead?' And one said this, and another said that.

21 Then the spirit came forward and stood before Yahweh and said, 'I will entice him.' And Yahweh said to him, 'By what?'

22 He said, 'I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.' He said, 'You shall entice him, and you shall also prevail. Go out and do so.'

23 Now therefore, behold, Yahweh has put a lying spirit in the mouth of all these prophets of yours, and Yahweh has spoken disaster concerning you."

24 Then Zedekiah son of Chenaanah came near and struck Micaiah on the cheek, and said, "Which way did the spirit of Yahweh pass from me to speak to you?"

25 Micaiah said, "Behold, you will see on that day, when you go into an inner room to hide."

26 The king of Israel said, "Take Micaiah and return him to Amon the governor of the city and to Joash the king's son,

27 and say, 'The king says this: Put this man in the prison, and feed him with scant bread and scant water, until I return in peace.'"

28 Micaiah said, "If you return in peace at all, Yahweh has not spoken by me." And he said, "Hear, all you peoples!"

29 So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up to Ramoth-gilead.

30 The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "I will disguise myself and go into the battle, but you wear your robes." So the king of Israel disguised himself and went into the battle.

31 Now the king of Aram had commanded the thirty-two captains of his chariots, saying, "Fight with neither small nor great, but only with the king of Israel."

32 When the captains of the chariots saw Jehoshaphat, they said, "Surely it is the king of Israel," and they turned to fight against him. And Jehoshaphat cried out.

33 When the captains of the chariots saw that it was not the king of Israel, they turned back from pursuing him.

34 A certain man drew his bow at random and struck the king of Israel between the joints of the armor. He said to his chariot driver, "Turn your hand and carry me out of the camp, for I am wounded."

35 The battle grew fiercer that day, and the king was held upright in his chariot facing Aram, and he died in the evening. The blood from the wound flowed into the bottom of the chariot.

36 A cry passed through the camp at the going down of the sun, saying, "Each man to his city, and each man to his land!"

37 So the king died, and he was brought to Samaria, and they buried the king in Samaria.

38 They washed the chariot by the pool of Samaria, and the dogs licked up his blood, and the prostitutes washed there, according to the word of Yahweh that he had spoken.

39 Now the rest of the acts of Ahab, and all that he did, and the ivory house that he built, and all the cities that he built — are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

40 So Ahab slept with his fathers, and Ahaziah his son reigned in his place.

41 Jehoshaphat son of Asa began to reign over Judah in the fourth year of Ahab king of Israel.

42 Jehoshaphat was thirty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.

43 He walked in all the way of Asa his father; he did not turn aside from it, doing what was right in the eyes of Yahweh.

44 But the high places were not removed; the people still sacrificed and burned incense on the high places.

45 And Jehoshaphat made peace with the king of Israel.

46 Now the rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, and his might that he showed, and how he fought — are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?

47 And the rest of the male shrine prostitutes who remained in the days of his father Asa, he removed from the land.

48 There was no king in Edom; a deputy was king.

49 Jehoshaphat made ships of Tarshish to go to Ophir for gold, but they did not go, for the ships were broken at Ezion-geber.

50 Then Ahaziah son of Ahab said to Jehoshaphat, "Let my servants go with your servants in the ships." But Jehoshaphat would not.

51 Jehoshaphat slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of David his father, and Jehoram his son reigned in his place.

52 Ahaziah son of Ahab began to reign over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigned two years over Israel.

53 He did what was evil in the eyes of Yahweh, and walked in the way of his father, in the way of his mother, and in the way of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who made Israel sin.

54 He served Baal and bowed down to him, and provoked Yahweh, the God of Israel, to anger, according to all that his father had done.

Clear English Bible — 2 Kings (Chapters 1–25): A Clear English Translation

This completes the Masoretic book of 2 Kings in this edition. The remaining books of the Old Testament stand in this edition as a clear-English modernization of the World English Bible (WEB) Classic text named in the front matter, except the books the front matter names as fresh translations made directly from the Hebrew; the New Testament stands on the Greek text named there. The book as printed here stands as DRAFT — NOT PUBLISHED.

Insertion record — 24 November 2026. The Masoretic book of 2 Kings (25 chapters, 719 verses) was inserted as a fresh translation made directly from the Masoretic Hebrew under Robert Tilford's Fresh Tanakh commission ruling of 23 November 2026 and its authorization-forward amendment, confirmed the same day, replacing the earlier WEB-based text of the book. The book carries one seam against the numbering it replaces, at a chapter boundary only: the Masoretic chapter 11 counts 20 verses and chapter 12 counts 22, against the English scheme's 21 and 21, because the verse the Masoretic text numbers 12:1 ("Jehoash was seven years old when he began to reign") stands in the English scheme as 11:21, and Masoretic 12:2–22 stand at the numbers the English scheme numbers 12:1–21 — so the block is reseated to the Masoretic numbering throughout, and the block header is unchanged. (The wave brief expected 854 verses in the English scheme; the ground check found 719 in both Masoretic witnesses, in JPS 1917 as printed, and in the seated block, and the build stands on the ground count.) The ground check before the build settled what the seated text was: a clear-English modernization of the World English Bible Classic in all three files, the Masoretic book alone, one identical draft-history hash in all three; no target carries any second form of the book, and the Daniel/Esther caution was not triggered. The translation was built in six reviser passes (chapters 1–4; 5–8; 9–12; 13–17; 18–21; 22–25) from the Masoretic text as it stands in the Westminster Leningrad Codex and Sefaria's Miqra according to the Masorah — the two witnesses consonant-exact in 629 of the book's 719 verses, the 90 divergences classified in the build record (50 ketiv/qere presentations, the qere printed; 20 spelling only; 1 encoding only; 6 verses where the Sefaria stream carries whole words the WLC stream does not, at 2:16, 3:24, 6:25, 16:6, 22:5 and 23:10; 1 Bolls initial-letter drop, at 14:9, where the draft follows Sefaria and the controls; and 12 mixed forms — at the fuller-Sefaria and mixed seats the draft follows the WLC as primary witness and the division is recorded in the open seats) — with JPS 1917 as the open control of record. Six independent checker passes that did not build the text read the draft against the Hebrew line and both controls: C1 (chapters 1–4) returned 114 PASS and no errors; C2 (5–8) 108 PASS and 1 error; C3 (9–12) 115 PASS and no errors; C4 (13–17) 151 PASS and 2 errors; C5 (18–21) 120 PASS and 1 error; C6 (22–25) 105 PASS and 2 errors — 713 verses passed as built, and the six errors (5:12, where the draft had printed the ketiv "Amanah" for the qere "Abanah"; 13:16, where "draw the bow" misread the Hebrew's "put your hand on the bow"; 14:2, where the queen mother's name stood as "Jehoaddan" for "Jehoaddin"; 18:27, where the draft had printed the plain "urine" against the qere's "the waters of their feet"; 23:24, where "the household gods" put a God-word in a verse whose designation target is none — the Hebrew is the teraphim; and 23:29, where the draft's pronouns made Josiah the killer where the Hebrew has Pharaoh Necoh kill Josiah) were corrected with the checkers' exact replacement texts and the whole book re-verified by count. One further correction is the desk's own, recorded openly in the check report: at 17:31 the draft had followed the ketiv's singular "the god of Sepharvaim" where both witnesses' qere reads the plural, and the seat had been double-counted in the build's first target-setting; the count gate caught the discrepancy, the draft now prints the qere "the gods of Sepharvaim", and the book's designation total is 98, not the 99 first asserted. The divine name יהוה stands 277 times in the book — no banked benchmark existed, so the counts were established from both witnesses before the build, by token-level analysis of the pointed text, the two witnesses agreeing at every verse — and prints "Yahweh" at exactly those seats; the seated WEB-based block counted 278, its one extra standing at 23:19, where the Masoretic text names no one. The designation אלהים in all its forms stands 98 times (אלהים 54; אלהי 25; אלהיך 3; אלהיו 4; אלהינו 2; אלהיהם 8; אלהיכם 2), printing "God" or "gods" — at 17:31 the count rests on the qere, the ketiv reading the singular אֱלֹהּ. The divine name אל has no designation seat in this book: its ten pointed tsere tokens in each witness are all the place name Beth-el (2:2, twice; 2:3; 2:23; 10:29; 17:28; 23:4; 23:15; 23:17; 23:19); and the bare אלה-cores are none of them the designation — אֵלֶּה, "these", the name אֵלָה, Elah (15:30; 17:1; 18:1; 18:9), אֲלֵהֶם, "to them", and יִזְרְעֶאלָה, Jezreel with the locative he — each settled by pointed inspection. The name שדי does not occur in 2 Kings as a divine name in either witness: the book's eight שדי-strings are all כַּשְׂדִּים, "the Chaldeans" (24:2; 25:4; 25:5; 25:10; 25:13; 25:24; 25:25; 25:26), and the book prints no "the Almighty". "The Lord" stands at two seats of the divine name אֲדֹנָי, both with the qamats pointing in both witnesses: 7:6 ("the Lord had made the camp of Aram hear a sound of chariots") and 19:23 (on the lips of Sennacherib's messengers, "you have mocked the Lord"). Every other "lord" in the book addresses or names a man — "my lord" to Elisha and to the king, "your lord" of Elijah (2:3; 2:5; 2:16; 9:7; 18:27), "his lord" of Naaman and of Hezekiah, "their lord" (6:22; 6:23), "your [plural] lord" (10:2; 10:3; 10:6; 19:6) — and prints lowercase throughout. No standalone יהּ seat stands in the book. The directed seats stand as the commission named them: chapter 2 entire (Elijah's ascent — the chariot and horses of fire at 2:11, Elisha's cry at 2:12, and the youths and the bears at 2:23–24 exactly as the Masoretic text stands); chapters 4–5 entire (the widow's oil; the Shunammite's son; Naaman's washing; Gehazi's sentence; and at 5:18 the Rimmon plea as it stands); chapter 17 entire (the fall of Samaria and the indictment at full force); chapters 18–20 entire (the Rabshakeh's speech at full force, 18:27 in the qere's terms; the angel of Yahweh at 19:35; the shadow on the steps at 20:9–11; the Babylonian envoys as they stand); chapters 22–23 entire (the book of the law found; Huldah's oracle; Josiah's reform at full force); and chapters 24–25 entire (Zedekiah blinded at 25:7, the temple burned and stripped at 25:8–17, Gedaliah, and Jehoiachin lifted up at 25:27–30, all exactly as the Masoretic text stands). The difference ledger records 660 of the book's 719 verses as differing in wording from both controls (33 differing from JPS 1917 only, 8 from the seated text only, 18 identical to both), and 38 open seats stand recorded, headed by the one Bolls drop, the 67 ketiv/qere seats, the witness divisions at 18 seats, and the 17:31 ketiv/qere seat with its corrected count. Build record: PACKET-2KINGS.md, LEDGER-2KINGS.md, CHECK-REPORT-2KINGS.md, and OPEN-SEATS-2KINGS.md in the desk's working folder (.tools/fresh-2kings/); the reader draft stands at ~/workspace/your_files/2-KINGS-FRESH-FROM-HEBREW-DRAFT-2026-11-24.md. The book stands as DRAFT — NOT PUBLISHED.

Draft history — 25 October 2026. 2 Kings chapters 1–25 were all internally audited (AUDITED), formerly stood as drafts awaiting Robert's read-through, and were formerly labeled a partial draft, unpublished. The completion statement above was substituted for the former draft header in the final handling under Ruling 20, after the campaign's rulings had been applied and verified; the former header's history is preserved here and in the repository history.

2 Kings 1

1 Moab rebelled against Israel after Ahab died.

2 Ahaziah fell through the lattice of his upper room in Samaria and was injured, and he sent messengers and told them, "Go and consult Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron, whether I will recover from this injury."

3 But an angel of Yahweh spoke to Elijah the Tishbite: "Get up, go up to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria, and say to them, 'Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are going to consult Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron?'

4 Therefore Yahweh says this: 'The bed you have gone up to, you will not come down from it, for you will surely die.'" And Elijah went.

5 The messengers came back to him, and he said to them, "Why have you come back?"

6 They told him, "A man came up to meet us and said to us, 'Go, return to the king who sent you, and say to him, "Yahweh says this: Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are sending to consult Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron? Therefore the bed you have gone up to, you will not come down from it, for you will surely die."'"

7 He said to them, "What did the man look like who came up to meet you and spoke these words to you?"

8 They answered him, "A hairy man, with a leather belt fastened around his waist." He said, "It is Elijah the Tishbite."

9 Then he sent to him a commander of fifty with his fifty men. He went up to him, and there he was, sitting on the top of the hill. He said to him, "Man of God, the king has spoken: 'Come down.'"

10 Elijah answered and said to the commander of fifty, "If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty." And fire came down from heaven and consumed him and his fifty.

11 Again he sent to him another commander of fifty with his fifty. He spoke up and said to him, "Man of God, the king has said this: 'Come down at once.'"

12 Elijah answered and said to them, "If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty." And fire of God came down from heaven and consumed him and his fifty.

13 Again he sent a third commander of fifty with his fifty. The third commander of fifty went up, came and knelt on his knees before Elijah, pleaded with him, and said to him, "Man of God, please let my life and the lives of these fifty servants of yours be precious in your eyes.

14 See, fire has come down from heaven and consumed the first two commanders of fifty with their fifties; but now let my life be precious in your eyes."

15 The angel of Yahweh said to Elijah, "Go down with him; do not be afraid of him." So he got up and went down with him to the king.

16 He said to him, "Yahweh says this: 'Because you sent messengers to consult Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron — is it because there is no God in Israel to consult his word? — therefore the bed you have gone up to, you will not come down from it, for you will surely die.'"

17 So he died, according to the word of Yahweh that Elijah had spoken. Jehoram reigned in his place, in the second year of Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, because he had no son.

18 The rest of the acts of Ahaziah that he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

2 Kings 2

1 When Yahweh was about to take Elijah up to heaven in a whirlwind, Elijah and Elisha were on their way from Gilgal.

2 Elijah said to Elisha, "Stay here, please, for Yahweh has sent me as far as Beth-el." Elisha said, "As Yahweh lives and as you yourself live, I will not leave you." So they went down to Beth-el.

3 The sons of the prophets who were at Beth-el came out to Elisha and said to him, "Do you know that today Yahweh is taking your lord away from over your head?" He said, "Yes, I know it; be silent."

4 Elijah said to him, "Elisha, stay here, please, for Yahweh has sent me to Jericho." He said, "As Yahweh lives and as you yourself live, I will not leave you." So they came to Jericho.

5 The sons of the prophets who were at Jericho drew near to Elisha and said to him, "Do you know that today Yahweh is taking your lord away from over your head?" He answered, "Yes, I know it; be silent."

6 Elijah said to him, "Stay here, please, for Yahweh has sent me to the Jordan." He said, "As Yahweh lives and as you yourself live, I will not leave you." So the two of them went on.

7 Fifty men of the sons of the prophets went and stood opposite them at a distance, while the two of them stood by the Jordan.

8 Elijah took his cloak, rolled it up, and struck the waters, and they parted to one side and the other, and the two of them crossed over on dry ground.

9 When they had crossed, Elijah said to Elisha, "Ask what I should do for you before I am taken from you." Elisha said, "Please let a double portion of your spirit come to me."

10 He said, "You have asked a hard thing. If you see me as I am taken from you, it will be so for you; but if not, it will not be so."

11 As they went on, walking and talking, suddenly a chariot of fire and horses of fire separated the two of them, and Elijah went up in a whirlwind to heaven.

12 Elisha saw it and cried out, "My father, my father, the chariot of Israel and its horsemen!" And he saw him no more. He took hold of his own clothes and tore them into two pieces.

13 He picked up Elijah's cloak that had fallen from him, went back, and stood on the bank of the Jordan.

14 He took Elijah's cloak that had fallen from him, struck the waters, and said, "Where is Yahweh, the God of Elijah?" He too struck the waters, and they parted to one side and the other, and Elisha crossed over.

15 When the sons of the prophets who were at Jericho saw him from opposite, they said, "The spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha." They came to meet him and bowed to the ground before him.

16 They said to him, "Look, there are fifty able men with your servants. Please let them go and look for your lord, in case the spirit of Yahweh has lifted him up and thrown him down on one of the mountains or into one of the valleys." He said, "Do not send them."

17 They pressed him until he was embarrassed, and he said, "Send them." They sent fifty men, and they searched for three days but did not find him.

18 They returned to him while he was staying at Jericho, and he said to them, "Did I not tell you, 'Do not go'?"

19 The men of the city said to Elisha, "Look, the site of this city is good, as my lord sees, but the water is bad and the land causes miscarriage."

20 He said, "Bring me a new bowl and put salt in it." They brought it to him.

21 He went out to the spring of the waters, threw salt there, and said, "Yahweh says this: 'I have healed these waters; from now on there will be no more death or miscarriage from them.'"

22 So the waters have remained healed to this day, according to the word Elisha spoke.

23 He went up from there to Beth-el. As he was going up on the road, some young boys came out of the city, jeered at him, and said to him, "Go up, baldhead! Go up, baldhead!"

24 He turned behind him, saw them, and cursed them in the name of Yahweh. Then two she-bears came out of the forest and tore apart forty-two of the children.

25 He went from there to Mount Carmel, and from there he returned to Samaria.

2 Kings 3

1 Jehoram son of Ahab became king over Israel in Samaria in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, and he reigned twelve years.

2 He did what was evil in the eyes of Yahweh, though not like his father and his mother, for he removed the pillar of Baal that his father had made.

3 Yet he clung to the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, with which he made Israel sin; he did not turn away from them.

4 Mesha, king of Moab, was a sheep breeder, and he paid the king of Israel one hundred thousand lambs and the wool of one hundred thousand rams.

5 When Ahab died, the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.

6 King Jehoram went out of Samaria at that time and mustered all Israel.

7 He went and sent to Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, saying, "The king of Moab has rebelled against me. Will you go with me to Moab to fight?" He said, "I will go up; I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses."

8 He said, "By which road shall we go up?" He answered, "By the road of the wilderness of Edom."

9 The king of Israel, the king of Judah, and the king of Edom went, and they made a roundabout journey of seven days, and there was no water for the camp or for the animals that followed them.

10 The king of Israel said, "Alas, Yahweh has called these three kings together to give them into the hand of Moab."

11 Jehoshaphat said, "Is there no prophet of Yahweh here, through whom we may inquire of Yahweh?" One of the servants of the king of Israel answered and said, "Elisha son of Shaphat is here, who poured water on Elijah's hands."

12 Jehoshaphat said, "The word of Yahweh is with him." So the king of Israel, Jehoshaphat, and the king of Edom went down to him.

13 Elisha said to the king of Israel, "What have I to do with you? Go to your father's prophets and to your mother's prophets." The king of Israel said to him, "No, for Yahweh has called these three kings together to give them into the hand of Moab."

14 Elisha said, "As Yahweh of hosts lives, before whom I stand, if it were not that I regard Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, I would not look at you or see you.

15 But now bring me a musician." When the musician played, the hand of Yahweh came upon him.

16 He said, "Yahweh says this: 'Make this valley full of ditches, ditch after ditch.'

17 For Yahweh says this: 'You will see no wind and you will see no rain, yet this valley will fill with water, and you will drink, you and your livestock and your animals.'

18 This is a light thing in the eyes of Yahweh; he will also give Moab into your hand.

19 You will strike every fortified city and every choice city, fell every good tree, stop up every spring of water, and ruin every good plot of land with stones."

20 In the morning, at the time of the offering, water suddenly came from the direction of Edom, and the land filled with water.

21 All Moab heard that the kings had come up to fight against them, and everyone old enough to gird on a belt and upward was summoned, and they stood at the border.

22 They rose early in the morning, and the sun shone on the water, and the Moabites saw the water opposite them red as blood.

23 They said, "This is blood. The kings have surely destroyed one another and struck each other down. Now, Moab, to the spoil!"

24 They came to the camp of Israel, and Israel rose and struck Moab, and they fled before them. They pressed in and struck Moab down.

25 They tore down the cities; on every good plot of land each man threw his stone and filled it; they stopped up every spring of water and felled every good tree, until only its stones were left at Kir-hareseth, and the slingers surrounded it and struck it.

26 When the king of Moab saw that the battle was too strong for him, he took with him seven hundred men who drew the sword, to break through to the king of Edom, but they could not.

27 He took his firstborn son, who was to reign in his place, and offered him up as a burnt offering on the wall. And great wrath came upon Israel, and they withdrew from him and returned to the land.

2 Kings 4

1 A certain woman, one of the wives of the sons of the prophets, cried out to Elisha, saying, "Your servant, my husband, is dead. You know that your servant feared Yahweh. The creditor has come to take my two children for himself as slaves."

2 Elisha said to her, "What can I do for you? Tell me, what do you have in the house?" She said, "Your servant has nothing at all in the house except a flask of oil."

3 He said, "Go, borrow vessels for yourself from outside, from all your neighbors, empty vessels; do not borrow few.

4 Then come in and shut the door behind you and behind your sons, and pour into all these vessels, and set aside each one that is full."

5 She left him, shut the door behind her and behind her sons; they kept bringing the vessels to her, and she kept pouring.

6 When the vessels were full, she said to her son, "Bring me another vessel." He said to her, "There is no vessel left." And the oil stopped.

7 She came and told the man of God. He said, "Go, sell the oil and pay your debt, and you and your sons shall live on what is left."

8 One day Elisha passed through Shunem, where there was a prominent woman, and she pressed him to eat food. Whenever he passed by, he would turn in there to eat food.

9 She said to her husband, "Look, I know that this is a holy man of God who passes by us regularly.

10 Please let us make a small walled upper room and put there for him a bed, a table, a chair, and a lamp, and when he comes to us he can turn in there."

11 One day he came there, turned into the upper room, and lay down there.

12 He said to Gehazi, his servant, "Call this Shunammite." He called her, and she stood before him.

13 He said to him, "Say to her now, 'Look, you have taken all this trouble for us. What can be done for you? Shall I speak for you to the king or to the commander of the army?'" She answered, "I live among my own people."

14 He said, "What, then, can be done for her?" Gehazi answered, "Well, she has no son, and her husband is old."

15 He said, "Call her." He called her, and she stood in the doorway.

16 He said, "At this appointed time, about this time next year, you will embrace a son." She said, "No, my lord, man of God, do not deceive your servant."

17 The woman conceived and bore a son at that appointed time, about that time the next year, as Elisha had told her.

18 The child grew. One day he went out to his father, to the reapers.

19 He said to his father, "My head, my head!" He said to the servant, "Carry him to his mother."

20 He lifted him and brought him to his mother. He sat on her knees until noon, and died.

21 She went up, laid him on the bed of the man of God, shut the door on him, and went out.

22 She called to her husband and said, "Please send me one of the servants and one of the donkeys, so that I can run to the man of God and come back."

23 He said, "Why are you going to him today? It is neither new moon nor Sabbath." She said, "It is well."

24 She saddled the donkey and said to her servant, "Drive on and go; do not hold back my riding unless I tell you."

25 She went and came to the man of God at Mount Carmel. When the man of God saw her from a distance, he said to Gehazi, his servant, "Look, there is that Shunammite.

26 Now run, please, to meet her and say to her, 'Is it well with you? Is it well with your husband? Is it well with the child?'" She answered, "It is well."

27 She came to the man of God at the hill and took hold of his feet. Gehazi came near to push her away, but the man of God said, "Leave her alone, for her soul is bitter within her, and Yahweh has hidden it from me and has not told me."

28 She said, "Did I ask for a son from my lord? Did I not say, 'Do not deceive me'?"

29 He said to Gehazi, "Gird up your loins, take my staff in your hand, and go. If you meet a man, do not greet him, and if a man greets you, do not answer him. Lay my staff on the boy's face."

30 The boy's mother said, "As Yahweh lives and as you yourself live, I will not leave you." So he got up and followed her.

31 Gehazi passed on ahead of them and laid the staff on the boy's face, but there was no sound and no sign of attention. He went back to meet him and told him, saying, "The boy has not awakened."

32 Elisha came into the house, and there was the boy, dead, laid on his bed.

33 He went in, shut the door behind the two of them, and prayed to Yahweh.

34 He went up and lay on the child, put his mouth on his mouth, his eyes on his eyes, and his hands on his hands, and stretched himself over him, and the child's flesh became warm.

35 He got up again, walked once here and once there in the house, went up, and stretched himself over him. The boy sneezed seven times, and the boy opened his eyes.

36 He called Gehazi and said, "Call this Shunammite." He called her, and she came to him. He said, "Lift up your son."

37 She came, fell at his feet, and bowed to the ground. She lifted up her son and went out.

38 Elisha returned to Gilgal. There was a famine in the land, and the sons of the prophets were sitting before him. He said to his servant, "Set on the large pot and boil stew for the sons of the prophets."

39 One went out into the field to gather greens, found a wild vine, gathered wild gourds from it, a lapful, came and sliced them into the pot of stew, for they did not know what they were.

40 They poured it out for the men to eat. As they ate from the stew, they cried out and said, "Man of God, there is death in the pot!" And they could not eat it.

41 He said, "Bring flour." He threw it into the pot and said, "Pour it out for the people, and let them eat." And there was nothing harmful in the pot.

42 A man came from Baal-shalishah and brought the man of God bread of the firstfruits, twenty loaves of barley and fresh grain in his sack. He said, "Give it to the people, and let them eat."

43 His servant said, "How can I set this before a hundred men?" He said, "Give it to the people, and let them eat, for Yahweh says this: 'They shall eat and have some left.'"

44 He set it before them, and they ate and had some left, according to the word of Yahweh.

2 Kings 5

1 Naaman, commander of the army of the king of Aram, was a great man before his lord and held in high esteem, because through him Yahweh had given victory to Aram; the man was a mighty warrior, but he had leprosy.

2 Aramean raiding bands had gone out and taken captive a young girl from the land of Israel, and she served Naaman's wife.

3 She said to her mistress, "If only my lord were with the prophet who is in Samaria! Then he would cure him of his leprosy."

4 Naaman went in and told his lord, saying, "This is what the girl from the land of Israel said."

5 The king of Aram said, "Go, and I will send a letter to the king of Israel." So he set out and took with him ten talents of silver, six thousand pieces of gold, and ten changes of clothing.

6 He brought the letter to the king of Israel; it said, "When this letter reaches you, see, I have sent my servant Naaman to you, so that you may cure him of his leprosy."

7 When the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his clothes and said, "Am I God, able to kill and to make alive, that this man sends to me to cure a man of his leprosy? Just consider and see how he is picking a quarrel with me."

8 When Elisha the man of God heard that the king of Israel had torn his clothes, he sent to the king, saying, "Why have you torn your clothes? Let him come to me, and he will know that there is a prophet in Israel."

9 So Naaman came with his horses and his chariots and stood at the entrance of Elisha's house.

10 Elisha sent a messenger to him, saying, "Go and wash in the Jordan seven times, and your flesh will be restored to you, and you will be clean."

11 But Naaman grew angry and went away, saying, "See, I thought he would surely come out to me, stand, and call on the name of Yahweh his God, and wave his hand over the place, and cure the leper."

12 "Are not Abanah and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? Could I not wash in them and be clean?" So he turned and went off in a rage.

13 His servants came near and spoke to him, saying, "My father, if the prophet had told you to do some great thing, would you not have done it? How much more, then, when he tells you, 'Wash, and be clean'?"

14 So he went down and dipped himself seven times in the Jordan, as the man of God had said, and his flesh was restored like the flesh of a young boy, and he was clean.

15 He returned to the man of God, he and his whole company, and he came and stood before him and said, "See now, I know that there is no God in all the earth except in Israel; so please accept a gift from your servant."

16 But he said, "As Yahweh lives, before whom I stand, I will accept nothing." Naaman urged him to take it, but he refused.

17 Naaman said, "If not, please let your servant be given two mules' load of earth, for your servant will no longer offer burnt offering or sacrifice to other gods, but only to Yahweh."

18 "In this one thing may Yahweh pardon your servant: when my master goes into the house of Rimmon to bow down there, leaning on my hand, and I bow down in the house of Rimmon — when I bow down in the house of Rimmon, may Yahweh pardon your servant in this thing."

19 He said to him, "Go in peace." So Naaman departed from him and went some distance.

20 Gehazi, the servant of Elisha the man of God, said, "See, my master has spared this Naaman the Aramean by not accepting from his hand what he brought. As Yahweh lives, I will run after him and get something from him."

21 So Gehazi hurried after Naaman. When Naaman saw someone running after him, he got down from the chariot to meet him and said, "Is all well?"

22 He said, "All is well. My master has sent me, saying, 'See, just now two young men from the hill country of Ephraim, from the sons of the prophets, have come to me; please give them a talent of silver and two changes of clothing.'"

23 Naaman said, "Please, take two talents." He pressed him, and tied up two talents of silver in two bags, with two changes of clothing, and gave them to two of his servants, and they carried them before Gehazi.

24 When he came to the hill, he took them from their hand and stored them in the house; then he sent the men away, and they departed.

25 He went in and stood before his lord, and Elisha said to him, "Where have you been, Gehazi?" He said, "Your servant has not gone anywhere."

26 He said to him, "Did my heart not go with you when a man turned back from his chariot to meet you? Is this a time to accept silver, and to accept clothing, olive groves and vineyards, sheep and cattle, male servants and female servants?

27 So Naaman's leprosy will cling to you and to your descendants forever." And he went out from his presence leprous, white as snow.

2 Kings 6

1 The sons of the prophets said to Elisha, "See now, the place where we live before you is too cramped for us.

2 Let us go to the Jordan, and each of us take a beam from there, and let us make a place for ourselves there to live in." He said, "Go."

3 One of them said, "Please be willing to go with your servants." He said, "I will go."

4 So he went with them. When they came to the Jordan, they began cutting down trees.

5 As one of them was felling a beam, the iron ax head fell into the water, and he cried out and said, "Alas, my lord! It was borrowed."

6 The man of God said, "Where did it fall?" He showed him the place. He cut off a stick, threw it in there, and made the iron float.

7 He said, "Lift it out for yourself." So he reached out his hand and took it.

8 The king of Aram was at war with Israel, and he took counsel with his servants, saying, "My camp will be at such and such a place."

9 The man of God sent word to the king of Israel, saying, "Take care not to pass through that place, for the Arameans are coming down there."

10 The king of Israel sent men to the place that the man of God had told him about and warned him of, and he kept watch there — not once, and not twice.

11 The heart of the king of Aram was greatly troubled over this, and he called his servants and said to them, "Will you not tell me which of our men is on the side of the king of Israel?"

12 One of his servants said, "No one, my lord, O king; but Elisha, the prophet who is in Israel, tells the king of Israel the very words you speak in your bedroom."

13 He said, "Go and find out where he is, so that I can send men and seize him." He was told, "See, he is in Dothan."

14 So he sent horses and chariots and a strong force there; they came by night and surrounded the city.

15 When the servant of the man of God rose early and went out, there was an army surrounding the city, with horses and chariots. His servant said to him, "Alas, my lord! What shall we do?"

16 He said, "Do not be afraid, for those who are with us are more than those who are with them."

17 Elisha prayed and said, "Yahweh, please open his eyes, so that he may see." And Yahweh opened the young man's eyes, and he saw: the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.

18 When they came down toward him, Elisha prayed to Yahweh and said, "Please strike this people with blindness." And he struck them with blindness, as Elisha had asked.

19 Elisha said to them, "This is not the way, and this is not the city. Follow me, and I will lead you to the man you are looking for." And he led them to Samaria.

20 When they had come into Samaria, Elisha said, "Yahweh, open the eyes of these men, so that they may see." Yahweh opened their eyes, and they saw, and there they were in the middle of Samaria.

21 When the king of Israel saw them, he said to Elisha, "My father, shall I strike them down? Shall I strike them down?"

22 He said, "You shall not strike them down. Would you strike down those you have taken captive with your sword and your bow? Set bread and water before them, so that they may eat and drink and go back to their lord."

23 So he prepared a great feast for them, and when they had eaten and drunk, he sent them away, and they went to their lord. And Aramean raiding bands no longer came into the land of Israel.

24 After this, Ben-hadad king of Aram gathered his whole army, went up, and besieged Samaria.

25 There was a great famine in Samaria while they besieged it, until a donkey's head sold for eighty pieces of silver, and a quarter of a kab of dove's dung for five pieces of silver.

26 As the king of Israel was passing by on the wall, a woman cried out to him, saying, "Help me, my lord, O king!"

27 He said, "If Yahweh does not help you, where can I find help for you? From the threshing floor, or from the winepress?"

28 The king said to her, "What is wrong?" She said, "This woman said to me, 'Give up your son, so that we may eat him today, and we will eat my son tomorrow.'

29 So we boiled my son and ate him. The next day I said to her, 'Give up your son, so that we may eat him,' but she has hidden her son."

30 When the king heard the woman's words, he tore his clothes. As he passed by on the wall, the people saw that he was wearing sackcloth underneath, against his skin.

31 He said, "May God do so to me, and more also, if the head of Elisha son of Shaphat remains on him today."

32 Elisha was sitting in his house, and the elders were sitting with him. The king sent a man ahead of him, but before the messenger reached him, Elisha said to the elders, "Do you see that this son of a murderer has sent someone to take off my head? See to it: when the messenger comes, shut the door and hold it shut against him. Is not the sound of his master's feet behind him?"

33 While he was still speaking with them, the messenger came down to him, and he said, "See, this disaster has come from Yahweh. Why should I wait for Yahweh any longer?"

2 Kings 7

1 Elisha said, "Hear the word of Yahweh. This is what Yahweh says: 'Tomorrow at about this time, a seah of fine flour will sell for a shekel, and two seahs of barley for a shekel, at the gate of Samaria.'"

2 The officer on whose hand the king leaned answered the man of God and said, "Even if Yahweh were to make windows in heaven, could this happen?" He said, "You will see it with your own eyes, but you will not eat any of it."

3 Four men with leprosy were at the entrance of the gate, and they said to one another, "Why should we sit here until we die?

4 If we say, 'We will go into the city,' the famine is in the city and we will die there; and if we stay here, we will die too. So come, let us go over to the camp of the Arameans. If they let us live, we will live; and if they kill us, we will only die."

5 They rose at twilight to go to the camp of the Arameans. When they reached the edge of the Aramean camp, there was no one there.

6 For the Lord had made the camp of the Arameans hear the sound of chariots, the sound of horses, the sound of a great army, and they said to one another, "See, the king of Israel has hired the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Egypt to come against us."

7 So they rose and fled in the twilight, leaving their tents, their horses, and their donkeys — the camp just as it was — and fled for their lives.

8 When these men with leprosy came to the edge of the camp, they went into one tent, ate and drank, and carried off silver, gold, and clothing from there, and went and hid them. Then they returned, went into another tent, carried things off from there, and went and hid them.

9 Then they said to one another, "We are not doing right. This day is a day of good news, and we are keeping silent. If we wait until morning light, we will be found guilty. So come, let us go and tell the king's household."

10 They came and called to the gatekeepers of the city and told them, saying, "We went to the camp of the Arameans, and there was no one there, not even a human voice — only the horses tied up, the donkeys tied up, and the tents just as they were."

11 The gatekeepers called out and reported it inside, to the king's household.

12 The king rose in the night and said to his servants, "Let me tell you what the Arameans have done to us. They know that we are hungry, so they have left the camp to hide in the open country, saying, 'When they come out of the city, we will take them alive and get into the city.'"

13 One of his servants answered and said, "Let some men take five of the remaining horses that are left in the city — see, they are like the whole multitude of Israel that is left in it; see, they are like the whole multitude of Israel that has perished — and let us send men and see."

14 So they took two chariots with horses, and the king sent them after the Aramean camp, saying, "Go and see."

15 They went after them as far as the Jordan, and the whole road was strewn with clothing and gear that the Arameans had thrown away in their haste. The messengers returned and told the king.

16 Then the people went out and plundered the camp of the Arameans. So a seah of fine flour sold for a shekel, and two seahs of barley for a shekel, according to the word of Yahweh.

17 The king had put the officer on whose hand he leaned in charge of the gate, and the people trampled him at the gate, and he died, just as the man of God had said when the king came down to him.

18 It happened just as the man of God had spoken to the king, saying, "Two seahs of barley for a shekel, and a seah of fine flour for a shekel, will be sold tomorrow at about this time at the gate of Samaria" —

19 and that officer had answered the man of God and said, "Even if Yahweh were to make windows in heaven, could such a thing happen?" and he had said, "You will see it with your own eyes, but you will not eat any of it" —

20 and so it happened to him: the people trampled him at the gate, and he died.

2 Kings 8

1 Elisha had spoken to the woman whose son he had brought back to life, saying, "Rise and go, you and your household, and live wherever you can as a foreigner, for Yahweh has called for a famine, and it will come on the land for seven years."

2 The woman rose and did as the man of God said. She went with her household and lived as a foreigner in the land of the Philistines for seven years.

3 At the end of the seven years, the woman returned from the land of the Philistines, and she went out to appeal to the king for her house and her land.

4 The king was talking with Gehazi, the servant of the man of God, saying, "Please tell me all the great things Elisha has done."

5 While he was telling the king how Elisha had brought the dead man back to life, the woman whose son he had brought back to life was appealing to the king for her house and her land. Gehazi said, "My lord, O king, this is the woman, and this is her son, whom Elisha brought back to life."

6 The king questioned the woman, and she told him. So the king assigned an officer to her, saying, "Restore everything that was hers, and all the produce of the field from the day she left the land until now."

7 Elisha came to Damascus. Ben-hadad, the king of Aram, was ill, and he was told, "The man of God has come here."

8 The king said to Hazael, "Take a gift in your hand and go to meet the man of God, and inquire of Yahweh through him, saying, 'Will I recover from this illness?'"

9 So Hazael went to meet him, taking a gift with him — all the fine goods of Damascus, a load for forty camels. He came and stood before him and said, "Your son Ben-hadad, king of Aram, has sent me to you, saying, 'Will I recover from this illness?'"

10 Elisha said to him, "Go and say to him, 'You will surely recover,' although Yahweh has shown me that he will surely die."

11 He fixed his gaze on him and stared until he was ashamed, and the man of God wept.

12 Hazael said, "Why is my lord weeping?" He said, "Because I know the harm you will do to the people of Israel: you will set their strongholds on fire, you will kill their young men with the sword, you will dash their little children to pieces, and you will rip open their pregnant women."

13 Hazael said, "What is your servant — a mere dog — that he should do this great thing?" Elisha said, "Yahweh has shown me you as king over Aram."

14 He left Elisha and came to his master, who said to him, "What did Elisha say to you?" He said, "He told me that you would surely recover."

15 The next day he took a thick cloth, dipped it in water, and spread it over his face, and he died. And Hazael became king in his place.

16 In the fifth year of Joram son of Ahab, king of Israel, while Jehoshaphat was king of Judah, Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, began to reign.

17 He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.

18 He walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as the house of Ahab had done, for Ahab's daughter was his wife, and he did what was evil in the eyes of Yahweh.

19 But Yahweh was not willing to destroy Judah, for the sake of David his servant, since he had promised to give him a lamp for his descendants always.

20 In his days Edom rebelled against the hand of Judah and set a king over themselves.

21 Joram crossed over to Zair with all his chariots. He rose by night and struck the Edomites who had surrounded him and the commanders of the chariots, and the troops fled to their tents.

22 So Edom has rebelled against the hand of Judah to this day. Libnah also rebelled at that same time.

23 The rest of the acts of Joram, and all that he did — are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?

24 Joram slept with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in the city of David, and his son Ahaziah became king in his place.

25 In the twelfth year of Joram son of Ahab, king of Israel, Ahaziah son of Jehoram, king of Judah, began to reign.

26 Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Athaliah, daughter of Omri, king of Israel.

27 He walked in the way of the house of Ahab and did what was evil in the eyes of Yahweh, as the house of Ahab had done, for he was a son-in-law of the house of Ahab.

28 He went with Joram son of Ahab to war against Hazael, king of Aram, at Ramoth-gilead, and the Arameans wounded Joram.

29 King Joram returned to Jezreel to be healed of the wounds the Arameans had given him at Ramah, when he fought against Hazael, king of Aram. And Ahaziah son of Jehoram, king of Judah, went down to see Joram son of Ahab in Jezreel, because he was ill.

2 Kings 9

1 Elisha the prophet called one of the sons of the prophets and said to him, "Tuck your cloak in at your waist, take this flask of oil in your hand, and go to Ramoth-gilead.

2 When you get there, look for Jehu son of Jehoshaphat son of Nimshi. Go in, make him stand up from among his companions, and bring him into an inner room.

3 Then take the flask of oil, pour it on his head, and say, 'This is what Yahweh says: I have anointed you king over Israel.' Then open the door and run; do not linger."

4 So the young man, the young prophet, went to Ramoth-gilead.

5 When he arrived, the commanders of the army were sitting together, and he said, "Commander, I have a word for you." Jehu said, "For which of us?" He said, "For you, commander."

6 Jehu rose and went into the house. The young man poured the oil on his head and said to him, "This is what Yahweh, the God of Israel, says: 'I have anointed you king over the people of Yahweh, over Israel.

7 You shall strike down the house of Ahab, your master, so that I may avenge on Jezebel the blood of my servants the prophets and the blood of all the servants of Yahweh.

8 The whole house of Ahab shall perish. I will cut off from Ahab every male, both bound and free in Israel.

9 I will make the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah.

10 The dogs shall eat Jezebel in the plot of ground at Jezreel, and no one shall bury her.'" Then he opened the door and fled.

11 Jehu came out to the servants of his master, and they said to him, "Is all well? Why did that madman come to you?" He said to them, "You know the man and the way he talks."

12 They said, "That is not true. Tell us." So he said, "He spoke to me like this: 'This is what Yahweh says: I have anointed you king over Israel.'"

13 At once each man took his cloak and put it under Jehu on the bare top of the steps. They blew the trumpet and said, "Jehu is king."

14 So Jehu son of Jehoshaphat son of Nimshi conspired against Joram. Now Joram had been keeping guard at Ramoth-gilead, he and all Israel, against Hazael king of Aram,

15 but King Joram had gone back to Jezreel to recover from the wounds the Arameans had given him when he fought Hazael king of Aram. Jehu said, "If this is your mind, let no one slip out of the city to go and tell the news in Jezreel."

16 Jehu mounted his chariot and went to Jezreel, for Joram was lying there, and Ahaziah king of Judah had come down to visit Joram.

17 The watchman standing on the tower in Jezreel saw Jehu's company as it came and said, "I see a company." Joram said, "Take a horseman, send him to meet them, and let him say, 'Do you come in peace?'"

18 The horseman rode to meet him and said, "This is what the king says: 'Do you come in peace?'" Jehu said, "What do you have to do with peace? Fall in behind me." The watchman reported, "The messenger reached them, but he is not coming back."

19 Joram sent a second horseman, who came to them and said, "This is what the king says: 'Do you come in peace?'" Jehu answered, "What do you have to do with peace? Fall in behind me."

20 The watchman reported, "He reached them, but he is not coming back. And the driving is like the driving of Jehu son of Nimshi, for he drives like a madman."

21 Joram said, "Harness up." His chariot was harnessed, and Joram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah went out, each in his chariot. They went out to meet Jehu and found him on the plot of ground of Naboth the Jezreelite.

22 When Joram saw Jehu, he said, "Do you come in peace, Jehu?" He answered, "What peace can there be, while your mother Jezebel's whorings and her many sorceries go on?"

23 Joram turned his hands and fled, saying to Ahaziah, "Treachery, Ahaziah!"

24 Jehu drew his bow with his full strength and struck Joram between the shoulders, so that the arrow went out through his heart, and he sank down in his chariot.

25 Jehu said to Bidkar, his officer, "Pick him up and throw him onto the plot of ground that belonged to Naboth the Jezreelite. Remember how you and I rode side by side behind his father Ahab, and Yahweh pronounced this oracle against him:

26 'I saw the blood of Naboth and the blood of his sons yesterday — the declaration of Yahweh — and I will repay you on this very plot of ground — the declaration of Yahweh.' So now pick him up and throw him onto the plot, according to the word of Yahweh."

27 When Ahaziah king of Judah saw this, he fled by the way of the garden house. Jehu pursued him and said, "Strike him too, in the chariot." They struck him at the ascent of Gur, near Ibleam, and he fled to Megiddo and died there.

28 His servants carried him by chariot to Jerusalem and buried him in his tomb with his fathers in the city of David.

29 In the eleventh year of Joram son of Ahab, Ahaziah had begun to reign over Judah.

30 Jehu came to Jezreel. Jezebel heard of it, put paint on her eyes, arranged her hair, and looked out of the window.

31 As Jehu entered the gate, she said, "Do you come in peace, Zimri, murderer of your master?"

32 He lifted his face toward the window and said, "Who is with me? Who?" Two or three eunuchs looked down at him.

33 He said, "Throw her down." They threw her down, and some of her blood spattered on the wall and on the horses, and he trampled her.

34 He went in, ate and drank, and then said, "See to that cursed woman and bury her, for she is a king's daughter."

35 They went to bury her, but they found nothing of her except the skull, the feet, and the palms of the hands.

36 They came back and told him. He said, "It is the word of Yahweh, which he spoke through his servant Elijah the Tishbite: 'On the plot of ground at Jezreel the dogs shall eat the flesh of Jezebel,

37 and Jezebel's corpse shall be like dung on the face of the field, on the plot at Jezreel, so that no one will say, This is Jezebel.'"

2 Kings 10

1 Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria. Jehu wrote letters and sent them to Samaria, to the rulers of Jezreel, the elders, and to those who were raising Ahab's sons, saying:

2 "Now, when this letter reaches you — your lord's sons are with you, and you have chariots and horses, a fortified city, and weapons —

3 pick out the best and most fit of your lord's sons, set him on his father's throne, and fight for your lord's house."

4 They were utterly terrified and said, "See, the two kings could not stand before him; how can we stand?"

5 The man over the household, the man over the city, the elders, and those raising the children sent to Jehu, saying, "We are your servants, and we will do everything you tell us. We will make no one king. Do what is good in your eyes."

6 He wrote them a second letter, saying, "If you are on my side and will obey my voice, take the heads of your lord's sons and come to me at Jezreel by this time tomorrow." Now the king's sons, seventy men, were with the great men of the city, who were raising them.

7 When the letter reached them, they took the king's sons, slaughtered the seventy men, put their heads in baskets, and sent them to him at Jezreel.

8 A messenger came and told him, "They have brought the heads of the king's sons." He said, "Lay them in two heaps at the entrance of the gate until morning."

9 In the morning he went out, stood, and said to all the people, "You are innocent. See, I conspired against my master and killed him, but who struck down all these?

10 Know, then, that nothing of the word of Yahweh shall fall to the ground, which Yahweh spoke against the house of Ahab, for Yahweh has done what he spoke through his servant Elijah."

11 So Jehu struck down all who remained of the house of Ahab in Jezreel, all his great men, his close friends, and his priests, until he left him no survivor.

12 He rose, set out, and went to Samaria. On the way, at Beth-eked of the shepherds,

13 Jehu met the brothers of Ahaziah king of Judah and said, "Who are you?" They answered, "We are the brothers of Ahaziah. We have come down to greet the sons of the king and the sons of the queen mother."

14 He said, "Take them alive." They took them alive and slaughtered them at the pit of Beth-eked, forty-two men, and he left none of them alive.

15 He went on from there and found Jehonadab son of Rechab coming to meet him. He greeted him and said to him, "Is your heart true to me, as my heart is to yours?" Jehonadab answered, "It is." "If it is, give me your hand." He gave him his hand, and Jehu took him up into the chariot with him.

16 He said, "Come with me and see my zeal for Yahweh." And he had him ride in his chariot.

17 When he came to Samaria, he struck down all who remained to Ahab in Samaria until he had destroyed them, according to the word of Yahweh that he spoke to Elijah.

18 Jehu gathered all the people and said to them, "Ahab served Baal a little; Jehu will serve him much more.

19 Now call to me all the prophets of Baal, all his worshipers, and all his priests. Let no one be missing, for I have a great sacrifice for Baal; whoever is missing shall not live." But Jehu was acting with cunning, in order to destroy the worshipers of Baal.

20 Jehu said, "Consecrate a solemn assembly for Baal." And they proclaimed it.

21 Jehu sent through all Israel, and all the worshipers of Baal came; there was not a man left who did not come. They entered the house of Baal, and the house of Baal was filled from end to end.

22 He said to the man in charge of the wardrobe, "Bring out garments for all the worshipers of Baal." And he brought out garments for them.

23 Jehu and Jehonadab son of Rechab entered the house of Baal. He said to the worshipers of Baal, "Search and make sure that none of the servants of Yahweh is here with you, but only the worshipers of Baal."

24 They went in to offer sacrifices and burnt offerings. Jehu had stationed eighty men outside and said, "If any of the men whom I am putting into your hands escapes, the one who lets him go shall pay with his own life for that life."

25 As soon as he had finished offering the burnt offering, Jehu said to the guards and the officers, "Go in and strike them down; let no one come out." They struck them with the edge of the sword, and the guards and officers threw the bodies out. Then they went into the inner part of the house of Baal.

26 They brought out the pillars from the house of Baal and burned them.

27 They broke down the pillar of Baal, broke down the house of Baal, and made it a latrine, as it is to this day.

28 So Jehu wiped out Baal from Israel.

29 But Jehu did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, which he caused Israel to commit — the golden calves that were in Beth-el and in Dan.

30 Yahweh said to Jehu, "Because you have done well in carrying out what is right in my eyes, and have done to the house of Ahab all that was in my heart, your sons to the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Israel."

31 But Jehu was not careful to walk in the law of Yahweh, the God of Israel, with all his heart. He did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam, which he caused Israel to commit.

32 In those days Yahweh began to trim Israel down, and Hazael struck them throughout all the territory of Israel,

33 from the Jordan eastward, all the land of Gilead — the Gadites, the Reubenites, and the Manassites — from Aroer, which is by the valley of the Arnon, including Gilead and Bashan.

34 The rest of the acts of Jehu, all that he did, and all his might — are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

35 Jehu slept with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria. Jehoahaz his son reigned in his place.

36 The days Jehu reigned over Israel in Samaria were twenty-eight years.

2 Kings 11

1 When Athaliah, the mother of Ahaziah, saw that her son was dead, she rose and destroyed all the offspring of the kingdom.

2 But Jehosheba, daughter of King Joram and sister of Ahaziah, took Joash son of Ahaziah and stole him away from among the king's sons who were being put to death — him and his nurse — into a bedroom. They hid him from Athaliah, so he was not put to death.

3 He stayed with her, hidden in the house of Yahweh, for six years, while Athaliah reigned over the land.

4 In the seventh year Jehoiada sent and brought the commanders of the hundreds, of the Carites and of the guards, and brought them to himself in the house of Yahweh. He made a covenant with them and put them under oath in the house of Yahweh, and he showed them the king's son.

5 He commanded them, saying, "This is what you shall do: one third of you who come on duty on the Sabbath shall keep watch over the king's house,

6 one third shall be at the gate of Sur, and one third at the gate behind the guards. You shall keep watch over the house as a barrier.

7 The two divisions of you who go off duty on the Sabbath shall keep watch over the house of Yahweh around the king.

8 Surround the king on every side, each man with his weapons in his hand. Whoever comes within the ranks shall be put to death. Be with the king when he goes out and when he comes in."

9 The commanders of the hundreds did all that Jehoiada the priest commanded. Each took his men, those coming on duty on the Sabbath and those going off duty on the Sabbath, and they came to Jehoiada the priest.

10 The priest gave the commanders of the hundreds the spears and the shields that had belonged to King David, which were in the house of Yahweh.

11 The guards stood, each with his weapons in his hand, from the south side of the house to the north side of the house, by the altar and the house, around the king.

12 Then he brought out the king's son, put the crown on him, and gave him the testimony. They made him king and anointed him; they clapped their hands and said, "Long live the king!"

13 Athaliah heard the noise of the guards and the people and came to the people in the house of Yahweh.

14 She looked, and there was the king standing by the pillar, as was the custom, with the commanders and the trumpets beside the king, and all the people of the land rejoicing and blowing the trumpets. Athaliah tore her clothes and cried, "Treason! Treason!"

15 Jehoiada the priest commanded the commanders of the hundreds, those appointed over the army, and said to them, "Bring her out between the ranks, and put to the sword anyone who follows her." For the priest had said, "She must not be put to death in the house of Yahweh."

16 They laid hands on her, and she went by the way of the horses' entrance to the king's house, and there she was put to death.

17 Jehoiada made a covenant between Yahweh and the king and the people, that they would be a people for Yahweh, and also between the king and the people.

18 All the people of the land went to the house of Baal and tore it down. They smashed its altars and its images completely, and they killed Mattan, the priest of Baal, before the altars. The priest appointed officers over the house of Yahweh.

19 He took the commanders of the hundreds, the Carites, the guards, and all the people of the land, and they brought the king down from the house of Yahweh and came by way of the gate of the guards to the king's house. He sat on the throne of the kings.

20 All the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet. Athaliah they had put to death with the sword at the king's house.

2 Kings 12

1 Jehoash was seven years old when he began to reign.

2 In the seventh year of Jehu, Jehoash began to reign, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Zibiah, from Beer-sheba.

3 Jehoash did what was right in the eyes of Yahweh all his days, as Jehoiada the priest had instructed him.

4 Only the high places were not removed; the people still sacrificed and burned incense at the high places.

5 Jehoash said to the priests, "All the money of the holy gifts that is brought into the house of Yahweh — the money in circulation, the money assessed for each person, and all the money that anyone is moved in his heart to bring into the house of Yahweh —

6 let the priests take it for themselves, each from his own acquaintance, and let them repair the damage to the house, wherever damage is found."

7 But by the twenty-third year of King Jehoash, the priests had not repaired the damage to the house.

8 King Jehoash called Jehoiada the priest and the other priests and said to them, "Why are you not repairing the damage to the house? From now on, take no more money from your acquaintances; give it over for the repair of the damage to the house."

9 The priests agreed to take no more money from the people and not to repair the damage to the house themselves.

10 Jehoiada the priest took a chest, bored a hole in its lid, and set it beside the altar, on the right side as one enters the house of Yahweh. The priests who guarded the threshold put into it all the money that was brought into the house of Yahweh.

11 Whenever they saw that there was much money in the chest, the king's scribe and the high priest came up, bagged the money that was found in the house of Yahweh, and counted it.

12 They gave the weighed-out money into the hands of those who did the work, who were appointed over the house of Yahweh, and they paid it out to the woodworkers and the builders who worked on the house of Yahweh,

13 and to the masons and the stonecutters, and to buy timber and cut stone to repair the damage to the house of Yahweh, and for every outlay on the house for its repair.

14 But no silver bowls, snuffers, basins, or trumpets, and no vessel of gold or vessel of silver, were made for the house of Yahweh from the money brought into the house of Yahweh,

15 for they gave it to those who did the work, and with it they repaired the house of Yahweh.

16 They did not require an accounting from the men into whose hand they gave the money to pay those who did the work, for they acted in faithfulness.

17 The money from guilt offerings and the money from sin offerings was not brought into the house of Yahweh; it belonged to the priests.

18 Then Hazael king of Aram went up, fought against Gath, and captured it. Hazael set his face to go up against Jerusalem,

19 so Jehoash king of Judah took all the holy gifts that Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, and Ahaziah, his fathers, kings of Judah, had dedicated, and his own holy gifts, and all the gold found in the treasuries of the house of Yahweh and of the king's house, and sent them to Hazael king of Aram. Then Hazael withdrew from Jerusalem.

20 The rest of the acts of Joash, and all that he did — are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?

21 His servants rose up, formed a conspiracy, and struck down Joash at Beth-millo, on the way that goes down to Silla.

22 Jozabad son of Shimeath and Jehozabad son of Shomer, his servants, struck him, and he died. They buried him with his fathers in the city of David, and Amaziah his son reigned in his place.

2 Kings 13

1 In the twenty-third year of Joash son of Ahaziah, king of Judah, Jehoahaz son of Jehu became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned seventeen years.

2 He did what was evil in the eyes of Yahweh, and he followed the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, with which he caused Israel to sin; he did not turn away from them.

3 The anger of Yahweh burned against Israel, and he gave them into the hand of Hazael king of Aram and into the hand of Ben-hadad son of Hazael all those days.

4 Jehoahaz pleaded with Yahweh, and Yahweh listened to him, because he saw Israel's oppression, how the king of Aram oppressed them.

5 Yahweh gave Israel a deliverer, and they came out from under the hand of Aram, and the children of Israel lived in their tents as they had before.

6 Yet they did not turn from the sins of the house of Jeroboam, with which he caused Israel to sin, but walked in them, and the Asherah also stood in Samaria.

7 He left Jehoahaz no people except fifty horsemen, ten chariots, and ten thousand foot soldiers, for the king of Aram had destroyed them and made them like dust at threshing.

8 The rest of the acts of Jehoahaz, and all that he did, and his might — are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?

9 Jehoahaz slept with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria, and Joash his son reigned in his place.

10 In the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, Jehoash son of Jehoahaz became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned sixteen years.

11 He did what was evil in the eyes of Yahweh; he did not turn from all the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, with which he caused Israel to sin, but walked in them.
