Amos 1

1 The words of Amos, who was among the herdsmen of Tekoa, which he saw concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash, king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.

2 And he said: Yahweh roars from Zion and utters his voice from Jerusalem; and the pastures of the shepherds will mourn, and the top of Carmel will wither.

3 Thus says Yahweh: For three transgressions of Damascus, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they threshed Gilead with threshing sledges of iron.

4 I will send fire into the house of Hazael, and it will devour the palaces of Ben-hadad.

5 And I will break the bar of Damascus, and cut off the inhabitant from the Valley of Aven, and him who holds the scepter from Beth-eden; and the people of Aram will go into captivity to Kir, says Yahweh.

6 Thus says Yahweh: For three transgressions of Gaza, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they carried away the whole community captive, to deliver them up to Edom.

7 I will send fire on the wall of Gaza, and it will devour its palaces.

8 And I will cut off the inhabitant from Ashdod, and him who holds the scepter from Ashkelon; and I will turn my hand against Ekron, and the remnant of the Philistines will perish, says the Lord Yahweh.

9 Thus says Yahweh: For three transgressions of Tyre, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they delivered up the whole community to Edom and did not remember the brotherly covenant.

10 I will send fire on the wall of Tyre, and it will devour its palaces.

11 Thus says Yahweh: For three transgressions of Edom, and for four, I will not turn it back, because he pursued his brother with the sword and destroyed his compassion, and his anger tore continually, and he kept his wrath forever.

12 I will send fire on Teman, and it will devour the palaces of Bozrah.

13 Thus says Yahweh: For three transgressions of the children of Ammon, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they ripped open the pregnant women of Gilead, in order to enlarge their border.

14 I will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah, and it will devour its palaces, with shouting on the day of battle, with a tempest on the day of the whirlwind.

15 And their king will go into captivity, he and his princes together, says Yahweh.

Amos 2

1 Thus says Yahweh: For three transgressions of Moab, and for four, I will not turn it back, because he burned the bones of the king of Edom to lime.

2 I will send fire on Moab, and it will devour the palaces of Kerioth; and Moab will die with tumult, with shouting, and with the sound of the trumpet.

3 And I will cut off the judge from her midst, and I will kill all her princes with him, says Yahweh.

4 Thus says Yahweh: For three transgressions of Judah, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they rejected the law of Yahweh and did not keep his statutes, and their lies led them astray, after which their fathers walked.

5 I will send fire on Judah, and it will devour the palaces of Jerusalem.

6 Thus says Yahweh: For three transgressions of Israel, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they sell the righteous for silver, and the needy for a pair of sandals.

7 They pant after the dust of the earth on the head of the poor, and turn aside the way of the humble; and a man and his father go to the same girl, to profane my holy name.

8 And they stretch out beside every altar on garments taken in pledge, and in the house of their God they drink the wine of those who have been fined.

9 Yet I destroyed the Amorite before them, whose height was like the height of the cedars, and he was strong as the oaks; yet I destroyed his fruit from above, and his roots from beneath.

10 And I brought you up out of the land of Egypt, and led you forty years in the wilderness, to possess the land of the Amorite.

11 And I raised up some of your sons as prophets, and some of your young men as Nazirites. Is this not so, children of Israel? declares Yahweh.

12 But you gave the Nazirites wine to drink, and commanded the prophets, saying: Do not prophesy.

13 See, I will press down in your place, as a cart that is full of sheaves presses down.

14 And flight will perish from the swift, and the strong will not strengthen his strength, and the mighty will not deliver himself.

15 And he who handles the bow will not stand, and he who is swift of foot will not deliver himself, and he who rides the horse will not deliver himself.

16 And he who is courageous among the mighty will flee away naked on that day, declares Yahweh.

Amos 3

1 Hear this word that Yahweh has spoken against you, children of Israel, against the whole family that I brought up out of the land of Egypt, saying:

2 You alone I have known of all the families of the earth; therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities.

3 Do two walk together, unless they have agreed?

4 Will a lion roar in the forest when he has no prey? Will a young lion give forth his voice out of his den, if he has caught nothing?

5 Can a bird fall into a trap on the ground, where there is no snare for it? Does a trap spring up from the ground, and catch nothing at all?

6 If a trumpet is blown in a city, will the people not tremble? If disaster befalls a city, has Yahweh not done it?

7 For the Lord Yahweh will do nothing, unless he reveals his counsel to his servants the prophets.

8 The lion has roared; who will not fear? The Lord Yahweh has spoken; who can but prophesy?

9 Proclaim it on the palaces at Ashdod and on the palaces in the land of Egypt, and say: Assemble yourselves on the mountains of Samaria, and see the great tumults in her midst, and the oppressions within her.

10 They do not know how to do right, declares Yahweh, who store up violence and robbery in their palaces.

11 Therefore thus says the Lord Yahweh: An adversary, all around the land; and he will bring down your strength from you, and your palaces will be plundered.

12 Thus says Yahweh: As the shepherd rescues out of the mouth of the lion two legs or a piece of an ear, so the children of Israel who dwell in Samaria will be rescued, with the corner of a couch and with the damask of a bed.

13 Hear, and testify against the house of Jacob, declares the Lord Yahweh, the God of hosts.

14 For on the day that I punish the transgressions of Israel upon him, I will also punish the altars of Bethel, and the horns of the altar will be cut off and fall to the ground.

15 And I will strike the winter house together with the summer house, and the houses of ivory will perish, and many houses will come to an end, declares Yahweh.

Amos 4

1 Hear this word, you cows of Bashan, who are on the mountain of Samaria, who oppress the poor, who crush the needy, who say to their lords: Bring, so that we may drink.

2 The Lord Yahweh has sworn by his holiness: See, days are coming upon you, and they will take you away with hooks, and your remnant with fishhooks.

3 And you will go out through the breaches, each woman straight before her, and you will be cast into Harmon, declares Yahweh.

4 Come to Bethel and transgress; to Gilgal and multiply transgression; and bring your sacrifices every morning, and your tithes every three days.

5 And burn a thanksgiving offering of leavened bread, and proclaim freewill offerings and publish them; for so you love to do, children of Israel, declares the Lord Yahweh.

6 And I also gave you cleanness of teeth in all your cities, and lack of bread in all your places; yet you did not return to me, declares Yahweh.

7 And I also withheld the rain from you, when there were still three months to the harvest; and I caused it to rain on one city, and I did not cause it to rain on another city. One plot was rained on, and the plot on which it did not rain withered.

8 So two or three cities staggered to one city to drink water, and were not satisfied; yet you did not return to me, declares Yahweh.

9 I struck you with blight and mildew; your many gardens and your vineyards and your fig trees and your olive trees the locust devoured; yet you did not return to me, declares Yahweh.

10 I sent pestilence among you after the manner of Egypt; I killed your young men with the sword, together with the capture of your horses; and I made the stench of your camp come up into your nostrils; yet you did not return to me, declares Yahweh.

11 I overthrew some of you, as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and you were like a brand plucked out of the burning; yet you did not return to me, declares Yahweh.

12 Therefore thus I will do to you, Israel; because I will do this to you, prepare to meet your God, Israel.

13 For see, he who forms the mountains and creates the wind, and declares to man what his thought is, who makes the morning darkness, and treads on the high places of the earth: Yahweh, the God of hosts, is his name.

Amos 5

1 Hear this word that I take up as a lamentation over you, house of Israel.

2 The virgin of Israel has fallen; she will rise no more. She is cast down on her land; there is no one to raise her up.

3 For thus says the Lord Yahweh: The city that goes forth a thousand will have a hundred left, and the one that goes forth a hundred will have ten left, of the house of Israel.

4 For thus says Yahweh to the house of Israel: Seek me, and live.

5 But do not seek Bethel, and do not enter Gilgal, and do not pass over to Beersheba; for Gilgal will surely go into captivity, and Bethel will come to nothing.

6 Seek Yahweh, and live, lest he break out like fire in the house of Joseph, and it devour, and there be no one to quench it in Bethel.

7 You who turn justice into wormwood, and lay righteousness down to the ground.

8 He who made the Pleiades and Orion, and turns deep darkness into morning, and darkens the day into night, who calls for the waters of the sea and pours them out on the face of the earth: Yahweh is his name.

9 He who flashes destruction on the strong, so that destruction comes on the fortress.

10 They hate him who reproves in the gate, and they abhor him who speaks with integrity.

11 Therefore, because you trample on the poor and take a levy of grain from him, you have built houses of hewn stone, but you will not dwell in them; you have planted pleasant vineyards, but you will not drink their wine.

12 For I know how many your transgressions are, and how mighty your sins are, you who afflict the righteous, who take a bribe, and who turn aside the needy in the gate.

13 Therefore the prudent person keeps silent in such a time, for it is an evil time.

14 Seek good and not evil, so that you may live; and so Yahweh, the God of hosts, will be with you, as you have said.

15 Hate evil and love good, and establish justice in the gate; perhaps Yahweh, the God of hosts, will be gracious to the remnant of Joseph.

16 Therefore thus says Yahweh, the God of hosts, the Lord: Lamentation will be in all the plazas, and in all the streets they will say: Alas! Alas! And they will call the farmer to mourning, and those skilled in lamentation to wailing.

17 And in all vineyards there will be lamentation, for I will pass through your midst, says Yahweh.

18 Woe to you who desire the day of Yahweh! Why do you want the day of Yahweh? It is darkness, and not light.

19 As if a man fled from a lion, and a bear met him; and he went into the house and leaned his hand on the wall, and a snake bit him.

20 Will the day of Yahweh not be darkness, and not light? Even gloom, with no brightness in it?

21 I hate, I despise your feasts, and I will take no delight in your solemn assemblies.

22 Though you offer me burnt offerings, I will not accept your grain offerings; and I will not look on the peace offerings of your fat animals.

23 Take away from me the noise of your songs, and I will not listen to the melody of your harps.

24 But let justice roll down like waters, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream.

25 Did you bring me sacrifices and offerings in the wilderness forty years, house of Israel?

26 You will take up Sikkuth your king and Kiyyun your images, the star of your god, which you made for yourselves.

27 Therefore I will exile you beyond Damascus, says Yahweh; the God of hosts is his name.

Amos 6

1 Woe to those who are at ease in Zion, and to those who are secure on the mountain of Samaria, the notable men of the first of the nations, to whom the house of Israel come!

2 Go to Calneh and see, and from there go to Hamath the great; then go down to Gath of the Philistines. Are they better than these kingdoms? Or is their border greater than your border?

3 You who put far away the evil day, and bring the seat of violence near;

4 who lie on beds of ivory and stretch themselves out on their couches, and eat lambs from the flock and calves from the midst of the stall;

5 who strum on the harp, and invent for themselves instruments of music, like David;

6 who drink wine in bowls and anoint themselves with the finest oils, but they are not grieved for the hurt of Joseph.

7 Therefore now they will go into captivity at the head of those who go into captivity, and the revelry of those who stretched themselves out will pass away.

8 The Lord Yahweh has sworn by himself, says Yahweh, the God of hosts: I abhor the pride of Jacob and hate his palaces, and I will deliver up the city with all that is in it.

9 And it will happen that if ten men remain in one house, they will die.

10 And when a man's relative takes him up, the one who burns him, to bring out the bones from the house, and says to the one in the innermost parts of the house, 'Is there anyone still with you?' and he says, 'No,' then he will say, 'Hush! For we must not mention the name of Yahweh.'

11 For, see, Yahweh commands, and the great house will be smashed into splinters, and the little house into chips.

12 Do horses run on the rocks? Does one plow there with oxen? For you have turned justice into poison, and the fruit of righteousness into wormwood;

13 you who rejoice in a thing of nothing, who say, 'Have we not taken horns for ourselves by our own strength?'

14 For, see, I will raise up against you a nation, O house of Israel, says Yahweh, the God of hosts, and they will afflict you from the entrance of Hamath to the Brook of the Arabah.

Amos 7

1 Thus the Lord Yahweh showed me: and see, he formed locusts at the beginning of the shooting up of the latter growth; and see, it was the latter growth after the king's mowings.

2 And when they had finished eating the grass of the land, I said, 'Lord Yahweh, forgive, I beg you! How can Jacob stand? For he is small.'

3 Yahweh relented concerning this. 'It will not be,' says Yahweh.

4 Thus the Lord Yahweh showed me: and see, the Lord Yahweh called to contend by fire, and it devoured the great deep and devoured the land.

5 Then I said, 'Lord Yahweh, stop, I beg you! How can Jacob stand? For he is small.'

6 Yahweh relented concerning this. 'This also will not be,' says the Lord Yahweh.

7 Thus he showed me: and see, the Lord stood beside a wall made by a plumb line, with a plumb line in his hand.

8 And Yahweh said to me, 'Amos, what do you see?' And I said, 'A plumb line.' Then the Lord said, 'See, I am setting a plumb line in the midst of my people Israel. I will not again pass by them any more.

9 And the high places of Isaac will be desolate, and the sanctuaries of Israel will be laid waste, and I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.'

10 Then Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, 'Amos has conspired against you in the midst of the house of Israel. The land is not able to bear all his words.

11 For Amos says this: Jeroboam will die by the sword, and Israel will surely go into captivity out of his land.'

12 And Amaziah said to Amos, 'Seer, go, flee away to the land of Judah, and eat bread there, and prophesy there,

13 but do not prophesy again any more at Bethel, for it is the king's sanctuary, and it is a royal house.'

14 Then Amos answered and said to Amaziah, 'I am no prophet, and I am no son of a prophet, but I am a herdsman and a dresser of sycamore figs;

15 and Yahweh took me from following the flock, and Yahweh said to me, 'Go, prophesy to my people Israel.'

16 Now therefore hear the word of Yahweh: You say, 'Do not prophesy against Israel, and do not preach against the house of Isaac.'

17 Therefore Yahweh says this: 'Your wife will be a prostitute in the city, and your sons and your daughters will fall by the sword, and your land will be divided by line, and you yourself will die in an unclean land, and Israel will surely go into captivity out of his land.'

Amos 8

1 Thus the Lord Yahweh showed me: and see, a basket of summer fruit.

2 And he said, 'Amos, what do you see?' And I said, 'A basket of summer fruit.' Then Yahweh said to me, 'The end has come upon my people Israel. I will not again pass by them any more.

3 And the songs of the temple will be wailings in that day,' says the Lord Yahweh. 'The dead bodies will be many; in every place they will be cast out in silence.'

4 Hear this, you who swallow up the needy and destroy the poor of the land,

5 saying, 'When will the new moon be gone, that we may sell grain? And the Sabbath, that we may market wheat, making the ephah small and the shekel great, and falsifying the balances of deceit;

6 that we may buy the poor for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals, and sell the refuse of the wheat?'

7 Yahweh has sworn by the pride of Jacob: 'Surely I will never forget any of their works.'

8 Shall not the land tremble for this, and everyone who dwells in it mourn? Yes, it will rise up wholly like the River, and it will be stirred up and sink again, like the River of Egypt.

9 And it will happen in that day,' says the Lord Yahweh, 'that I will cause the sun to go down at noon, and I will darken the earth in the clear day.

10 And I will turn your feasts into mourning and all your songs into lamentation, and I will bring sackcloth on all loins and baldness on every head, and I will make it like the mourning for an only son, and its end like a bitter day.

11 See, the days are coming,' says the Lord Yahweh, 'that I will send a famine in the land, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of Yahweh.

12 And they will wander from sea to sea, and from the north even to the east; they will run back and forth to seek the word of Yahweh, and will not find it.

13 In that day the beautiful virgins and the young men will faint for thirst.

14 Those who swear by the guilt of Samaria and say, 'As your god, Dan, lives,' and, 'As the way of Beersheba lives,' they will fall and never rise up again.'

Amos 9

1 I saw the Lord standing beside the altar, and he said, 'Strike the capitals, that the thresholds may shake, and break them in pieces on the head of all of them, and I will kill the last of them with the sword. Not one of them will flee away, and not one of them will escape.

2 Though they dig into Sheol, from there my hand will take them; and though they climb up to heaven, from there I will bring them down.

3 And though they hide themselves on the top of Carmel, from there I will search and take them; and though they are hidden from my sight in the bottom of the sea, from there I will command the serpent, and it will bite them.

4 And though they go into captivity before their enemies, from there I will command the sword, and it will kill them, and I will set my eyes on them for evil and not for good.'

5 And the Lord Yahweh of hosts is he who touches the land and it melts, and all who dwell in it mourn, and it rises up wholly like the River and sinks again like the River of Egypt;

6 he who builds his upper chambers in the heavens and has founded his vault on the earth, he who calls for the waters of the sea and pours them out on the face of the earth — Yahweh is his name.

7 Are you not like the children of the Cushites to me, O children of Israel?' says Yahweh. 'Have I not brought up Israel out of the land of Egypt, and the Philistines from Caphtor, and Aram from Kir?

8 See, the eyes of the Lord Yahweh are on the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from off the face of the earth, except that I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob,' says Yahweh.

9 For, see, I will command, and I will sift the house of Israel among all the nations, as grain is sifted in a sieve, yet not the least kernel will fall to the earth.

10 All the sinners of my people will die by the sword, who say, 'The evil will not overtake or confront us.'

11 In that day I will raise up the booth of David that has fallen, and close up its breaches, and I will raise up its ruins, and I will build it as in the days of old,

12 that they may possess the remnant of Edom and all the nations on whom my name is called,' says Yahweh who does this.

13 See, the days are coming,' says Yahweh, 'that the plowman will overtake the reaper, and the treader of grapes him who sows seed, and the mountains will drip sweet wine, and all the hills will melt.

14 And I will bring my people Israel back from captivity, and they will build the ruined cities and inhabit them, and they will plant vineyards and drink their wine; they will also make gardens and eat their fruit.

15 And I will plant them on their land, and they will no more be plucked up out of their land that I have given them,' says Yahweh your God.

Clear English Bible — Obadiah (Chapter 1): A Clear English Translation

COMPLETE — This book of the Clear English Bible is complete. This is a fresh translation made directly from the Hebrew: the Masoretic text of the Westminster Leningrad Codex, verified consonant by consonant against the Miqra according to the Masorah (the Sefaria edition). It was inserted into this edition on 23 November 2026, under the editor's Fresh Tanakh commission ruling of the same date and its authorization-forward rule, replacing the clear-English modernization of the World English Bible Classic that stood here before. This text was prepared with AI assistance. Robert Tilford is the editor.

Draft history — 25 October 2026. Obadiah chapter 1 was internally audited (AUDITED), formerly stood as a draft awaiting Robert's read-through, and was formerly labeled a partial draft, unpublished. The completion statement above was substituted for the former draft header in the final handling under Ruling 20, after the campaign's rulings had been applied and verified; the former header's history is preserved here and in the repository history.

Insertion record — 23 November 2026. The text of Obadiah in this file was replaced by the fresh translation from the Hebrew described above (a single chapter, 21 verses — the Masoretic and English numbering are identical, so the block keeps its shape and its header), inserted under the editor's Fresh Tanakh commission ruling of 23 November 2026 and its authorization-forward rule, by which finished book drafts in this lane advance into the editions without a separate word for each book. The translation was built in two passes (verses 1–11 and 12–21), each independently checked against the Hebrew: both passes passed clean, with no errors found — the sixth book of the commission, after Daniel, Amos, Malachi, Hosea, and Joel, to pass both of its checker passes without an error. The divine name stands as "Yahweh" at all 7 of its seats in this book — the count established from both Masoretic witnesses, whose per-verse tallies agree at every verse; no banked benchmark existed for this book. The text it replaced stands in the repository history. The differences between the two texts, each with its Hebrew ground stated, and the 28 places where the Hebrew bears two readings and the seat stands open, are recorded in the translation's build records (PACKET-OBADIAH.md, LEDGER-OBADIAH.md, OPEN-SEATS-OBADIAH.md, CHECK-REPORT-OBADIAH.md, kept with the desk's fresh-obadiah working papers).

Obadiah 1

1 The vision of Obadiah. This is what the Lord Yahweh says concerning Edom: We have heard news from Yahweh, and an ambassador has been sent among the nations: Arise, and let us rise up against her for battle.

2 See, I have made you small among the nations; you are greatly despised.

3 The pride of your heart has deceived you, you who live in the clefts of the rock, whose dwelling is high, who says in his heart: Who will bring me down to the ground?

4 Though you soar like the eagle, and though you set your nest among the stars, from there I will bring you down, declares Yahweh.

5 If thieves came to you, if robbers by night — how you are ruined! — would they not steal only until they had enough? If grape gatherers came to you, would they not leave some gleanings?

6 How Esau has been searched out! How his hidden treasures have been sought out!

7 All the men of your covenant have sent you to the border; the men at peace with you have deceived you and prevailed against you; those who eat your bread have set a snare under you. There is no understanding in him.

8 Will I not on that day, declares Yahweh, destroy the wise men from Edom, and understanding from the mountain of Esau?

9 Your mighty men will be dismayed, Teman, so that everyone will be cut off from the mountain of Esau by slaughter.

10 For the violence done to your brother Jacob, shame will cover you, and you will be cut off forever.

11 On the day you stood aloof, on the day strangers carried off his wealth and foreigners entered his gates and cast lots for Jerusalem, even you were like one of them.

12 Do not look on the day of your brother, in the day of his disaster. Do not rejoice over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction. Do not speak proudly in the day of distress.

13 Do not enter the gate of my people in the day of their calamity. Do not look, you too, on their affliction in the day of their calamity. Do not seize their wealth in the day of their calamity.

14 Do not stand at the crossroads to cut off his fugitives. Do not hand over his survivors in the day of distress.

15 For the day of Yahweh is near upon all the nations. As you have done, it will be done to you; your reprisal will return on your own head.

16 For as you have drunk on my holy mountain, so all the nations will drink continually. They will drink and swallow down, and will be as though they had not been.

17 But on Mount Zion there will be deliverance, and it will be holy; and the house of Jacob will possess their possessions.

18 The house of Jacob will be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau stubble. They will burn among them and devour them, and there will be no survivor for the house of Esau, for Yahweh has spoken.

19 Those of the Negev will possess Mount Esau, and those of the Shephelah the Philistines. They will possess the field of Ephraim and the field of Samaria, and Benjamin will possess Gilead.

20 The exiles of this host of the children of Israel, who are among the Canaanites, will possess as far as Zarephath; and the exiles of Jerusalem, who are in Sepharad, will possess the cities of the Negev.

21 Saviours will come up on Mount Zion to judge Mount Esau, and the kingdom will be Yahweh's.

Clear English Bible — Jonah (Chapters 1–4): A Clear English Translation

This completes the Masoretic book of Jonah in this edition. The remaining books of the Old Testament stand in this edition as a clear-English modernization of the World English Bible (WEB) Classic text named in the front matter, except the books the front matter names as fresh translations made directly from the Hebrew; the New Testament stands on the Greek text named there. The book as printed here stands as DRAFT — NOT PUBLISHED.

Insertion record — 24 November 2026. The Masoretic book of Jonah (4 chapters, 48 verses) was inserted as a fresh translation made directly from the Masoretic Hebrew under Robert Tilford's Fresh Tanakh commission ruling of 23 November 2026 and its authorization-forward amendment, confirmed the same day, replacing the earlier WEB-based text of the book. The translation is the pilot of 23 November 2026, built before the commission's waves to test whether the Fresh-from-Hebrew method of the Fresh Torah could be carried beyond the Torah to a whole small book; it rested for the editor's pass until this insertion, and is inserted as it stood at that pass. The block is printed in the English numbering, as the seated text was printed: the English scheme [17, 10, 10, 11] counts the same 48 verses as the Hebrew scheme [16, 11, 10, 11], the two dividing at one boundary only — Hebrew 2:1, the verse of the great fish, stands as English 1:17, and the prayer, English 2:1–10, is Hebrew 2:2–11; chapters 3 and 4 number alike in both systems. The ground check before the build settled what the seated text was: a clear-English modernization of the World English Bible Classic in all three files, the Masoretic book alone, one identical draft-history hash in all three; no target carries any second form of the book, and the Daniel/Esther caution was not triggered. The consonantal text was compared letter by letter, by machine, across three presentations of the Masoretic text — the Westminster Leningrad Codex (the base), the Unicode/XML Leningrad Codex, and Mechon Mamre: 42 of the 48 verses are consonant-exact across all three, and the six remaining differ only in things that are not text — section markers carried by two witnesses and not extracted from the third, a stray Latin letter inside one encoded word in the XML witness at 3:3, a combining mark inside the word qiqayon in the XML witness at 4:6, and a section marker appended after the last verse in the Mamre page — so no verse carries a genuine consonantal disagreement. The difference ledger records 34 differences from the controls (the seated text, JPS 1917, and the ESV — the last consulted for the ledger only, never as the base, its stored copies deleted on the desk's own correction of 23 November 2026), each with its ground in the Hebrew. The independent checker returned PASS WITH CORRECTIONS: no error of sense was found — no clause dropped, added, softened, or reversed, no name misstated, no number wrong — and the nine corrections it required were all applied to the text as printed here (among them the causative restored at 1:13; the object marker honoured at 1:16, "feared Yahweh with a great fear"; the ra'ah chain restored at 4:6, "to deliver him from his evil"; chesed aligned on its one rendering, "loving-kindness", at 2:8; and the noun form printed at 4:3 and 4:8, "my death is better than my life"), with four minor points recorded without change. The divine name יהוה stands 26 times in the verse body and prints "Yahweh" at exactly those seats; the compound "Yahweh God" stands at 4:6 only, exactly where the Hebrew has יהוה־אלהים. One word is left standing in Hebrew in the text: qiqayon, the plant of chapter 4, whose kind no witness settles — the leading modern identification, the castor-oil plant, stands named in the pilot's apparatus — as Sheol is left standing in the prayer. Eight open seats stand recorded in the pilot's apparatus, headed by 3:4 nehpakhet, "will be overthrown", which also bears "will be turned"; none of them is settled by this insertion. Daniel's block is byte-identical before and after (sha256 prefix 0a88959fcce30f57). Build record: the pilot stands at ~/workspace/your_files/JONAH-FRESH-FROM-HEBREW-PILOT-2026-11-23.md, with PACKET-JONAH.md and CHECK-REPORT-JONAH.md in the desk's working folder (.tools/jonah-pilot/), and the insertion pack in .tools/jonah-pilot/seating-prep/. The book stands as DRAFT — NOT PUBLISHED.

Draft history — 25 October 2026. Jonah chapters 1–4 were all internally audited (AUDITED), formerly stood as drafts awaiting Robert's read-through, and were formerly labeled a partial draft, unpublished. Jonah 1

1 And the word of Yahweh came to Jonah the son of Amittai, saying,

2 "Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and proclaim against it, for their evil has come up before me."

3 But Jonah arose to flee to Tarshish, away from the presence of Yahweh. He went down to Joppa and found a ship going to Tarshish, and he paid its fare and went down into it, to go with them to Tarshish, away from the presence of Yahweh.

4 But Yahweh hurled a great wind onto the sea, and there was a great storm on the sea, and the ship threatened to break up.

5 Then the sailors were afraid, and each man cried out to his god, and they hurled the goods that were in the ship into the sea, to lighten the load that was upon them. But Jonah had gone down into the innermost parts of the ship, and he lay down and fell fast asleep.

6 And the captain drew near to him and said to him, "What is the matter with you, sleeper? Arise, call on your God! Perhaps God will think of us, and we shall not perish."

7 And they said, each man to his neighbour, "Come, let us cast lots, that we may know on whose account this evil is upon us." And they cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.

8 And they said to him, "Tell us, please: on whose account is this evil upon us? What is your work, and where do you come from? What is your land, and of what people are you?"

9 And he said to them, "I am a Hebrew, and I fear Yahweh, the God of the heavens, who made the sea and the dry land."

10 Then the men feared a great fear, and they said to him, "What is this you have done?" For the men knew that he was fleeing from the presence of Yahweh, because he had told them.

11 And they said to him, "What shall we do to you, that the sea may be calm for us?" For the sea was growing more and more stormy.

12 And he said to them, "Lift me up and hurl me into the sea, and the sea will be calm for you; for I know that it is on my account that this great storm is upon you."

13 But the men rowed hard to bring the ship back to the dry land, and they could not, for the sea was growing more and more stormy against them.

14 And they cried to Yahweh and said, "Please, Yahweh, do not let us perish for this man's life, and do not put innocent blood upon us; for you, Yahweh, have done as you pleased."

15 And they lifted Jonah up and hurled him into the sea, and the sea stood still from its raging.

16 Then the men feared Yahweh with a great fear, and they offered a sacrifice to Yahweh, and made vows.

17 And Yahweh appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.

Jonah 2

1 Then Jonah prayed to Yahweh his God from the belly of the fish,

2 and he said: "I called out of my distress to Yahweh, and he answered me. From the belly of Sheol I cried for help, and you heard my voice.

3 For you cast me into the deep, into the heart of the seas, and the flood surrounded me; all your breakers and your waves passed over me.

4 And I said, 'I have been driven out from before your eyes; yet I will look again toward your holy temple.'

5 The waters closed around me, up to my very life; the deep surrounded me; seaweed was wrapped around my head.

6 I went down to the roots of the mountains. The earth — its bars closed behind me forever. Yet you brought up my life from the pit, Yahweh my God.

7 When my soul fainted within me, I remembered Yahweh, and my prayer came to you, into your holy temple.

8 Those who regard empty vanities forsake their own loving-kindness.

9 But I will sacrifice to you with the voice of thanksgiving; what I have vowed I will pay. Salvation belongs to Yahweh!"

10 And Yahweh spoke to the fish, and it vomited Jonah out onto the dry land.

Jonah 3

1 And the word of Yahweh came to Jonah a second time, saying,

2 "Arise, go to Nineveh, that great city, and proclaim to it the proclamation that I am speaking to you."

3 And Jonah arose and went to Nineveh, according to the word of Yahweh. Now Nineveh was a city great to God, a journey of three days.

4 And Jonah began to go into the city, a day's journey, and he proclaimed and said, "Forty days more, and Nineveh will be overthrown!"

5 And the people of Nineveh believed God, and they proclaimed a fast and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them to the least of them.

6 And the word reached the king of Nineveh, and he arose from his throne and took off his robe, and he covered himself with sackcloth and sat on the ashes.

7 And he had it cried out in Nineveh, by the decree of the king and his great men, saying, "Man and animal, herd and flock, shall not taste anything; they shall not graze, and they shall not drink water.

8 And let man and animal be covered with sackcloth, and let them cry to God mightily, and let each man turn from his evil way and from the violence that is in their hands.

9 Who knows? God may turn and relent, and turn back from his fierce anger, and we shall not perish."

10 And God saw their deeds, that they had turned from their evil way, and God relented concerning the evil that he had said he would do to them, and he did not do it.

Jonah 4

1 But it was evil to Jonah — a great evil — and he burned with anger.

2 And he prayed to Yahweh and said, "Please, Yahweh, was this not my word when I was still in my own land? That is why I hastened to flee to Tarshish beforehand, for I knew that you are a gracious God and compassionate, slow to anger and abounding in loving-kindness, and relenting concerning evil.

3 And now, Yahweh, please take my life from me, for my death is better than my life."

4 And Yahweh said, "Is it right for you to be angry?"

5 And Jonah went out of the city and sat down to the east of the city, and he made himself a booth there and sat under it in the shade, until he should see what would happen in the city.

6 And Yahweh God appointed a qiqayon plant, and it came up over Jonah to be a shade over his head, to deliver him from his evil. And Jonah rejoiced over the qiqayon with a great joy.

7 And God appointed a worm at the coming up of the dawn on the next day, and it struck the qiqayon, and it withered.

8 And when the sun rose, God appointed a scorching east wind, and the sun struck Jonah's head, and he fainted, and he asked that he might die, and he said, "My death is better than my life."

9 And God said to Jonah, "Is it right for you to be angry about the qiqayon?" And he said, "It is right for me to be angry, even to death."

10 And Yahweh said, "You had pity on the qiqayon, for which you did not labour and which you did not make grow, which came up in a night and perished in a night.

11 And should I not have pity on Nineveh, that great city, in which there are more than a hundred and twenty thousand people who do not know between their right hand and their left, and many animals?"

Clear English Bible — Micah (Chapters 1–7): A Clear English Translation

This completes the Masoretic book of Micah in this edition. The remaining books of the Old Testament stand in this edition as a clear-English modernization of the World English Bible (WEB) Classic text named in the front matter, except the books the front matter names as fresh translations made directly from the Hebrew; the New Testament stands on the Greek text named there. The book as printed here stands as DRAFT — NOT PUBLISHED.

Insertion record — 23 November 2026. The Masoretic chapters of Micah (7 chapters, 105 verses in Masoretic numbering) were inserted as a fresh translation made directly from the Masoretic Hebrew under Robert Tilford's Fresh Tanakh commission ruling of 23 November 2026 and its authorization-forward amendment, confirmed the same day, replacing the earlier WEB-based text of those chapters. The block is reseated in the Masoretic scheme: the verse that stood as English 5:1 now stands as 4:14, closing chapter 4, and the verses that stood as English 5:2–15 now stand as 5:1–14; chapters 1–3 and 6–7 keep their bounds, and the block header is unchanged, the chapter count being the same in both schemes. The translation was built in two reviser passes (Masoretic chapters 1–4; chapters 5–7) from the Masoretic text as it stands in the Westminster Leningrad Codex and Sefaria's Miqra according to the Masorah — the two witnesses consonant-exact in 97 of the book's 105 verses, the eight divergences classified in the build record (four ketiv/qere presentation, one defect of the Bolls extraction at 4:10, three spelling only) — with JPS 1917 as the open control of record. Two independent checker passes that did not build the text read the draft against the Hebrew line and both controls: the chapters 5–7 pass returned no errors; the chapters 1–4 pass found one error, at 4:13, where the draft had followed JPS's second person against the Hebrew's first person singular והחרמתי, and the checker's exact replacement text was applied and re-verified by count before insertion. The divine name יהוה stands 40 times in the book — no banked benchmark existed, so the count was established from both witnesses before the build; the two witnesses agree at every verse — and prints "Yahweh" at every seat; no standalone יהּ seat stands in Micah. The difference ledger records 104 of the book's 105 verses as differing materially from the seated text or the open control, and 37 open seats stand recorded. The directed seats stand as the commission named them: 1:2 (אדני יהוה, "the Lord Yahweh"); 2:13 (the breaker and the king); 4:1–3 (the mountain of Yahweh's house, printed as Micah's Hebrew stands); Masoretic 5:1–2 (the Bethlehem seat — "whose origins are from of old, from days of eternity"); 6:8 ("do justice, and love loyal love, and walk humbly"); and 7:18–20 (the name-play carried unglossed, the person shifts unharmonised). Build record: PACKET-MICAH.md, LEDGER-MICAH.md, CHECK-REPORT-MICAH.md, and OPEN-SEATS-MICAH.md in the desk's working folder (.tools/fresh-micah/). The book stands as DRAFT — NOT PUBLISHED.

Draft history — 25 October 2026. Micah chapters 1–7 were all internally audited (AUDITED), formerly stood as drafts awaiting Robert's read-through, and were formerly labeled a partial draft, unpublished. The completion statement above was substituted for the former draft header in the final handling under Ruling 20, after the campaign's rulings had been applied and verified; the former header's history is preserved here and in the repository history.

Micah 1

1 The word of Yahweh that came to Micah the Morashtite in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.
2 Hear, peoples, all of you; listen, earth and all that fills it; and let the Lord Yahweh be a witness against you, the Lord from his holy temple.
3 For see, Yahweh is coming out from his place; he will come down and tread on the high places of the earth.
4 The mountains will melt under him, and the valleys will split apart, like wax before the fire, like water poured down a steep place.
5 All this is for the transgression of Jacob and for the sins of the house of Israel. What is the transgression of Jacob? Is it not Samaria? And what are the high places of Judah? Are they not Jerusalem?
6 So I will make Samaria a heap in the field, a place for planting vineyards; I will pour down its stones into the valley and uncover its foundations.
7 All her carved images will be beaten to pieces, and all her hire will be burned with fire, and I will lay all her idols desolate; for she gathered them from the hire of a prostitute, and to the hire of a prostitute they will return.
8 For this I will lament and wail; I will go stripped and naked; I will make a lament like the jackals and mourning like the ostriches.
9 For her wounds are incurable, for it has come as far as Judah; it has reached the gate of my people, as far as Jerusalem.
10 Do not tell it in Gath; do not weep at all; in Beth-le-aphrah, wallow yourself in the dust.
11 Pass on, inhabitant of Shaphir, in nakedness and shame; the inhabitant of Zaanan has not come out; the wailing of Beth Ezel will take from you its standing place.
12 For the inhabitant of Maroth waits anxiously for good, because evil has come down from Yahweh to the gate of Jerusalem.
13 Harness the chariot to the swift steed, inhabitant of Lachish; she was the beginning of sin to the daughter of Zion, for the transgressions of Israel were found in you.
14 Therefore you will give parting gifts to Moresheth Gath; the houses of Achzib will be a deception to the kings of Israel.
15 I will yet bring to you, inhabitant of Mareshah, one who will possess you; the glory of Israel will come as far as Adullam.
16 Shave your head bald and cut off your hair for the children of your delight; make your baldness wide like the vulture, for they have gone into exile from you.

Micah 2

1 Woe to those who devise iniquity and work evil on their beds; in the morning light they carry it out, because it is in the power of their hand.
2 They covet fields and seize them, and houses, and take them away; they oppress a man and his house, a man and his inheritance.
3 Therefore Yahweh says this: See, I am devising evil against this family, from which you will not draw out your necks, and you will not walk haughtily, for it is an evil time.
4 In that day they will take up a taunt against you and lament a doleful lamentation, saying: We are utterly ruined; he changes the portion of my people; how he removes it from me! He divides our fields to traitors.
5 Therefore you will have no one to cast a measuring line by lot in the assembly of Yahweh.
6 Do not prophesy, they prophesy; do not prophesy about these things; disgrace will not overtake us.
7 Should it be said, house of Jacob: Is the Spirit of Yahweh impatient? Are these his doings? Do not my words do good to the one who walks uprightly?
8 But lately my people has risen up as an enemy; you strip the robe and the garment from those who pass by in safety, returned from war.
9 You drive out the women of my people from their pleasant houses; from their young children you take my glory forever.
10 Arise and depart, for this is not your resting place, because of the uncleanness that destroys, with a grievous destruction.
11 If a man walking in wind and falsehood lies: I will preach to you about wine and strong drink, he would be the preacher of this people.
12 I will surely gather all of you, Jacob; I will surely gather the remnant of Israel; I will put them together like the sheep of Bozrah, like a flock in the middle of its pasture; they will be noisy with people.
13 The breaker has gone up before them; they break through and pass through the gate and go out by it; their king passes on before them, and Yahweh at their head.

Micah 3

1 And I said: Listen, please, heads of Jacob and rulers of the house of Israel; is it not for you to know justice?
2 You who hate good and love evil, who tear their skin from them and their flesh from their bones,
3 who also eat the flesh of my people, and strip their skin from them, and break their bones, and chop them in pieces, as for the pot, and as flesh within the cauldron.
4 Then they will cry out to Yahweh, but he will not answer them; he will hide his face from them at that time, as they have made their deeds evil.
5 Yahweh says this concerning the prophets who lead my people astray: they bite with their teeth and cry: Peace; but against anyone who puts nothing into their mouths, they prepare war against him.
6 Therefore it will be night for you, without vision, and darkness for you, without divination; the sun will go down on the prophets, and the day will grow black over them.
7 The seers will be ashamed and the diviners put to shame; they will all cover their lips, for there is no answer from God.
8 But as for me, I am full of power by the Spirit of Yahweh, and of justice, and of might, to declare to Jacob his transgression and to Israel his sin.
9 Listen to this, please, heads of the house of Jacob and rulers of the house of Israel, who detest justice and twist all that is upright,
10 who build Zion with blood and Jerusalem with wrongdoing.
11 Its heads judge for a bribe, its priests teach for a price, and its prophets divine for silver; yet they lean on Yahweh and say: Is Yahweh not in our midst? No evil will come upon us.
12 Therefore, because of you, Zion will be plowed as a field, Jerusalem will become heaps of ruins, and the mountain of the house will become high places of a forest.

Micah 4

1 And it will happen in the latter days: the mountain of the house of Yahweh will be established on the top of the mountains, and it will be exalted above the hills, and peoples will stream to it.
2 Many nations will come and say: Come, let us go up to the mountain of Yahweh and to the house of the God of Jacob, and he will teach us from his ways, and we will walk in his paths; for the law will go out from Zion, and the word of Yahweh from Jerusalem.
3 He will judge between many peoples and decide for strong nations far away; and they will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks; nation will not lift up sword against nation, and they will no longer learn war.
4 Each man will sit under his vine and under his fig tree, and no one will make them afraid, for the mouth of Yahweh of hosts has spoken.
5 For all the peoples walk, each in the name of its god, but we will walk in the name of Yahweh our God forever and ever.
6 In that day, declares Yahweh, I will assemble the lame and gather the one who was driven away, and the one whom I have afflicted,
7 and I will make the lame a remnant and the one cast far off a strong nation, and Yahweh will reign over them on Mount Zion from now on and forever.
8 And you, Tower of the Flock, the hill of the daughter of Zion, to you it will come; the former dominion will come, the kingdom of the daughter of Jerusalem.
9 Now why do you cry out loudly? Is there no king in you? Has your counselor perished, that pain has seized you like a woman giving birth?
10 Writhe and groan, daughter of Zion, like a woman giving birth; for now you will go out from the city and dwell in the field and come as far as Babylon; there you will be rescued; there Yahweh will redeem you from the hand of your enemies.
11 Now many nations have gathered against you, who say: Let her be defiled, and let our eyes gaze on Zion.
12 But they do not know the thoughts of Yahweh, and they do not understand his counsel, for he has gathered them like sheaves to the threshing floor.
13 Arise and thresh, daughter of Zion, for I will make your horn iron and your hooves bronze, and you will crush many peoples; and I will devote their gain to Yahweh, and their wealth to the Lord of the whole earth.
14 Now gather yourself in troops, daughter of troops; they have laid siege against us; with a rod they will strike the judge of Israel on the cheek.

Micah 5

1 But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, who are small to be among the clans of Judah, out of you shall come forth to me one who is to be ruler in Israel, whose origins are from of old, from days of eternity.
2 Therefore he will give them up until the time when she who is in labor has given birth; then the remnant of his brothers will return to the children of Israel.
3 And he will stand and shepherd in the strength of Yahweh, in the majesty of the name of Yahweh his God; and they will dwell, for then he will be great to the ends of the earth.
4 And he will be peace, when Assyria comes into our land and when he treads in our palaces; then we will raise against him seven shepherds and eight princes of men.
5 And they will rule the land of Assyria with the sword, and the land of Nimrod in its gates; and he will deliver us from Assyria, when he comes into our land and when he treads within our border.
6 And the remnant of Jacob will be in the midst of many peoples like dew from Yahweh, like showers on the grass, which does not wait for man and does not wait for the sons of men.
7 And the remnant of Jacob will be among the nations, in the midst of many peoples, like a lion among the beasts of the forest, like a young lion among flocks of sheep, which, if it passes through, treads down and tears in pieces, and there is no one to deliver.
8 Let your hand be lifted up over your adversaries, and let all your enemies be cut off.
9 And it will happen on that day, declares Yahweh, that I will cut off your horses from your midst and destroy your chariots.
10 And I will cut off the cities of your land and tear down all your strongholds.
11 And I will cut off sorceries from your hand, and you will have no soothsayers.
12 And I will cut off your carved images and your standing stones from your midst, and you will no longer bow down to the work of your hands.
13 And I will uproot your Asherah poles from your midst and destroy your cities.
14 And I will execute vengeance in anger and wrath on the nations that did not listen.

Micah 6

1 Listen now to what Yahweh says: Arise, plead your case before the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice.
2 Hear, mountains, the case of Yahweh, and you enduring foundations of the earth; for Yahweh has a case against his people, and he will contend with Israel.
3 My people, what have I done to you, and how have I wearied you? Answer me.
4 For I brought you up from the land of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of slavery; and I sent before you Moses, Aaron, and Miriam.
5 My people, remember now what Balak king of Moab planned, and what Balaam son of Beor answered him, from Shittim to Gilgal, so that you may know the righteous acts of Yahweh.
6 With what shall I come before Yahweh, and bow myself before God on high? Shall I come before him with burnt offerings, with calves a year old?
7 Will Yahweh be pleased with thousands of rams, with tens of thousands of rivers of oil? Shall I give my firstborn for my transgression, the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?
8 He has told you, O man, what is good, and what Yahweh requires of you: only to do justice, and to love loyal love, and to walk humbly with your God.
9 The voice of Yahweh calls to the city, and it is wisdom to fear your name: Hear the rod, and who has appointed it.
10 Are there still in the house of the wicked treasures of wickedness, and a scant ephah that is accursed?
11 Shall I acquit with wicked balances, and with a bag of deceitful weights?
12 Her rich men are full of violence, her inhabitants speak lies, and their tongue is deceitful in their mouth.
13 Therefore I also have struck you with a grievous wound; I have made you desolate because of your sins.
14 You will eat, but not be satisfied; your hunger will be within you; you will store up, but not save, and what you save I will give up to the sword.
15 You will sow, but not reap; you will tread olives, but not anoint yourself with oil, and crush grapes, but not drink the wine.
16 And the statutes of Omri are kept, and all the works of the house of Ahab, and you walk in their counsels, so that I may make you a desolation and her inhabitants a hissing, and you will bear the reproach of my people.

Micah 7

1 Woe is me, for I have become like the gatherings of summer fruit, like the gleanings of the vintage; there is no cluster to eat, no first-ripe fig that my soul desires.
2 The godly man has perished from the earth, and there is no one upright among men; they all lie in wait for blood; every man hunts his brother with a net.
3 Their hands are on evil to do it well; the prince asks, and the judge for a bribe, and the great man speaks the evil desire of his soul, and they weave it together.
4 The best of them is like a brier, the most upright is worse than a thorn hedge; the day of your watchmen, your visitation, has come; now will be their confusion.
5 Do not trust in a neighbor, do not put confidence in a friend; from the woman who lies in your bosom, guard the doors of your mouth.
6 For the son dishonors the father, the daughter rises up against her mother, the daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; a man's enemies are the men of his own house.
7 But as for me, I will look to Yahweh; I will wait for the God of my salvation; my God will hear me.
8 Do not rejoice over me, my enemy; though I have fallen, I will arise; though I sit in darkness, Yahweh will be a light to me.
9 I will bear the wrath of Yahweh, because I have sinned against him, until he pleads my case and executes judgment for me; he will bring me out to the light, and I will see his righteousness.
10 And my enemy will see, and shame will cover her who said to me: Where is Yahweh your God? My eyes will look on her; now she will be trampled like the mire of the streets.
11 A day for building your walls; on that day the boundary will be far extended.
12 On that day they will come to you, from Assyria and the cities of Egypt, and from Egypt to the River, and from sea to sea, and from mountain to mountain.
13 And the land will become a desolation because of its inhabitants, for the fruit of their deeds.
14 Shepherd your people with your staff, the flock of your heritage, who dwell alone in a forest in the midst of Carmel; let them feed in Bashan and Gilead as in days of old.
15 As in the days of your coming out from the land of Egypt, I will show him wonders.
16 Nations will see and be ashamed of all their might; they will put a hand on the mouth; their ears will become deaf.
17 They will lick dust like the serpent, like crawling things of the earth; they will tremble out of their strongholds; they will come in fear to Yahweh our God, and be afraid because of you.
18 Who is a God like you, pardoning iniquity and passing over the transgression of the remnant of his heritage? He does not retain his anger forever, for he delights in loyal love.
19 He will again have compassion on us; he will tread our iniquities underfoot; and you will cast all their sins into the depths of the sea.
20 You will show faithfulness to Jacob, loyal love to Abraham, as you swore to our fathers from days of old.

Clear English Bible — Nahum (Chapters 1–3): A Clear English Translation

This completes the Masoretic book of Nahum in this edition. The remaining books of the Old Testament stand in this edition as a clear-English modernization of the World English Bible (WEB) Classic text named in the front matter, except the books the front matter names as fresh translations made directly from the Hebrew; the New Testament stands on the Greek text named there. The translation was built in two reviser passes (Masoretic chapter 1; chapters 2–3) from the Masoretic text as it stands in the Westminster Leningrad Codex and Sefaria's Miqra according to the Masorah — the two witnesses consonant-exact in 37 of the book's 47 verses, the ten divergences classified in the build record (six defects of the Bolls extraction, three spelling only, one form variant) — with JPS 1917 as the open control of record. The difference ledger records 46 of the book's 47 verses as differing materially from the seated text or the open control, and 23 open seats stand recorded. The directed seats stand as the commission named them: 1:2–8 (the opening theophany, the partial acrostic as it stands); 1:3 ("slow to anger and great in power"); 1:7 ("Yahweh is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble"); Masoretic 2:1 (the messenger's feet, printed as Nahum's Hebrew stands); Masoretic 2:14 and 3:5 ("Behold, I am against you — the declaration of Yahweh of hosts"); and 3:19 (the closing clapping of hands, at full force). Build record: PACKET-NAHUM.md, LEDGER-NAHUM.md, CHECK-REPORT-NAHUM.md, and OPEN-SEATS-NAHUM.md in the desk's working folder (.tools/fresh-nahum/). The book stands as DRAFT — NOT PUBLISHED.

Nahum 1

1 The burden of Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite.
2 Yahweh is a jealous and avenging God. Yahweh avenges and is full of wrath. Yahweh takes vengeance on his adversaries, and he keeps wrath for his enemies.
3 Yahweh is slow to anger and great in power, and he will by no means leave the guilty unpunished. Yahweh has his way in the whirlwind and in the storm, and the clouds are the dust of his feet.
4 He rebukes the sea and makes it dry, and dries up all the rivers. Bashan and Carmel languish, and the flower of Lebanon languishes.
5 The mountains quake before him, and the hills melt away. The earth heaves at his presence, the world, and all who dwell in it.
6 Who can stand before his indignation? Who can endure the fierceness of his anger? His wrath is poured out like fire, and the rocks are broken apart by him.
7 Yahweh is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble; and he knows those who take refuge in him.
8 But with an overflowing flood he will make a complete end of her place, and he will pursue his enemies into darkness.
9 What do you devise against Yahweh? He will make a complete end. Affliction will not rise up a second time.
10 For, entangled like thorns and drunken with their drink, they are consumed like fully dry stubble.
11 Out of you has come one who devises evil against Yahweh, who counsels wickedness.
12 Thus says Yahweh: Though they are in full strength and likewise many, even so they will be cut down and pass away. Though I have afflicted you, I will afflict you no more.
13 Now I will break his yoke from off you, and I will tear your bonds apart.
14 Yahweh has commanded concerning you: Your name will no longer be sown. From the house of your gods I will cut off the carved image and the molten image. I will make your grave, for you are worthless.

Nahum 2

1 Behold, on the mountains, the feet of a messenger who proclaims peace! Celebrate your feasts, Judah; fulfill your vows, for the worthless one will never again pass through you. He is utterly cut off.
2 A scatterer has come up against your face. Guard the stronghold! Watch the road! Strengthen your loins! Muster your strength with all your might!
3 For Yahweh is restoring the splendor of Jacob, like the splendor of Israel, for plunderers have plundered them and ruined their vine branches.
4 The shield of his warriors is reddened; the valiant men are dressed in scarlet. The chariots flash with fire of steel on the day of his preparation, and the cypress spears are brandished.
5 The chariots rage madly in the streets; they jostle one another in the squares. Their appearance is like torches; they dart like flashes of lightning.
6 He summons his mighty ones; they stumble in their march. They hurry to her wall, and the protective shelter is set in place.
7 The gates of the rivers are opened, and the palace dissolves.
8 It is decreed: she is stripped and carried away, and her maidservants moan like the voice of doves, beating on their breasts.
9 Nineveh has been like a pool of water from her earliest days, yet they are fleeing: Stand! Stand! But no one turns back.
10 Plunder the silver! Plunder the gold! For there is no end to the store, an abundance of every precious thing.
11 Empty, void, and waste! The heart melts, the knees knock together, anguish is in all loins, and the faces of them all have turned pale.
12 Where is the den of the lions, the feeding place of the young lions, where the lion and the lioness walked, and the lion's cub, and no one made them afraid?
13 The lion tore enough for his cubs and strangled prey for his lionesses; he filled his caves with prey and his dens with torn flesh.
14 Behold, I am against you — the declaration of Yahweh of hosts. I will burn her chariots in smoke, and the sword will devour your young lions. I will cut off your prey from the earth, and the voice of your messengers will no longer be heard.

Nahum 3

1 Woe to the bloody city! She is wholly full of lies and plunder; the prey never departs.
2 The sound of the whip, the sound of the rattling of the wheels, galloping horses, and bounding chariots!
3 Charging horsemen, the flashing sword and the glittering spear, a multitude of slain and a mass of corpses, and there is no end to the bodies; they stumble over their bodies.
4 Because of the countless harlotries of the prostitute, lovely in grace, a mistress of sorceries, who sells nations through her harlotries and families through her sorceries.
5 Behold, I am against you — the declaration of Yahweh of hosts. I will lift your skirts over your face, and I will show the nations your nakedness and the kingdoms your shame.
6 I will throw detestable filth on you and make you vile, and I will set you up as a spectacle.
7 All who see you will flee from you and say: Nineveh is laid waste. Who will grieve for her? Where shall I seek comforters for you?
8 Are you better than No-Amon, who was situated among the rivers, who had the waters around her, whose rampart was the sea, and her wall was from the sea?
9 Cush and Egypt were her strength, without limit. Put and Libya were her helpers.
10 Yet she too went into exile; she went into captivity. Her young children also were dashed in pieces at the head of every street, and they cast lots for her honored men, and all her great men were bound in chains.
11 You also will be drunk; you will be hidden. You also will seek a stronghold because of the enemy.
12 All your fortresses are like fig trees with the first-ripe figs: if they are shaken, they fall into the mouth of the eater.
13 Behold, your people within you are women. The gates of your land are set wide open to your enemies; fire has devoured your bars.
14 Draw water for the siege! Strengthen your fortresses! Go into the clay and tread the mortar; take hold of the brick mold!
15 There the fire will devour you; the sword will cut you off; it will devour you like the locust. Make yourself many like the locust; make yourself many like the locust swarm.
16 You have multiplied your merchants more than the stars of the sky. The locust strips off and flies away.
17 Your crowned ones are like the locusts, and your officials are like swarms of locusts, which settle on the walls on a cold day; but when the sun rises they flee away, and their place is not known, where they are.
18 Your shepherds slumber, king of Assyria; your nobles lie down to rest. Your people are scattered on the mountains, and there is no one to gather them.
19 There is no relief for your fracture; your wound is grievous. All who hear the report of you clap their hands over you, for on whom has your evil not passed, continually?

Clear English Bible — Habakkuk (Chapters 1–3): A Clear English Translation

This completes the Masoretic book of Habakkuk in this edition. The remaining books of the Old Testament stand in this edition as a clear-English modernization of the World English Bible (WEB) Classic text named in the front matter, except the books the front matter names as fresh translations made directly from the Hebrew; the New Testament stands on the Greek text named there. The book as printed here stands as DRAFT — NOT PUBLISHED.

Insertion record — 23 November 2026. The Masoretic chapters of Habakkuk (3 chapters, 56 verses) were inserted as a fresh translation made directly from the Masoretic Hebrew under Robert Tilford's Fresh Tanakh commission ruling of 23 November 2026 and its authorization-forward amendment, confirmed the same day, replacing the earlier WEB-based text of those chapters. The Masoretic and English numberings are identical for this book, so the block keeps its bounds exactly — no reseat was needed, and the block header is unchanged. The translation was built in two reviser passes (Masoretic chapters 1–2; chapter 3) from the Masoretic text as it stands in the Westminster Leningrad Codex and Sefaria's Miqra according to the Masorah — the two witnesses consonant-exact in 53 of the book's 56 verses, the three divergences classified in the build record (two ketiv/qere presentation, at 2:2 and 3:14; one spelling only, at 2:5) — with JPS 1917 as the open control of record. Two independent checker passes that did not build the text read the draft against the Hebrew line and both controls: chapter 3 passed with zero errors; chapters 1–2 yielded one error, at 2:7, where the draft had reassigned the awakening from the shakers to the shaken man against the Hebrew — corrected with the checker's exact replacement text and re-verified by count before insertion. The divine name יהוה stands 13 times in the book — no banked benchmark existed, so the count was established from both witnesses before the build; the two witnesses agree at every verse — and prints "Yahweh" at every seat; no standalone יהּ seat stands in Habakkuk. The difference ledger records 51 of the book's 56 verses as differing materially from the seated text or the open control, and 27 open seats stand recorded. The directed seats stand as the commission named them: 1:12 (the received Masoretic לא נמות, "we shall not die", printed as it stands, the tiqqun-sopherim tradition of "you shall not die" recorded in the open seats and not printed); 1:13 (the theodicy question at full force); 2:4 ("the righteous shall live by his faithfulness"); 2:14 ("the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of Yahweh, as the waters cover the sea"); 2:20 ("Yahweh is in his holy temple; let all the earth keep silence before him"); 3:2 ("in wrath remember mercy"); and 3:19 (אדני יהוה printed as it stands, "The Lord Yahweh is my strength", the name the scaffold had lost restored). Habakkuk 1

1 The burden which Habakkuk the prophet saw.
2 How long, Yahweh, will I cry out, and you will not hear? I cry out to you: Violence! and you will not save.
3 Why do you show me iniquity and look on trouble? Destruction and violence are before me; strife is there, and contention rises up.
4 Therefore the law is paralyzed, and justice never goes forth; for the wicked surround the righteous; therefore justice goes forth perverted.
5 Look among the nations and watch, and be utterly amazed; for I am working a work in your days that you will not believe, though it is told.
6 For see, I am raising up the Chaldeans, that bitter and hasty nation, who march through the breadth of the earth to possess dwelling places that are not theirs.
7 They are dreadful and fearsome; their judgment and their dignity proceed from themselves.
8 Their horses are swifter than leopards and fiercer than the evening wolves. Their horsemen gallop onward; their horsemen come from far away; they fly like an eagle hastening to devour.
9 All of them come for violence; their faces are set forward; they gather captives like sand.
10 They scoff at kings, and rulers are a laughingstock to them. They laugh at every stronghold; they heap up earth and take it.
11 Then they sweep by like the wind and go on, and are guilty; their strength is their god.
12 Are you not from everlasting, Yahweh my God, my Holy One? We shall not die. Yahweh, you have appointed him for judgment; you, Rock, have established him for correction.
13 Your eyes are too pure to look on evil, and you cannot look on trouble. Why do you look on the treacherous and keep silent when the wicked swallows up the one who is more righteous than he?
14 You make people like the fish of the sea, like the creeping things that have no ruler over them.
15 He takes up all of them with a hook; he drags them in his net and gathers them in his dragnet; therefore he rejoices and is glad.
16 Therefore he sacrifices to his net and burns incense to his dragnet, because by them his portion is rich and his food is plentiful.
17 Will he keep on emptying his net, and continually slaughter nations without mercy?

Habakkuk 2

1 I will stand at my watchpost and station myself on the rampart; I will look out to see what he will say to me, and what I shall answer concerning my complaint.
2 Yahweh answered me and said: Write the vision and make it plain on tablets, so that the one who reads it may run.
3 For the vision is still for the appointed time; it hastens toward the end and will not lie. If it delays, wait for it, for it will surely come; it will not be late.
4 Behold, his soul is puffed up; it is not upright in him. But the righteous shall live by his faithfulness.
5 Moreover, wine is treacherous; the arrogant man does not rest. He has enlarged his appetite like Sheol, and like death he is never satisfied; he gathers to himself all the nations and collects to himself all the peoples.
6 Will not all of these take up a taunt against him and a mocking riddle against him, and say: Woe to him who increases what is not his — how long? — and loads himself down with pledges!
7 Will not your creditors rise up suddenly, and those who shake you awaken, and you will become plunder for them?
8 Because you have plundered many nations, all the remnant of the peoples will plunder you, because of human blood and the violence done to the land, to the city and to all who dwell in it.
9 Woe to him who gains evil gain for his house, to set his nest on high, to be delivered from the hand of evil.
10 You have devised shame for your house, cutting off many peoples, and you have sinned against your own life.
11 For the stone will cry out from the wall, and the beam from the woodwork will answer it.
12 Woe to him who builds a city with blood and establishes a town by injustice.
13 Behold, is it not from Yahweh of Armies that the peoples labor for the fire, and the nations weary themselves for nothing?
14 For the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of Yahweh, as the waters cover the sea.
15 Woe to him who gives his neighbor drink, adding your poison and making him drunk, so that you may gaze on their nakedness.
16 You are filled with shame instead of glory. Drink, you also, and be exposed; the cup of Yahweh's right hand will turn upon you, and utter disgrace will be upon your glory.
17 For the violence done to Lebanon will cover you, and the destruction of the animals will terrify you, because of human blood and the violence done to the land, to the city and to all who dwell in it.
18 What profit is a carved image, that its maker has carved it, or a cast image, a teacher of lies, that the maker of its form trusts in it, to make mute idols?
19 Woe to him who says to the wood: Awake! and to the silent stone: Arise! Can it teach? Behold, it is overlaid with gold and silver, and there is no breath at all in it.
20 But Yahweh is in his holy temple; let all the earth keep silence before him.

Habakkuk 3

1 A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet, set to Shigionoth.
2 Yahweh, I have heard the report of you, and I am afraid. Yahweh, revive your work in the midst of the years; in the midst of the years make it known; in wrath remember mercy.
3 God comes from Teman, and the Holy One from Mount Paran. Selah. His glory covered the heavens, and the earth is full of his praise.
4 His splendor is like the light; rays shine from his hand, where his power is hidden.
5 Before him goes plague, and fiery bolts go out at his feet.
6 He stood, and shook the earth; he looked, and made the nations tremble. The everlasting mountains were dashed in pieces, the ancient hills bowed down; his goings are everlasting.
7 I saw the tents of Cushan in affliction; the curtains of the land of Midian tremble.
8 Was Yahweh angry with the rivers? Was your anger against the rivers, or your wrath against the sea, that you ride on your horses, on your chariots of salvation?
9 Your bow is laid bare; the rods of the word are sworn. Selah. You split the earth with rivers.
10 The mountains saw you, and trembled; a storm of waters passed over; the deep gave its voice, and lifted its hands on high.
11 The sun and moon stood still in their dwelling; at the light of your arrows as they go, at the gleam of your glittering spear.
12 In indignation you march through the earth; in anger you thresh the nations.
13 You went out for the salvation of your people, for the salvation of your anointed. You crushed the head from the house of the wicked, laying bare the foundation to the neck. Selah.
14 You pierced the head of his warriors with his own rods; they storm to scatter me, their rejoicing like one devouring the poor in secret.
15 You trod the sea with your horses, the foaming of mighty waters.
16 I heard, and my belly trembled; my lips quivered at the sound; rottenness enters into my bones, and I tremble where I stand, as I wait quietly for the day of trouble, when the people come up who invade us.
17 For though the fig tree does not blossom, and there is no fruit on the vines, the produce of the olive fails, and the fields yield no food, the flock is cut off from the fold, and there is no herd in the stalls;
18 Yet I will rejoice in Yahweh; I will exult in the God of my salvation.
19 The Lord Yahweh is my strength, and he makes my feet like the feet of a deer, and makes me walk on my high places. For the music director, on my stringed instruments.
